Des changements significatifs de performance ont également été observés entre les différents moments pour la dextérité manuelle (χ ²(2) = 20,320, p < 0,001), la visée et la réception (χ ²(2) = 25,033, p < 0,001), ainsi que pour l’équilibre (χ ²(2) = 14,966, p < 0,001). La visée et la réception ont affiché la plus forte augmentation médiane entre T0 et T2. Les compétences motrices se sont améliorées au cours du programme de 10 semaines, en particulier entre T1 et T2, l’augmentation médiane la plus importante ayant été observée pour la visée et la réception. Ces résultats préliminaires doivent être interprétés avec prudence compte tenu de la conception en groupe unique et des effets possibles liés à la pratique spécifique à la tâche.

titre: Attention and Word Learning (@WL) study: protocol for a longitudinal study examining early predictors of coordinated visual attention and word learning in preterm and full-term infants.
auteurs: Fu Xiaoxue, Goldschlager Jess, Murphy Harper, Hu Joyce, Yurkovic-Harding Julia, Yu Chen, Bradshaw Jessica
resume: Despite an improved survival rate, preterm birth (PT, <37 weeks of gestation) remains a significant public health concern due to the elevated risks of developing neurocognitive impairments among survivors. Compared with full-term (FT) infants, PT infants show early deficits in visual attention and motor skills as well as language delays. Infant–parent coordinated visual attention (CVA), the coordination of attention to an object with a caregiver, creates critical opportunities for language learning. In FT dyads, CVA emerges from attention-motor coordination, enhances infants’ sustained attention and coincides with parental object naming. Yet, it remains unclear how PT-related differences in attention and motor abilities shape the development of CVA and, in turn, infants’ word learning. To address this gap, the Attention and Word Learning (@WL) study aims to investigate the mechanistic pathway through which PT-related disruptions in basic attention functions and motor abilities impact the moment-to-moment formation of CVA and the associated word learning experience. In this longitudinal study, infant attention and motor abilities are assessed at 12–14 months (T1). Attention subfunctions are measured using three screen-based eye-tracking tasks. Gross and fine motor skills are assessed using a laboratory assessment and a parent-report questionnaire. Six months later, at 18–20 months (T2), mobile eye tracking is used during infant-caregiver free play to examine CVA from a first-person perspective. Dyads play with four novel toys assigned with pseudoword names. Infants’ comprehension of these names is subsequently assessed using an eye-tracking looking-while-listening task. Receptive and expressive vocabulary size are measured by parent reports at T1 and T2. Analyses will test group differences (PT vs FT) in CVA and word learning at T2, and whether birth status moderates the associations between T1 attention and motor abilities and T2 CVA. We will also explore whether CVA mediates associations between early attention and motor abilities and later vocabulary size. Findings will clarify developmental pathways linking PT birth to language acquisition and enhance the ability to identify clinically useful predictors of language difficulties following PT birth. Ethical approval was granted by the University of South Carolina (Pro00136706). Study results will be disseminated through academic conferences and journal publications. Study data will be shared on Databrary.
titre_fr: Étude sur l'attention et l'apprentissage des mots (@WL) : protocole d'une étude longitudinale visant à examiner les facteurs prédictifs précoces de la coordination entre l'attention visuelle et l'apprentissage des mots chez les nourrissons prématurés et nés à terme.
resume_fr: Malgré une amélioration du taux de survie, la prématurité (PT, < 37 semaines de gestation) reste un enjeu majeur de santé publique en raison des risques élevés de troubles neurocognitifs chez les survivants. Par rapport aux nourrissons nés à terme (FT), les nourrissons prématurés présentent des déficits précoces en matière d’attention visuelle et de motricité, ainsi que des retards de langage. L’attention visuelle coordonnée entre le nourrisson et ses parents (CVA), c’est-à-dire la coordination de l’attention portée à un objet avec un adulte de référence, crée des occasions cruciales pour l’apprentissage du langage. Chez les dyades de nourrissons nés à terme, la CVA résulte de la coordination attention-moteur, renforce l’attention soutenue des nourrissons et coïncide avec la désignation des objets par les parents. Cependant, on ignore encore comment les différences liées à la prématurité en matière d’attention et de capacités motrices influencent le développement de la CVA et, par conséquent, l’apprentissage des mots chez les nourrissons. Pour combler cette lacune, l’étude « Attention and Word Learning » (@WL) vise à explorer le mécanisme par lequel les perturbations liées au PT au niveau des fonctions d’attention de base et des capacités motrices influencent la formation instantanée de la CVA et l’expérience d’apprentissage des mots qui y est associée. Dans cette étude longitudinale, l’attention et les capacités motrices des nourrissons sont évaluées entre 12 et 14 mois (T1). Les sous-fonctions de l’attention sont mesurées à l’aide de trois tâches d’oculométrie sur écran. Les capacités motrices globales et fines sont évaluées à l’aide d’une évaluation en laboratoire et d’un questionnaire rempli par les parents. Six mois plus tard, entre 18 et 20 mois (T2), l’oculométrie mobile est utilisée pendant une séance de jeu libre entre le nourrisson et son aidant afin d’examiner la CVA d’un point de vue subjectif. Les dyades jouent avec quatre nouveaux jouets auxquels ont été attribués des noms sous forme de pseudomots. La compréhension de ces noms par les nourrissons est ensuite évaluée à l’aide d’une tâche d’oculométrie consistant à « regarder tout en écoutant ». La taille du vocabulaire réceptif et expressif est mesurée à partir des déclarations des parents aux moments T1 et T2. Les analyses permettront de tester les différences entre les groupes (PT vs FT) en matière de CVA et d’apprentissage des mots à T2, et de déterminer si le statut à la naissance modère les associations entre l’attention et les capacités motrices à T1 et la CVA à T2. Nous examinerons également si la CVA joue un rôle de médiation dans les associations entre l’attention et les capacités motrices précoces et la taille du vocabulaire ultérieure. Les résultats permettront de clarifier les voies de développement reliant la naissance par accouchement par voie basse à l’acquisition du langage et d’améliorer la capacité à identifier des prédicteurs cliniquement utiles des difficultés linguistiques consécutives à une naissance par accouchement par voie basse. L’autorisation éthique a été accordée par l’Université de Caroline du Sud (Pro00136706). Les résultats de l’étude seront diffusés lors de congrès universitaires et dans des publications scientifiques. Les données de l’étude seront partagées sur Databrary.

titre: Schiff-base cross-linked pullulan-chondroitin sulfate hydrogel incorporating raloxifene-poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) micelles for localized therapy of postmenopausal osteoarthritis.
auteurs: Mourya Atul, Singh Hoshiyar, Arya Shristi, Shaikh Arbaaz Sujat, Bojja Bhavana, Devangan Pawan, Bazaz Mohd Rabi, Dandekar Manoj P, Kaki Venkata Rao, Guru Santosh Kumar, Bajaj Priyanka, Madan Jitender
resume: Postmenopausal osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disorder characterized by cartilage erosion and subchondral bone loss, intensified by estrogen deficiency in menopausal women. Raloxifene (RLX), a selective estrogen receptor modulator, shows anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective potential but is associated with limited oral bioavailability (~2%) and systemic side effects. Therefore, in the present investigation, raloxifene-conjugated poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) micelles hybridized self-cross-linking hydrogel (R-PMeOZ@SCH) was engineered for intra-articular therapy. Next, the R-PMeOZ micelles exhibited a narrow particle size distribution with an average hydrodynamic diameter of 147.63 ± 0.66 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.14 ± 0.01, and a ζ-potential of -7.33 ± 1.75 mV. The hydrogel was synthesized via Schiff-base reaction between oxidized pullulan (OxyPul) and chondroitin sulfate-adipic hydrazide (CSADH), enabling controlled release and site-specific delivery. R-PMeOZ@SCH demonstrated suitable rheology, swelling, and controlled release profile for intra-articular administration. In a postmenopausal OA rats treated with R-PMeOZ@SCH demonstrated a progressive improvement in motor coordination, cartilage integrity, subchondral bone architecture and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels compared to disease control. X-ray and μ-CT analyses unveiled improvement in articular space width and reduction in Kellgren-Lawrence score for R-PMeOZ@SCH treated group compared to the disease control. It also reduced mRNA expression of MMP-9, ADAMTS-4, and ADAMTS-5 by 5.89, 2.54, and 7.12-fold, respectively, compared to disease control. Histological evaluation demonstrated a significant reduction in OARSI and modified Mankin's scores and an improvement in relative GAG level in comparison to disease control, highlighting the disease-modifying potential of R-PMeOZ@SCH for clinical translation.
titre_fr: Hydrogel à base de pullulane réticulé et de sulfate de chondroïtine, à structure de type Schiff, incorporant des micelles de raloxifène-poly(2-méthyl-2-oxazoline) pour le traitement localisé de l'arthrose postménopausique.
resume_fr: L'arthrose postménopausique est une affection articulaire dégénérative caractérisée par une érosion du cartilage et une perte osseuse sous-chondrale, aggravées par une carence en œstrogènes chez les femmes ménopausées. Le raloxifène (RLX), un modulateur sélectif des récepteurs œstrogéniques, présente un potentiel anti-inflammatoire et chondroprotecteur, mais il est associé à une biodisponibilité orale limitée (~2 %) et à des effets indésirables systémiques. Par conséquent, dans la présente étude, un hydrogel auto-réticulant hybridé à des micelles de poly(2-méthyl-2-oxazoline) conjuguées au raloxifène (R-PMeOZ@SCH) a été mis au point pour un traitement intra-articulaire. Par la suite, les micelles R-PMeOZ ont présenté une distribution granulométrique étroite, avec un diamètre hydrodynamique moyen de 147,63 ± 0,66 nm, un indice de polydispersité (PDI) de 0,14 ± 0,01 et un potentiel ζ de -7,33 ± 1,75 mV. L’hydrogel a été synthétisé par une réaction de Schiff entre du pullulane oxydé (OxyPul) et du sulfate de chondroïtine-hydrazide adipique (CSADH), permettant une libération contrôlée et une administration ciblée. Le R-PMeOZ@SCH a présenté une rhéologie, un gonflement et un profil de libération contrôlée adaptés à une administration intra-articulaire. Chez des rats postménopausiques atteints d’arthrose et traités par le R-PMeOZ@SCH, on a observé une amélioration progressive de la coordination motrice, de l’intégrité du cartilage et de l’architecture osseuse sous-chondrale, ainsi qu’une réduction des taux de cytokines inflammatoires par rapport au groupe témoin. Les analyses par rayons X et micro-tomographie (μ-CT) ont révélé une amélioration de la largeur de l’espace articulaire et une réduction du score de Kellgren-Lawrence chez le groupe traité par le R-PMeOZ@SCH par rapport au groupe témoin. Il a également réduit l’expression de l’ARNm de la MMP-9, de l’ADAMTS-4 et de l’ADAMTS-5 de 5,89, 2,54 et 7,12 fois, respectivement, par rapport au groupe témoin. L’évaluation histologique a mis en évidence une réduction significative des scores OARSI et de Mankin modifié, ainsi qu’une amélioration du taux relatif de GAG par rapport au groupe témoin, soulignant le potentiel modificateur de la maladie du R-PMeOZ@SCH en vue d’une application clinique.

titre: Resistance to Thyroid Hormone Alpha: Clinical Spectrum, Diagnostic Clues, and Therapeutic Strategies - A Narrative Review.
auteurs: Amer Bushra, Haidarah Albaraa, Alam Ahmad, Kamrul-Hasan A B M
revue: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
resume: Resistance to thyroid hormone alpha (RTHα) is a rare, inherited disorder of thyroid hormone action caused by pathogenic variants in the thyroid hormone receptor alpha gene. Unlike resistance to thyroid hormone beta, RTHα typically presents with near-normal thyroid function tests and a non-elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), contributing to substantial underdiagnosis. The biochemical hallmark is a low or low-normal free thyroxine (FT4) level with a disproportionately high free triiodothyronine (FT3) level, yielding a reduced FT4:FT3 ratio and often a low or low-normal reverse T3. Clinical features reflect the tissue distribution of TRα1 and include growth retardation, delayed skeletal maturation, constipation, normocytic anemia, neurodevelopmental delay, dyspraxia, and macrocephaly. These closely mimic primary hypothyroidism but occur without TSH elevation. Most pathogenic THRA variants are heterozygous and act through a dominant-negative mechanism, whereby mutant receptors interfere with co-expressed wild-type TRα activity. Frameshift and nonsense variants generally produce more severe phenotypes than missense variants, though considerable variability exists even among individuals carrying identical mutations. Levothyroxine remains the only therapeutic intervention reported, with evidence suggesting that earlier treatment initiation is associated with better neurodevelopmental and growth outcomes, while established skeletal abnormalities show limited reversibility. Standard newborn screening programs typically fail to detect RTHα, contributing to diagnostic delay. This narrative review consolidates current knowledge on the genetic basis, molecular pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, differential diagnosis, and treatment outcomes of RTHα. Its aim is to enhance clinician recognition and guide future research, including expanded screening strategies and genotype-informed treatments.
titre_fr: Résistance à l'hormone thyroïdienne alpha : spectre clinique, éléments diagnostiques et stratégies thérapeutiques – Une revue narrative.
resume_fr: La résistance à l'hormone thyroïdienne alpha (RTHα) est une maladie héréditaire rare affectant l'action des hormones thyroïdiennes, causée par des variants pathogènes du gène du récepteur alpha des hormones thyroïdiennes. Contrairement à la résistance à l'hormone thyroïdienne bêta, la RTHα se caractérise généralement par des tests de la fonction thyroïdienne quasi normaux et un taux de thyréostimuline (TSH) non élevé, ce qui contribue à un sous-diagnostic important. La caractéristique biochimique principale est un taux de thyroxine libre (FT4) faible ou dans la limite inférieure de la normale, associé à un taux de triiodothyronine libre (FT3) disproportionnellement élevé, ce qui se traduit par un rapport FT4/FT3 réduit et, souvent, par un taux de T3 inverse faible ou dans la limite inférieure de la normale. Les manifestations cliniques reflètent la distribution tissulaire du TRα1 et comprennent un retard de croissance, un retard de maturation squelettique, une constipation, une anémie normocytaire, un retard neurodéveloppemental, une dyspraxie et une macrocéphalie. Ces manifestations ressemblent étroitement à celles d’un hypothyroïdisme primaire, mais surviennent sans élévation de la TSH. La plupart des variants pathogènes du gène THRA sont hétérozygotes et agissent selon un mécanisme dominant-négatif, dans lequel les récepteurs mutants interfèrent avec l’activité des récepteurs TRα de type sauvage co-exprimés. Les variants de type « frameshift » et « non-sens » produisent généralement des phénotypes plus sévères que les variants de type « missense », bien qu’une variabilité considérable existe même parmi les individus porteurs de mutations identiques. La lévothyroxine reste la seule intervention thérapeutique rapportée, des données suggérant qu’un début de traitement plus précoce est associé à de meilleurs résultats en matière de développement neurologique et de croissance, tandis que les anomalies squelettiques établies ne sont que partiellement réversibles. Les programmes standard de dépistage néonatal ne permettent généralement pas de détecter le RTHα, ce qui contribue à retarder le diagnostic. Cette revue narrative synthétise les connaissances actuelles sur les bases génétiques, la physiopathologie moléculaire, le spectre clinique, le diagnostic différentiel et les résultats thérapeutiques du RTHα. Son objectif est d’améliorer la reconnaissance de cette pathologie par les cliniciens et d’orienter les recherches futures, notamment vers des stratégies de dépistage élargies et des traitements fondés sur le génotype.

titre: Appraisal of Clinical Practice Guideline: physical therapy management of children with developmental coordination disorder.
auteurs: Cameron Kate L
titre_fr: Évaluation d'une recommandation de pratique clinique : prise en charge kinésithérapeutique des enfants atteints d'un trouble de la coordination du développement.

titre: Rosmarinic acid attenuates arsenic-associated neurotoxicity in mice: Behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological evidence.
auteurs: Mehran Parand, Mohtadi Shokooh, Rashidi Nooshabadi Mohammadreza, Azadnasab Reza, Khorsandi Layasadat, Khodayar Mohammad Javad
revue: Journal of trace elements in medicine and biology : organ of the Society for Minerals and Trace Elements (GMS)
resume: Arsenic has a significant role in the pathogenesis of neurological disorders. Rosmarinic acid (RA) is a naturally occurring phenolic compound known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. The present study aims to explore the effects of RA against neurotoxicity caused by sodium arsenite (SA) exposure in mice. Forty-two male mice were randomly assigned to six equal groups: control group, RA group (50 mg/kg, orally for a period of 14 days), SA group (50 ppm via drinking water for 8 weeks), and treatment groups were co-treated with 50 ppm of SA for 8 weeks, along with 10, 25, and 50 mg/kg of RA, respectively during the final 14 days of the study. On the last week of the study, behavioral tests were performed. In addition, at the end of the study, biochemical assessments and histopathological study were conducted. The findings indicated that SA significantly impairs locomotor activity, neuromuscular function, motor coordination, and cognitive performance. SA markedly increased the levels of thiobarbituric acid reactive substances, nitric oxide, and tumor necrosis factor-α and the expression of arsenite methyltransferase (AS3MT) and sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) proteins in the brain cortex and diminished the levels of total thiol, and the enzymatic activities of superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, and catalase. In addition, treatment with SA induced histological damage in the hippocampus. Conversely, treatment with RA improved SA-associated behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological impairments. These findings demonstrate that RA exhibits potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, providing a protective effect against SA-associated neurobehavioral toxicity in mice, which may be mediated by the upregulation of AS3MT and SIRT3 proteins. However, further mechanistic and clinical studies are required to verify and extend these findings.
titre_fr: L'acide rosmarinique atténue la neurotoxicité associée à l'arsenic chez la souris : preuves comportementales, biochimiques et histopathologiques.
resume_fr: L'arsenic joue un rôle important dans la pathogenèse des troubles neurologiques. L'acide rosmarinique (AR) est un composé phénolique naturel connu pour ses activités antioxydantes et anti-inflammatoires. La présente étude vise à explorer les effets de la PR contre la neurotoxicité causée par l'exposition à l'arsénite de sodium (AS) chez la souris. Quarante-deux souris mâles ont été réparties au hasard dans six groupes égaux : groupe témoin, groupe PR (50 mg/kg, par voie orale pendant une période de 14jours), le groupe SA (50 ppm via l'eau potable pendant 8 semaines) et les groupes de traitement ont été co-traités avec 50 ppm de SA pendant 8 semaines, avec 10, 25 et 50 mg/kg de PR, respectivement pendant les 14 derniers jours de l'étude. Au cours de la dernière semaine de l'étude, des tests comportementaux ont été effectués. En outre, à la fin de l'étude, des évaluations biochimiques et une étude histopathologique ont été menées. Les résultats ont indiqué que l'AS altère significativement la fonction locomotrice activité, fonction neuromusculaire, coordination motrice et performance cognitive. La SA a considérablement augmenté les niveaux de substances réactives à l'acide thiobarbiturique, d'oxyde nitrique et de facteur de nécrose tumorale-α et l'expression des protéines arsénite méthyltransférase (AS3MT) et sirtuine 3 (SIRT3) dans le cortex cérébral et a diminué les niveaux de thiol total et les activités enzymatiques de la superoxyde dismutase, de la glutathion peroxydase et de la catalase. In addition, le traitement par SA a induit des lésions histologiques dans l'hippocampe. Inversement, le traitement avec la PR a amélioré les déficiences comportementales, biochimiques et histopathologiques associées à la SA. Ces résultats démontrent que la PR présente des propriétés antioxydantes et anti-inflammatoires potentielles, fournissant un effet protecteur contre la toxicité neurocomportementale associée à la SA chez la souris, qui peut être médiée par la régulation positive des protéines AS3MT et SIRT3. Cependant, fd'autres études mécanistiques et cliniques sont nécessaires pour vérifier et étendre ces résultats.

titre: Beyond Seizure Management in a Developmental Epileptic Encephalopathy: Expanding the SLC6A1 Neurodevelopmental Disorder Phenotype.
auteurs: Varnet Marie E, Dahshi Hamza, Goodspeed Kimberly, McDonnell Pamela Pojomovsky, Stripe Laina Lusk, Armstrong Dallas Michael
resume: SLC6A1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (SLC6A1-NDD) is emerging as a leading genetic cause of epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and NDD caused by monoallelic loss of function variants in SLC6A1 (solute carrier family 6 member 1) which encodes a gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (GAT1). Descriptions of SLC6A1-NDD have centered around epilepsy, but caregivers report other features that drive key aspects of the disease burden. This retrospective chart review and prospective natural history study (NHS) aims to highlight the nonseizure clinical features of SLC6A1-NDD. Medical records of individuals with SLC6A1-NDD from University of Texas Southwestern (UTSW) and from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) were reviewed. Participants had a confirmed or strongly suspected pathogenic variant in SLC6A1. Twenty of these individuals were also enrolled in an NHS at UTSW which included standardized scales and caregiver interviews. Sixty-three individuals were included (40 from UTSW, 23 from CHOP) with 31 males. Developmental delay was present in 97%, developmental regression in 41%, and 58% of those had an atypical regression. Of the total cohort, 60% have ASD. Maladaptive behaviors were present in a majority with aggression occurring in 57% of those. Twenty individuals completed standardized scales as part of the NHS at UTSW. The developmental coordination disorder questionnaire (DCDQ) demonstrated that 90% met criteria for probable developmental coordination disorder. Sleep problems were reported in 56%, but when assessed with the sleep disturbance scale for children (SDSC), all NHS participants scored >39, indicating clinically significant sleep problems. Total SDSC score positively correlated with behavior problems. Daily effects from SLC6A1-NDD cannot be described by epilepsy alone. Combining retrospective and prospective NHS data expands phenotypic and genotypic knowledge. We report the highest association with ASD and unusual developmental regression patterns. Maladaptive behaviors are frequent, commonly aggression. DCDQ and SDSC scores correlated with caregiver concerns but also found higher instances of movement and sleep problems, underrecognized by caregivers and providers. Often, odd movements defy categorization between stereotypies, tics, and epileptic movements. GABA homeostasis disruptions are integral to symptom formation but require better understanding.
titre_fr: Au-delà de la gestion des crises dans une encéphalopathie épileptique développementale : élargir le phénotype du trouble neurodéveloppemental SLC6A1.
resume_fr: Le trouble neurodéveloppemental lié au SLC6A1 (SLC6A1-NDD) est en train de devenir l'une des principales causes génétiques de l'épilepsie, du trouble du spectre autistique (TSA) et du trouble neurodéveloppemental lié au SLC6A1 causé par des variantes de perte de fonction monoalléliques dans le SLC6A1 (famille de porteurs de soluté 6 membres 1) qui code pour un transporteur d'acide gamma-aminobutyrique (GABA) (GAT1). Les descriptions de SLC6A1-NDD se sont concentrées sur l'épilepsie, mais les soignants signalent d'autres caractéristiques qui déterminent les aspects clés de la charge de morbidité.sa revue rétrospective des graphiques et son étude prospective d'histoire naturelle (NHS) visent à mettre en évidence les caractéristiques cliniques sans crise du SLC6A1-NDD. Les dossiers médicaux des personnes atteintes de SLC6A1-NDD de l'Université du Texas Southwestern (UTSW) et de l'Hôpital pour enfants de Philadelphie (CHOP) ont été examinés. Les participants avaient un variant pathogène confirmé ou fortement suspecté dans le SLC6A1. Vingt de ces personnes ont également été inscrites dans un NHS à l'UTSWqui comprenait des échelles standardisées et des entretiens avec les soignants. Soixante-trois personnes ont été incluses (40 de l'UTSW, 23 de CHOP) avec 31 hommes. Le retard de développement était présent dans 97 % des cas, la régression du développement dans 41 % des cas, et 58 % d'entre eux présentaient une régression atypique. Sur l'ensemble de la cohorte, 60 % sont atteints de TSA. Les comportements inadaptés étaient présents dans la majorité des cas, 57 % d'entre eux étant agressifs. Vingt personnes ont rempli des échelles standardisées dans le cadre due NHS à UTSW. Le questionnaire sur le trouble de la coordination du développement (DCDQ) a démontré que 90 % répondaient aux critères du trouble probable de la coordination du développement. Des problèmes de sommeil ont été signalés dans 56 % des cas, mais lorsqu'ils ont été évalués à l'aide de l'échelle des troubles du sommeil chez les enfants (SDSC), tous les participants au NHS ont obtenu un score >39, ce qui indique des problèmes de sommeil cliniquement significatifs. Score SDSC total en corrélation positive avec les problèmes de comportement. Effets quotidiens des cannettes SLC6A1-NDDot être décrit par l'épilepsie seule. La combinaison de données rétrospectives et prospectives du NHS élargit les connaissances phénotypiques et génotypiques. Nous rapportons l'association la plus élevée avec les TSA et des schémas de régression développementale inhabituels. Les comportements inadaptés sont fréquents, généralement agressifs. Les scores DCDQ et SDSC étaient corrélés aux préoccupations des soignants, mais ont également révélé des cas plus élevés de problèmes de mouvement et de sommeil, sous-estimés par les soignants et les prestataires. Souvent, étrangeles mouvements défient la catégorisation entre les stéréotypies, les tics et les mouvements épileptiques. Les perturbations de l'homéostasie GABA font partie intégrante de la formation des symptômes, mais nécessitent une meilleure compréhension.

titre: Understanding participation and quality of life of university students with probable DCD using structural equation modeling.
auteurs: Tal-Saban Miri, Weintraub Naomi, Magen Hagit
resume: Individuals with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) attending higher-education institutions face challenges in their everyday life. Nevertheless, research regarding participation and quality of life (QoL) in this population is limited. To explore determinants of participation and QoL in university students with probable DCD (pDCD) through structural equation modelling (SEM). A cross-sectional comparative and correlational design. A random sample of 297 undergraduate university students was divided into three groups based on cutoff scores of the Adolescents & Adults Coordination Questionnaire: pDCD; n = 40, borderline pDCD (BpDCD) n = 45 and typically developing (TD) n = 212. Measures included self-report questionnaires relating to pDCD, attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms, executive functions (EF), including metacognition and behavioral regulation, as well as participation and QoL. Students with pDCD reported reduced participation and QoL and impairment in EF and ADHD compared to TD students. SEM results showed that pDCD had a direct significant effect on EF, ADHD symptoms and participation and an indirect effect on QoL, mediated most strongly by participation. ADHD and behavioral regulation had a direct effect on QoL, whereas the relationship between metacognition and QoL was mediated by participation. Through a SEM model, this study demonstrated that pDCD in university students is associated with reduced participation and QoL, and emphasized the role of EF, ADHD and participation in explaining QoL. These findings offer important insights for the assessment and intervention of higher-education students with pDCD.
type_etude: Étude observationnelle (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)
titre_fr: Comprendre la participation et la qualité de vie des étudiants universitaires atteints de DCD probable à l'aide de la modélisation des équations structurelles.
resume_fr: Les personnes atteintes de trouble de la coordination du développement (DCD) fréquentant des établissements d'enseignement supérieur font face à des défis dans leur vie quotidienne. Néanmoins, les recherches concernant la participation et la qualité de vie (QdV) dans cette population sont limitées. Explorer les déterminants de la participation et de la QV chez les étudiants universitaires atteints de DCD probable (pDCD) grâce à la modélisation des équations structurelles (SEM). Un plan transversal comparatif et corrélatif. Un plan aléatoirel'échantillon de 297 étudiants universitaires de premier cycle a été divisé en trois groupes en fonction des scores de seuil du questionnaire de coordination pour les adolescents et les adultes : pDCD ; n = 40, pDCD limite (BpDCD) n = 45 et généralement en développement (TD) n = 212. Les mesures comprenaient des questionnaires d'auto-évaluation relatifs au DCDp, aux symptômes du déficit de l'attention et du trouble d'hyperactivité (TDAH), aux fonctions exécutives (FE), y compris la métacognition et la régulation comportementale, ainsi quecomme la participation et la QV. Les élèves atteints de DCDp ont signalé une participation et une qualité de vie réduites et une altération de la FE et du TDAH par rapport aux élèves TD. Les résultats de la SEM ont montré que le pDCD avait un effet significatif direct sur la FE, les symptômes et la participation au TDAH et un effet indirect sur la QdV, médié le plus fortement par la participation. Le TDAH et la régulation comportementale ont eu un effet direct sur la QdV, alors que la relation entre la métacognition et la QdV était médiée par la participationation. À travers un modèle SEM, cette étude a démontré que le pDCD chez les étudiants universitaires est associé à une participation et à une QdV réduites, et a souligné le rôle de la FE, du TDAH et de la participation dans l'explication de la QdV. Ces résultats offrent des informations importantes pour l'évaluation et l'intervention des étudiants de l'enseignement supérieur atteints de DCP.

titre: Perceptual-motor processes in cycling: A scoping review.
auteurs: Vauclin Pierre, Wheat Jon, Seifert Ludovic
resume: Cycling is increasingly recognized as a sustainable and efficient mode of transport, demanding a high level of perceptual-motor coordination for safety and performance. Despite extensive research on biomechanics and physiological capacities in cycling, perceptual-motor dynamics - a critical factor in effective bike control and adaptability - remain underexplored. This scoping review synthesizes experimental evidence on the perceptual-motor skills required for cycling, organizing findings around individual, task, and environmental constraints. Searches were conducted in Web of Science. A total of 4566 articles were screened and 30 articles met the inclusion criteria. Of the 30 articles included, 56 experiments were conducted: 28 involved manipulating the environment, 16 involved manipulating the task and 12 involved manipulating individual constraints. While the current body of literature remains too limited to draw firm conclusions on the effects of specific, isolated constraints on perceptual-motor skills in cycling, it consistently shows that adaptive behaviour emerges from the continuous interplay between individual, task, and environmental constraints. This review points out the lack of research on the coupling between perception and action. Specifically, we argue that the dynamics of perception and action is particularly suited to understand cycling behaviour and how it could better inform educational programmes, bike design and urban infrastructure.
titre_fr: Processus perceptivo-moteurs dans le cyclisme : un examen de la portée.
resume_fr: Le vélo est de plus en plus reconnu comme un mode de transport durable et efficace, exigeant un haut niveau de coordination perceptivo-motrice pour la sécurité et la performance. Malgré des recherches approfondies sur la biomécanique et les capacités physiologiques du cyclisme, la dynamique perceptivo-motrice - un facteur essentiel pour un contrôle et une adaptabilité efficaces du vélo - reste sous-explorée. Cette revue de la portée synthétise les preuves expérimentales sur les compétences perceptivo-motricesrequis pour le cyclisme, en organisant les résultats autour des contraintes individuelles, professionnelles et environnementales. Les recherches ont été menées dans Web of Science. Au total, 4 566 articles ont été examinés et 30 articles répondaient aux critères d'inclusion. Sur les 30 articles inclus, 56 expériences ont été menées : 28 impliquaient la manipulation de l'environnement, 16 impliquaient la manipulation de la tâche et 12 impliquaient la manipulation de contraintes individuelles. Alors que le corpus actuel de la littératurereste trop limité pour tirer des conclusions fermes sur les effets de contraintes spécifiques et isolées sur les compétences perceptivo-motrices en cyclisme, il montre constamment que le comportement adaptatif émerge de l'interaction continue entre les contraintes individuelles, professionnelles et environnementales. Cette revue met en évidence le manque de recherche sur le couplage entre perception et action. Plus précisément, nous soutenons que la dynamique de la perception et de l'action est particulièrement supour comprendre le comportement cycliste et comment il pourrait mieux éclairer les programmes éducatifs, la conception de vélos et les infrastructures urbaines.

titre: Age-group differences in diffusion MRI characteristics of cortico-cerebellar tracts and their association with bimanual performance.
auteurs: Beeckmans Maud, Van Malderen Shanti, Ferreira Sara Magalhães, Hehl Melina, Emsell Louise, Sunaert Stefan, Radwan Ahmed, Cuypers Koen
resume: Aging is associated with alterations in white matter structure and decline in bimanual performance. These parallel changes may be interrelated, as previous studies have linked cerebral white matter properties to both motor and cognitive function. The cerebellum plays a central role in complex motor coordination and higher-order processes, yet age-related differences in cortico-cerebellar pathways remain insufficiently understood. This study therefore examined two major cortico-cerebellar tracts - the dentato-rubro-thalamo-cortical tract (DRTT) and the cortico-ponto-cerebellar tract (CPCT) - to assess age-related differences in white matter properties and their association with bimanual motor performance. Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging data from 46 younger and 46 older healthy adults were analyzed using a state-of-the-art fixel-based analysis approach to derive fiber-specific metrics reflecting micro- and macrostructural axonal properties. An overall reduction in fiber density and cross-section was observed in older adults, primarily driven by macrostructural differences; alongside localized increases in these structural properties in specific regions. No significant associations were found between cortico-cerebellar white matter properties and bimanual motor performance. These findings corroborate the general patterns of age-related white matter decline while underscoring the importance of within-tract analyses. Although cortico-cerebellar pathways demonstrate age-related structural differences, their contribution to age-related alterations in bimanual coordination performance in healthy aging may be limited or obscured by tract-level averaging masking regional effects and the multifactorial nature of bimanual motor coordination, which reflects the interaction of distributed neural and peripheral systems. The observed regional increases of fiber-specific measures in older adults may reflect age-related adaptations. Yet, their functional significance remains uncertain and warrants further investigation.
titre_fr: Différences entre les groupes d'âge dans les caractéristiques IRM de diffusion des voies cortico-cérébelleuses et leur association avec la performance bimanuelle.
resume_fr: Le vieillissement est associé à des altérations de la structure de la substance blanche et à une baisse de la performance bimanuelle. Ces changements parallèles peuvent être interdépendants, car des études antérieures ont lié les propriétés de la substance blanche cérébrale aux fonctions motrices et cognitives. Le cervelet joue un rôle central dans la coordination motrice complexe et les processus d'ordre supérieur, mais les différences liées à l'âge dans les voies cortico-cérébelleuses restent insuffisamment comprises.fore a examiné deux voies cortico-cérébelleuses majeures - la voie dentato-rubro-thalamo-corticale (DRTT) et la voie cortico-ponto-cérébelleuse (CPCT) - pour évaluer les différences liées à l'âge dans les propriétés de la substance blanche et leur association avec la performance motrice bimanuelle. Les données d'imagerie par résonance magnétique par diffusion de 46 adultes en bonne santé plus jeunes et 46 adultes plus âgés ont été analysées à l'aide d'une approche d'analyse basée sur le fixel de pointe pour dériver une métrique spécifique aux fibress reflétant les propriétés axonales micro et macrostructurales. Une réduction globale de la densité et de la section transversale des fibres a été observée chez les personnes âgées, principalement en raison de différences macrostructurales ; parallèlement à des augmentations localisées de ces propriétés structurelles dans des régions spécifiques. Aucune association significative n'a été trouvée entre les propriétés de la substance blanche cortico-cérébelleuse et les performances motrices bimanuelles. Ces résultats corroborent les tendances générales d'undéclin de la matière blanche lié à la géographie tout en soulignant l'importance des analyses intra-trait. Bien que les voies cortico-cérébelleuses démontrent des différences structurelles liées à l'âge, leur contribution aux altérations liées à l'âge des performances de coordination bimanuelle dans le vieillissement en bonne santé peut être limitée ou obscurcie par des effets régionaux de masquage de la moyenne au niveau du tractus et la nature multifactorielle de la coordination motrice bimanuelle, qui reflète l'interaction desystèmes neuronaux et périphériques distribués. Les augmentations régionales observées des mesures spécifiques aux fibres chez les personnes âgées peuvent refléter des adaptations liées à l'âge. Pourtant, leur signification fonctionnelle reste incertaine et mérite une enquête plus approfondie.

titre: Do Caregivers Value a Developmental Coordination Disorder Diagnosis to Inform Their Child's Care? A Cross-Sectional Survey.
auteurs: Thompson Bronwyn, McMillan Lucinda, Mason Rosemary, Johnston Leanne
resume: Explore caregiver-reported value of developmental coordination disorder (DCD) diagnosis in children with multiple developmental concerns. Participants were caregivers of 105 children aged 3-15 years (mean = 5.9, SD = 2.23) awaiting assessment at a tertiary diagnostic child development service who scored "suspect for" DCD on the Little-Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire or DCD Questionnaire (DCDQ'07). Caregivers completed the Parental Perceptions of DCD Diagnosis Survey, developed for this study. Most caregivers (88.6%) reported a DCD diagnosis was moderately or very important. There were no clinically meaningful relationships between caregiver importance and number of developmental concerns (τb=0.194, p = 0.019), level of motor concern (DCDQ'07 τb=-0.002, p = 0.987; Little-DCDQ-CA τb=0.135, p = 0.278) or presence of co-existing diagnoses (r=-0.042, p = 0.671). The three most common factors contributing to caregivers' perceived value of diagnosis were: better understanding of their child, access to school services, and minimizing future impacts. The most common factors caregivers perceived as important for professionals were better understanding of their child, provision of medical or therapy services, and provision of participation support. Caregivers of children with multiple developmental concerns valued a DCD diagnosis. For clinicians, this may inform decisions within the DCD diagnostic process of children with multiple developmental difficulties.
type_etude: Étude observationnelle (détection par mots-clés, à confirmer)
titre_fr: Les soignants apprécient-ils un diagnostic de trouble de la coordination du développement pour éclairer les soins de leur enfant ? Une enquête transversale.
resume_fr: Explorer la valeur déclarée par le soignant du diagnostic de trouble de la coordination du développement (DCD) chez les enfants ayant de multiples problèmes de développement. Les participants étaient des soignants de 105 enfants âgés de 3 à 15 ans (moyenne = 5,9, écart-type = 2,23) en attente d'évaluation dans un service de diagnostic tertiaire du développement de l'enfant qui ont obtenu la note « suspect pour » DCD sur le questionnaire sur les troubles de la coordination peu développementale ou le questionnaire DCD (DCDQ'07). Les soignants ont rempli leEnquête sur les perceptions parentales du diagnostic de DCD, développée pour cette étude. La plupart des soignants (88,6 %) ont déclaré qu'un diagnostic de DCD était modérément ou très important. Il n'y avait pas de relations cliniquement significatives entre l'importance du soignant et le nombre de problèmes de développement (τb =0,194, p = 0,019), le niveau de préoccupation motrice (DCDQ'07 τb=-0,002, p = 0,987 ; Little-DCDQ-CA τb=0,135, p = 0,278) ou présence de diagnostics coexistants (r=-0,042, p = 0,671). Les trois facteurs les plus courants contribuant à la valeur perçue du diagnostic par les soignants étaient : une meilleure compréhension de leur enfant, l'accès aux services scolaires et la minimisation des impacts futurs. Les facteurs les plus courants que les soignants percevaient comme importants pour les professionnels étaient une meilleure compréhension de leur enfant, la fourniture de services médicaux ou thérapeutiques et la fourniture de soins de santé.soutien à l'intégration. Les soignants d'enfants ayant de multiples problèmes de développement ont apprécié un diagnostic de DCD. Pour les cliniciens, cela peut éclairer les décisions dans le processus de diagnostic de DCD des enfants ayant de multiples difficultés de développement.

titre: Maternal High-Fat Diet, During Preimplantation or Gestation/Lactation, Alters Mouse Offspring Metabolic, Molecular and Locomotor Phenotypes.
auteurs: Peral-Sanchez Irene, Sezer Eda, Ojeda Diego A, Calder Philip C, McHugh Patrick C, Morris Rachel, Norman Jeanette L, Ward Jon, Fleming Tom P, Eckert Judith J, Smyth Neil R, Willaime-Morawek Sandrine
resume: Maternal nutrition during offspring development influences the offspring physiology and risk of long-term chronic disease. Here, we investigate the effects of maternal high-fat diet during distinct developmental windows (preimplantation alone, EmbHFD; or throughout gestation and lactation, HFD) on adult offspring metabolic, molecular and motor behavioural outcome. Our mouse model, utilising healthy nonobese MF1 mothers, induced distinct offspring outcomes dependent upon dietary duration with some sex-specific effects. EmbHFD offspring had high serum leptin (females), elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP), low locomotory activity and diminished motor coordination. Similarly, HFD offspring not only had raised serum leptin, high SBP and poor motor coordination but also experienced excess weight gain, deficits in energy metabolism, reduced relative brown adipose tissue (BAT) mass (females) and increased muscle lipid accumulation. Transcriptomic profiling of HFD female offspring revealed upregulation of thermogenic and lipid-handling genes (e.g., Ucp1 and ApoE) in BAT alongside downregulation of mitotic regulators, suggesting impaired regenerative capacity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate, first, the risk to offspring of even transient maternal fatty diet without maternal obesity. Second, they highlight the sensitivity of periconceptional nutrition on the emergence of offspring multisystem metabolism and physiology, supporting the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) concept.
titre_fr: Régime alimentaire maternel riche en graisses, pendant la préimplantation ou la gestation/l'allaitement, modifie les phénotypes métaboliques, moléculaires et locomoteurs de la progéniture de la souris.
resume_fr: La nutrition maternelle pendant le développement de la progéniture influence la physiologie de la progéniture et le risque de maladie chronique à long terme. Ici, nous étudions les effets de l'alimentation riche en graisses de la mère pendant des périodes de développement distinctes (préimplantation seule, EmbHFD ; ou tout au long de la gestation et de l'allaitement, HFD) sur les résultats métaboliques, moléculaires et comportementaux de la progéniture adulte. Notre modèle de souris, utilisant des mères MF1 non obèses en bonne santé, a induit une progéniture distincteles résultats dépendent de la durée du régime alimentaire avec certains effets spécifiques au sexe. La progéniture EmbHFD présentait une leptine sérique élevée (femelles), une pression artérielle systolique élevée (pas), une faible activité locomotrice et une diminution de la coordination motrice. De même, la progéniture HFD avait non seulement augmenté la leptine sérique, une pas élevée et une mauvaise coordination motrice, mais avait également connu un gain de poids excessif, des déficits du métabolisme énergétique, une réduction de la masse relative du tissu adipeux brun (BAT) (femmes)et augmentation de l'accumulation de lipides musculaires. Le profil transcriptomique de la progéniture femelle HFD a révélé une régulation à la hausse des gènes thermogènes et de manipulation des lipides (par exemple, Ucp1 et ApoE) chez les CHAUVES-SOURIS parallèlement à une régulation à la baisse des régulateurs mitotiques, suggérant une altération de la capacité de régénération. Collectivement, ces résultats démontrent, d'abord, le risque pour la progéniture d'un régime gras maternel même transitoire sans obésité maternelle. Deuxièmement, ils mettent en évidence les sensitivité de la nutrition periconceptionnelle sur l'émergence du métabolisme et de la physiologie multisystémiques de la progéniture, soutenant le concept Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD).

titre: Quality by design-assisted development of an intranasal Shikonin-loaded Mucoadhesive microemulsion for enhanced brain delivery: optimization, characterization, and Pharmacodynamic evaluation in a schizophrenia model.
auteurs: Inuganti Pavan Kumar, Gandla Kumaraswamy, Repudi Lalitha, Majeed Shahnaz, Muthukumarasamy Ravindran
resume: The present study aimed to develop and optimize a shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion for intranasal delivery with the objective of improving nasal residence and facilitating central drug delivery. Shikonin is a naturally occurring naphthoquinone derivative with reported anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. A Quality by Design (QbD)-based strategy was employed to establish a robust formulation with defined critical quality attributes and improved nasal delivery characteristics. Solubility screening identified castor oil, Tween 80, and propylene glycol as the most suitable oil, surfactant, and co-surfactant, respectively. Pseudoternary phase diagram studies facilitated the selection of an optimal microemulsion region, and formulation optimization was performed using a Box-Behnken design by evaluating the effects of oil concentration, Smix concentration, and sonication time on critical quality attributes. The optimized formulation consisted of 10% oil, 30% Smix, and 10 min sonication time, producing nanosized droplets with a particle size below 100 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.30, a positive zeta potential of approximately +30 mV, and entrapment efficiency exceeding 85%. Chitosan was incorporated as a mucoadhesive polymer to increase formulation viscosity and interaction with the nasal mucosa, thereby promoting prolonged nasal residence and potentially facilitating drug absorption. The resulting formulation exhibited markedly increased viscosity and mucoadhesive strength, confirming improved nasal retention. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed the formation of uniformly distributed spherical nanodroplets. The optimized shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion exhibited significantly improved in vitro drug release (87.3 ± 1.25% at 8 h) compared with the plain shikonin solution (69.2 ± 1.63%). Ex vivo permeation studies across sheep nasal mucosa demonstrated superior permeation from shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion (91.2 ± 0.41%) relative to the drug solution (73.27 ± 0.14%), accompanied by higher steady-state flux and apparent permeability coefficient values. In ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral model rats, intranasal shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion significantly reduced hyperlocomotion, improved motor coordination, and attenuated cataleptic behavior relative to the disease control group. Orally administered chlorpromazine was included as a pharmacological reference treatment; however, the findings were not interpreted as evidence of route-equivalent or therapeutic equivalence between the two treatments. Histopathological analyses of cortical and hippocampal tissues revealed preservation of neuronal architecture and attenuation of ketamine-associated tissue alterations. Collectively, these findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the potential of the optimized intranasal shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion for central delivery and modulation of schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities. However, the formulation was evaluated at laboratory scale, and pilot-scale/large-scale manufacturing feasibility and scale-up validation remain to be established before further translational development.
titre_fr: Quality by design-assisted development of an intranasal Shikonin-loaded Mucoadhesive microemulsion for enhanced brain delivery : optimization, characterization, and Pharmacodynamic evaluation in a schizophrenia model.
resume_fr: La présente étude visait à développer et à optimiser une microémulsion mucoadhésive chargée de shikonine pour l'administration intranasale dans le but d'améliorer la résidence nasale et de faciliter l'administration centrale de médicaments. titre: Neuroimaging and neurophysiological changes following structured interventions in children with developmental coordination disorder: a scoping review.
auteurs: Domke Molina Francisca, Lopez-Espejo Mauricio
resume: Longitudinal neuroimaging and neurophysiological studies can indicate whether structured interventions in developmental coordination disorder (DCD) are accompanied by neurobiological change, but this literature has not been synthesized across modalities, follow-up intervals, and analytic approaches. To map longitudinal neurobiological outcomes after structured interventions in children and adolescents with DCD or probable DCD and the analytic approaches used, including neurobiological-clinical/functional linkage analyses. We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S. Eligible sources included participants aged 0-18 years with confirmed or probable DCD, a structured intervention, and neurobiological assessment at baseline and ≥1 post-intervention time point. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. We searched six databases, two trial registries, and preprint platforms on January 10, 2026 (updated August 21, 2026), without date or language restrictions. Formal critical appraisal was not undertaken; methodological and reporting features were charted descriptively. Of 747 records identified, 13 sources (eight independent cohorts) published between 2012 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Neurobiological sample sizes ranged from 20 to 88 (median 49). Designs included randomized controlled, non-randomized controlled, and quasi-experimental pre-post studies. Interventions clustered into Cognitive Orientation to daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP; 6 sources), exercise/motor-learning programs (4), and neuromuscular/biomechanical approaches (3). Modalities included diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state functional MRI, structural MRI/voxel-based morphometry, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, electroencephalography/event-related potentials, and surface electromyography. MRI-based longitudinal outcomes were reported exclusively in CO-OP cohorts, with several publications arising from shared registered trials and partial cohort overlap. Six sources included neurobiological follow-up beyond the immediate post-intervention assessment. Analytic approaches varied in pre-post versus group-by-time contrasts, region-of-interest versus whole-brain analyses, and correction for multiple comparisons. Seven sources reported neurobiological-clinical/functional linkage analyses; five tested change-based associations, and statistically significant findings were limited to individualized movement-quality outcomes. The evidence base is small, heterogeneous, and unevenly distributed across intervention categories and modalities. Priorities include independent replication, longitudinal neuroimaging of non-CO-OP interventions where scientifically justified, more consistent follow-up, and prespecified, adequately powered linkage analyses.

titre: Assessment of Vigilance Recovery in Rats Following Anesthesia Using a Touchscreen-Based Continuous Performance Task.
auteurs: Choi Jinyoung, Park Gwi H, Vincent Kathleen F, Solt Ken
resume: Cognitive recovery following general anesthesia is clinically important but incompletely understood. Rodent studies in anesthesia research have primarily examined memory and learning, while vigilance and other neurocognitive domains remain underexplored. To address this gap, we employed the rodent Continuous Performance Task (rCPT), a touchscreen-based translational paradigm, to characterize anesthetic-specific recovery trajectories of vigilance following anesthetic emergence. Sixteen adult Sprague Dawley rats (8 male, 8 female) were trained to proficiency on the rCPT. Once trained, loss of righting was induced by sevoflurane (3% for 20 min), propofol (10 mg/kg i.v. bolus), ketamine (50 mg/kg i.v. over 10 min), or dexmedetomidine (20 µg/kg i.v. bolus), delivered in a randomized order every other week. Animals were placed supine in the cognitive testing chamber and their performance was recorded for four hours. Return of righting reflex (RORR) was used to indicate anesthetic emergence. Vigilance recovery was defined as 20 consecutive trials with an average hit rate >0.6. titre: Coexisting Hearing Impairment in Children Presenting With Speech and Language Delay: A Case Series Highlighting the Importance of Routine Audiological Assessment.
auteurs: Linn Kyaw, May Win Lai, Kyaw Khin Nandar, Win Aye Myat Sandar, Zin Phyu Phyu Khaing, Soe Su Myat, Aung Hnin Wint Wint
resume: Speech and language delay is a common reason for referral to developmental pediatric services. Hearing impairment is an important and potentially manageable cause but may be overlooked because its clinical presentation often overlaps with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and other neurodevelopmental disorders. In Myanmar, where universal newborn hearing screening has not yet been routinely implemented, delayed recognition of hearing impairment remains an important clinical challenge. We describe four children aged 5-7 years who were assessed at the Developmental Paediatrics Service of CLL HEALTH Community Paediatric Clinics, Yangon, Myanmar, after referral for speech delay, behavioral concerns, suspected ASD, attention difficulties, or school readiness assessment. Comprehensive developmental assessment together with formal audiological evaluation identified bilateral moderate sensorineural hearing loss in one child with language disorder, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in a child with developmental coordination disorder and executive dysfunction, bilateral severe-to-profound hearing loss in a child initially suspected of having ADHD, and unilateral mild-to-moderate hearing loss in a child with ASD. None of the children had undergone newborn hearing screening. Hearing impairment either explained the presenting concerns or coexisted with neurodevelopmental disorders, contributing to communication, behavioral, and educational difficulties. This case series highlights the diagnostic challenges of recognizing hearing impairment in children presenting with developmental concerns in Myanmar, particularly in the absence of routine newborn hearing screening. Hearing impairment may mimic neurodevelopmental disorders, coexist with them, or contribute substantially to developmental difficulties. Routine audiological assessment should, therefore, be incorporated into the evaluation of all children presenting with speech and language delay or broader developmental concerns to facilitate timely diagnosis and appropriate multidisciplinary intervention.

titre: Virtual hand rehabilitation training system based on neural network-assisted surface electromyography feature extraction and analysis.
auteurs: Huang Rixi, Yu Guangjie, Ma Zhongxian, Zheng Ying, Zhang Yue, He Bingwei, Chen Xin-Yuan
revue: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
resume: Traditional hand rehabilitation relies heavily on professional therapists, which brings great challenges and limitations to patients with hand dysfunction, making convenient and flexible home rehabilitation difficult to achieve. This study aims to develop an innovative virtual hand rehabilitation system to improve patients' finger motor coordination and provide an effective, convenient home rehabilitation solution. This study adopted a technical development and preliminary verification design. A targeted virtual rehabilitation system was developed and preliminarily validated through patient participation trials. Based on the Unity platform and C# scripting, the system integrates VR technology, sEMG real-time signal monitoring and LSTM neural networks. Three virtual rehabilitation game scenarios were constructed to realize interactive training and accurate gesture recognition. The system achieves over 90% accuracy in recognizing eight complex hand gestures. Ten patients with hand dysfunction participated in the test, and all feedback confirmed improved rehabilitation engagement, safety and convenience. The proposed system has reliable recognition performance and good user experience. It offers a novel and feasible approach for home-based fine motor rehabilitation of hand dysfunction patients with broad application potential.

titre: Effects of in ovo acrylamide injection on bone mineral composition and morphometric, geometric and mechanical parameters of femur and tibia bone of newly hatched chickens.
auteurs: Wojciechowska-Puchałka J, Wieczorek J, Kustra K, Trela M, Muszyński S, Tomaszewska E, Lis M W
resume: Acrylamide (ACR) is a recognized toxic compound that can contaminate food and animal feed and thus pose a risk of transfer to eggs. Due to the fact that this substance has a negative effect on the neural tube. We decided to test the hypothesis that ACR leads to weakening bone strength in long bones of chicken chicks and, consequently, to motor coordination disorders. Therefore, the aim of this study was to determine the effect of administration of ACR in ovo at various doses (0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, and 1 mg/egg) on the mechanical, morphometric and geometric properties of the tibia and femur, as well as indicators of mineralization/bone formation in the body (Ca, P, Ca:P, ALP) among one-day-old chicks. Chicken embryos on day 6 of incubation were divided into 6 equal experimental groups (n = 96 per group), which were injected with the following substances: (1) 0.9% saline solution (0-ACR), (2) ACR at a dose of 0.25 mg/egg (L-ACR), (3) ACR at a dose of 0.5 mg/egg (M-ACR), (4) ACR at a dose of 1 mg/egg (H-ACR), (5) ACR at a dose of 2 mg/egg and (6) ACR at a dose of 4 mg/egg. Hatchability was 74.0, 67.7, 66.7 and 49.5% in groups 0-ACR, L-ACR, M-ACR and H-ACR, respectively, whereas in the groups treated with doses of 2.0 and 4.0 mg ACR per egg, all embryos died. Statistical analysis revealed a varied and dose-dependent effect of ACR on the geometric, osteometric, and mechanical properties and mineral composition of the long bones of one-day-old chicks. The administration of ACR at a dose of 0.5 mg/egg resulted in an increase in the vertical external diameter (VED) (P = 0.025) and radius of gyration (R<sub>g</sub>) (P = 0.034) in the tibia, the vertical internal diameter (VID) (P = 0.014) in the femur, as well as the calcium (Ca) (P = 0.020) and phosphorus (P) (P = 0.041) content in pooled femur and tibia samples relative to the control group. In addition, an increase in ultimate load (F<sub>max</sub>) (P = 0.022) and work to fracture (W<sub>max</sub>) (P = 0.036) was demonstrated, but only in the tibia in the group treated with ACR at a dose of 0.25 mg/egg compared to the group injected with 0.9% saline solution. Furthermore, elevated strains (ε<sub>y</sub> and ε<sub>max</sub>) of the tibia were observed at all applied doses (0.25, 0.5, and 1 mg/egg) (P = 0.002, P = 0.003, P < 0.001 for ε<sub>y</sub>, respectively, and P = 0.009, P = 0.010, P = 0.016 for ε<sub>max</sub>, respectively) and higher ultimate strain (ε<sub>max</sub>) (P = 0.032) of the femur in the M-ACR group. However, the body weight of birds as well as Ca, P, Ca:P, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels in blood remained at similar levels in all experimental groups. In summary, the findings do not indicate generalized weakening of long bones at hatch. Instead, they show endpoint- and bone-specific responses whose biological persistence and mechanism remain to be established. Thus, these studies advance understanding of long bone development and bone mineralization among one-day-old chicks following ACR administration and provide a basis for continuing research beyond the hatching period to determine the likelihood of health effects later in life.

titre: Specific learning disorders and underlying processes: can WISC-IV subtests predict SLD neurocognitive profiles in Italian children aged 7-14 years?
auteurs: Capobianco Micaela, Faccio Miriam, Giammarco Carla, Camplone Dario, Adriani Walter
resume: Specific Learning Disorder (SLD) is studied via WISC IV, as well as via neurocognitive impairment profiles arising from clinical tests. However, state-of-the-art appears to be deficitary about the possibility of shared neurocognitive profiles within a given phenotype. We aim to fulfil this gap by investigating, in SLD, formal correlations between WISC IV subtests and nine impairment domains, with their own degrees of severity. 160 Italian children, aged 7 to 14 years, have been divided in four groups (Males vs. Females; Primary vs. Lower Secondary School); scores obtained in nine specific domains of abilities have been confronted versus WISC IV scales, using Pearson R correlations, and obtaining 15 × 9 matrices for each group. The most relevant correlations have been found in the primary-school group only, and in the female group only. The primary-school children presented a strong correlation of WMI with handwriting and reading. On the other hand, in the female group, mental calculation abilities correlated to several subtest indexes, such as: IQ; VCI; WMI. Reading comprehension abilities also correlated to WMI. A possible explanation to neurocognitive profiles in females is represented by fronto-parietal networks: anomalies in gray-to-white matter ratio, in gray-matter depth, and in white-matter tracts appear to be typical of young females. Results found in the primary-school group underline the developmental role of working memory in learning how to properly read and write. Thus, specific phenotypic areas are implicated in deficitary neurocognitive networks affected in children with SLD.

titre: Janus-Structured Composites for Energy Harvesting, Thermal Management, and Superior Triboelectric Output Performance.
auteurs: Lang Jia-Qi, Lv Zi-Qi, Luo Li-Jun, Zhang Zhen, Ma Ming-Guo
resume: The intensifying global energy crisis and the steady advancement of the dual-carbon strategy have imposed increasingly stringent requirements on zero-energy temperature control technologies and renewable energy utilization systems across domains, such as building energy conservation, flexible electronics, and sensing. Herein, a multifunctional Janus-structured CA/PVDF/MXene (CPM) composite film was fabricated via electrospinning using a blended solution of cellulose acetate (CA) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) as an electrospinning precursor. The composite achieves subambient cooling of approximately 7.0 °C outdoors, demonstrating excellent daytime radiative cooling performance. The CPM-based triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) exhibits outstanding electrical output, with an open-circuit voltage of 101.3 V, a short-circuit current of 3.9 μA, and a transferred charge of 34.9 nC. Moreover, the CPM-TENG shows excellent self-powered sensing capabilities, accurately detecting mechanical signals including human motion and handwriting traces, highlighting promising potential for applications in flexible wearable electronics. The composite possesses mechanical properties (200% enhancement in tensile strength), photothermal conversion capability (achieving a surface temperature of 64.6 °C under 0.8 W/cm2 irradiation), and Joule thermal response (reaching 156.4 °C at 6 V). This study provides a systematic design for multifunctional flexible electronic devices that integrate passive intelligent temperature regulation, mechanical energy harvesting, and high-sensitivity self-powered sensing.

titre: Brittle Star-Inspired Composites With Excellent Tribopositivity, Tensile Properties, and Self-Healing Capability for Self-Powered Flexible Sensors.
auteurs: Ding Guoquan, Yan Zhihui, Fang Ganlin, Jiang Kejin, Li Yuying, Dong Shanshan, Luo Bin, Duan Qingshan, Li Peng, Chen Zhenming, Zhao Hui
resume: Self-powered sensing devices for human-machine interaction suffer from poor mechanical robustness, fragile structural stability, and fluctuating sensing signals under cyclic deformation, severely restricting their long-term operational reliability. Integrating self-healing functionality into triboelectric substrates is an effective approach to address these bottlenecks, but it remains challenging to simultaneously realize superior stretchability, steady electrical output, and efficient self-healing performance in a single material system. Inspired by the arm structure of brittle stars, a waterborne polyurethane (WPU) incorporating dynamic disulfide and hydrogen bonds was fabricated, and the hydrogen-bonding interfacial network between MXene and WPU was tailored. A composite system enabling synergistic multilevel energy dissipation through reversible dynamic bonds and disulfide exchange was therefore constructed. The resulting MXene/WPU (M-WPU) composite film exhibits a tensile strength of 14.7 MPa, an elongation at break of 970%, a triboelectric output of 14 µA, and a self-healing efficiency of 89% after thermal healing at 100°C for 12 h. The flexible sensor assembled from this M-WPU film, integrated with machine learning, enables accurate handwriting recognition and human-machine interaction. Notably, after macroscopic crack self-healing, the M-WPU can still maintain stable electrical signal output, offering novel design insights for the development of long-life, highly reliable self-powered flexible sensors.

titre: Grid to glide: A simple visual cue that alleviates upper-limb freezing.
auteurs: Gál Ota, Srp Martin, Dušek Petr, Hoskovcová Martina, Růžička Evžen
resume: Freezing of the upper limb (FoUL) is a poorly explored manifestation of Parkinson's disease. This report describes a case of a 54-year-old woman with FoUL predominantly affecting handwriting. Writing on grid paper with small squares (0.5 × 0.5 cm) markedly reduced FoUL frequency. A subsequent daily home-based writing and calligraphic training program led to sustained improvements in handwriting legibility, drawing ability, and transfer to writing on blank paper without the grid, without any change in medication. The immediate response to grid paper suggests that simple visual cueing-possibly by promoting block-letter writing and reducing motor planning complexity-could represent a practical strategy for writing-related FoUL, meriting further systematic investigation.

titre: Digital Device Use and Hand-Wrist Disorders: A Scoping Review.
auteurs: Santandrea Sheila, Candido Arianna, Mazza Valeria, Cricco Chiara, Tedeschi Roberto
resume: The widespread use of smartphones and electronic devices has raised concerns about their impact on hand and wrist health. This scoping review synthesised current evidence on musculoskeletal and soft-tissue disorders associated with device use. Thirty-two studies were included, examining smartphones, computers and other digital tools. Smartphones were primarily linked to De Quervain's tenosynovitis and flexor pollicis longus tendinopathy, while computers and visual display units were associated with carpal tunnel syndrome and repetitive strain injuries. Key risk factors included repetitive thumb movements, prolonged static wrist postures and extended daily exposure. Biomechanical studies confirmed increased joint loading and muscle activity during intensive use. Preventive strategies - such as limiting usage time, improving ergonomics, alternating hands and incorporating regular breaks - showed potential benefits, particularly when combined with user education. Most included studies were cross-sectional, limiting causal inference and highlighting the need for longitudinal research.

titre: Exploring feature variability in digitally captured signatures-Part II: Discrimination between genuine and simulated signatures and the effects of collection sessions and writing position.
auteurs: Heckeroth Jonathan, Kerkhoff Axel, Schmidt Paul, Marquis Raymond, Kupferschmid Erich, Weyermann Céline
resume: This study investigated the discrimination between genuine and simulated digitally captured signatures (DCSs) to support their forensic examination. The dataset included genuine questioned signatures from 65 writers, collected across multiple sessions and in three writing positions, together with reference signatures collected in the standard position. In addition, eight simulations were produced by different individuals for each writer and treated as simulated questioned signatures, yielding a total of 520 simulations. Features of genuine and simulated questioned signatures were compared relative to writer-specific reference material. All examined features except the size-related characteristics and the number of pen lifts differed significantly between genuine and simulated signatures. Dynamic features, particularly total duration, achieved strong discrimination with an overall error rate as low as 7%. Combining features reduced the error rate marginally and not significantly (to 6%). Simulations were less often misclassified when reference signatures exhibited lower standardized within-writer variability in duration. This suggests that correspondence between questioned and reference signatures may carry greater evidential value under such conditions. A similar, but non-significant, trend was observed with increasing signature complexity. Exploratory analyses suggested benefits of writer-specific interpretation of signature features. While no clear temporal effect on classification error rates was observed across the collection period, writing position influenced performance, highlighting the importance of considering non-standard writing conditions in forensic practice. Overall, despite substantial variability in genuine signatures, DCS features enabled reliable discrimination between genuine and simulated signatures, with continuous dynamic features providing key discriminatory information and extending the possibilities of forensic examination beyond pen-and-paper signatures.

All examined features except the size-related characteristics and the number of pen lifts differed significantly between genuine and simulated signatures. Dynamic features, particularly total duration, achieved strong discrimination with an overall error rate as low as 7%. Combining features reduced the error rate marginally and not significantly (to 6%). Simulations were less often misclassified when reference signatures exhibited lower standardized within-writer variability in duration. This suggests that correspondence between questioned and reference signatures may carry greater evidential value under such conditions. A similar, but non-significant, trend was observed with increasing signature complexity. Exploratory analyses suggested benefits of writer-specific interpretation of signature features. While no clear temporal effect on classification error rates was observed across the collection period, writing position influenced performance, highlighting the importance of considering non-standard writing conditions in forensic practice. Overall, despite substantial variability in genuine signatures, DCS features enabled reliable discrimination between genuine and simulated signatures, with continuous dynamic features providing key discriminatory information and extending the possibilities of forensic examination beyond pen-and-paper signatures.

titre: The ADHD advantage: Comorbid attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is associated with earlier diagnosis and better academic outcomes in children with specific language disorder.
auteurs: Soongprasit Manas, Tiachunpun Nuthawadee, Jongrakthanakij Nitchawan, Tongpoung Piangjai, Thongpan Masatha
resume: Specific learning disorder (SLD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by difficulties in reading, writing, and mathematics despite normal intelligence. One of the most common comorbidity of SLD is attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, differences between patients with SLD alone and SLD with ADHD remain underinvestigated. This study aims to compare clinical and psychosocial characteristics between these two groups. This retrospective study analyzes pediatric psychiatric patient data from Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) at the Learning Disorder Outpatient Clinic, Ramathibodi Hospital, Thailand from 2017 to 2023. Chi-square tests, t-tests, and mediation analyses were used to examine group differences and causal relationships among significant factors. Among 251 patients, the SLD with ADHD group exhibited less severe delays in reading (p = 0.003), writing (p = 0.001), and math (p = 0.007). This group also visited the clinic earlier (median: grade 3) than the SLD alone group (median: grade 5). Mediation analysis revealed that ADHD had a direct impact on reading and math delays (coefficients: 0.47, 0.38). No significant differences were found in gender, IQ, birth risks, parental education, or family income. Early detection explained the advantage in writing skills but not fully for reading and math, suggesting that other neurocognitive factors may be involved. Therefore, early recognition and referral should be encouraged to promote better academic outcomes.

titre: A Semi-Interpenetrating Network Hydrogel With Synergistic Ionic-Electronic Dual-Conduction for High-Performance Wearable Sensing.
auteurs: Lu Li, Zhang Chunmei, Li Guilong, Chen Guifang, Wang Junjie, Kang Ye, Zhou Jialing, Wang Jian
resume: The growing demand for precise human motion monitoring has spurred the development of versatile flexible wearable sensors. However, the uncomplicated and rapid fabrication of such integrated sensors remains a formidable challenge, as achieving high performance is frequently accompanied by tedious manufacturing procedures and the severe trade-off of isolating single properties. Herein, this study presents a well-rounded hydrogel featuring an integrated dual-conduction mechanism, composed of polyacrylamide (PAM), phytic acid (PA), and poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS), successfully synthesized via a facile one-pot strategy. The hydrogel exhibits an exceptional comprehensive performance equilibrium, delivering a superior combination of extreme stretchability (∼2134%), stable conductivity (5.3 S/m), rapid-response sensitivity (160 ms, a gauge factor of 12 at > 600% strain), and long-term fatigue durability. Practically, the hydrogel sensor can not only precisely monitor the macroscopic motion amplitudes of various human joints but also reliably capture subtle, continuous biomechanical signals, such as user-specific handwriting patterns, Morse code tapping, and wireless wearable human-machine interface. Consequently, this work establishes a highly competitive material paradigm for versatile wearable electronic skins, demonstrating immense potential in both macroscopic motion tracking and high-fidelity micro-signal recognition.
