titre: Baduanjin Exercise Across Clinical Conditions: An Umbrella Review.
titre_fr: Baduanjin Exercise Across Clinical Conditions: An Umbrella Review.
auteurs: Yuan Dongsheng, Xu Bo, Zhao Renkun, Cui Yongsheng, Yang Kexin, Jin Zhefeng, Sun Kai, Wei Jiaming, Zhu Liguo, Qin Xiaokuan, Yin He
resume: Baduanjin (BDJ) is a traditional Chinese mind-body exercise increasingly evaluated in rehabilitation and chronic disease care. The growth of systematic reviews has made the literature difficult to interpret because review volume, methodological quality, certainty of evidence, and overlap of primary trials are rarely considered together. This umbrella review aimed to map the clinical condition spectrum of BDJ research and to appraise the credibility and redundancy of the existing review evidence. Eight English and Chinese databases were searched from inception to April 2026 for systematic reviews and meta-analyses in which BDJ was a standalone or separable intervention. Eligible reviews were mapped by clinical condition. Representative core reviews were selected using prespecified hierarchical criteria. Methodological quality, certainty of evidence, and primary-trial overlap were assessed using A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), grading of recommendations assessment, development and evaluation (GRADE), and corrected covered area (CCA), respectively. A total of 261 reviews were included. Thirty-one core reviews underwent AMSTAR 2 appraisal, 21 condition-outcome pairs underwent GRADE assessment, and 10 review clusters underwent CCA analysis. Review activity was concentrated in cardiovascular/cardiac rehabilitation, musculoskeletal pain, cognitive/neurological rehabilitation, endocrine/metabolic disorders, psychological/sleep/emotional conditions, oncology/postoperative rehabilitation, and respiratory disease. AMSTAR 2 ratings were moderate in one review, low in 18, and critically low in 12. Nineteen condition-outcome pairs were rated low certainty and 2 very low certainty. Several clusters showed high or very high primary-trial overlap. BDJ has been reviewed widely, but the evidence is methodologically uneven, frequently overlapping, and of low or very low certainty. Current findings should be interpreted as uncertain evidence signals rather than practice recommendations.

titre: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) Pharyngeal Total Score in Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
titre_fr: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) Pharyngeal Total Score in Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
auteurs: Zeng Hongji, Wang Chuang, Zhang Chen, Liang Shuguang, Zeng Zishang, Yan Shu, Luo Siyu, Zhao Weijia, Yang Ying, Zeng Xi
resume: The Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) is widely used to quantify swallowing physiology during videofluoroscopic swallowing assessment, but the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for its pharyngeal total score in post-stroke dysphagia remains unclear. This study estimated the MCID for improvement in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score during inpatient rehabilitation. This prospective multicenter observational study included stroke survivors with dysphagia admitted for inpatient rehabilitation 2 weeks to 3 months after stroke onset. Baseline and 10-day follow-up assessments included the MBSImP pharyngeal total score, Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). The FOIS was used as the primary anchor, while the PAS and PGIC were secondary anchors. Anchor-based estimates were calculated using average change, change difference, linear regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Distribution-based estimates and minimal detectable change were used as complementary context for interpreting the anchor-based estimates. Sensitivity analyses were performed using stricter or collapsed anchor definitions, including collapsed FOIS categories, ≥ 2-level FOIS improvement, collapsed PAS categories, and a stricter PGIC threshold. An exploratory interaction analysis additionally examined whether the MBSImP change associated with exactly 1-level versus exactly 2-level FOIS improvement varied according to baseline FOIS level. A total of 161 participants were included. The MBSImP pharyngeal total score decreased from a median of [9.00 (7.00, 11.00)] to [4.00 (2.00, 6.00)]. The mean improvement, used for anchor-based MCID estimation, was 4.27 points. Changes in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score were significantly correlated with the FOIS, PAS, and PGIC (r > 0.3). The pooled average-change and change-difference estimates under the prespecified anchor definitions were 2.977 and 2.004 points, respectively. Under stricter or category-based anchor definitions, average-change estimates increased to 4.633-5.141 points, whereas change-difference estimates remained comparatively stable at 1.731-2.554 points. ROC-derived cutoffs were 2-3 points under the prespecified definitions and 5 points under the stricter definitions. In the exploratory FOIS analysis, there was no evidence that the contrast between exactly 1-level and exactly 2-level improvement varied by baseline FOIS level (P for interaction = 0.776); findings were similar when restricted to baseline FOIS levels 2-5 (P = 0.503). Clinically important change in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score depended on the anchor definition and intended interpretation. Under the prespecified anchor definitions, average-change estimates were approximately 3 points, whereas stricter functional or swallowing-safety improvement definitions showed estimates close to 5 points. In contrast, change-difference estimates were comparatively stable at approximately 2 points across anchor definitions.

titre: Reliability of a Standardized Isokinetic Knee Strength Protocol Across a Slow-Fast Velocity Spectrum in Physically Active Adults with the Biodex System 4 Pro.
titre_fr: Reliability of a Standardized Isokinetic Knee Strength Protocol Across a Slow-Fast Velocity Spectrum in Physically Active Adults with the Biodex System 4 Pro.
auteurs: Augustsson Jesper, Strågegård Jannie, Peterson Elin, Gunhamn Ted
revue: International journal of sports physical therapy
resume: Isokinetic dynamometry is widely used to assess knee muscle strength in both clinical and athletic settings; however, the reliability of measurements across different angular velocities representing distinct regions of the force-velocity spectrum requires further investigation. Purpose: To examine the test-retest reliability of concentric isokinetic knee extension and flexion strength at slow and fast angular velocities using the Biodex System 4. Repeated measures. A total of 15 healthy, physically active adults, women (n=7) and men (n=8), within the age range 21-34 years (inclusion criterion: 18-40 years) participated in the study. Each subject completed two test sessions spaced one week apart. Peak torques of the dominant leg during knee extension and flexion were measured using the Biodex System 4 at angular velocities of 90°/s and 180°/s. Reliability was analyzed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) with 95% confidence intervals and the coefficient of variation (CV). The results showed high to very high reliability across all test conditions (ICC = 0.92-0.99; 95% CI: 0.78-1.00). CV values ranged from 2.7% to 4.2%, and no significant differences in peak torque were observed between test sessions. The isokinetic measurements were reliable at both 90°/s and 180°/s, supporting their use in rehabilitation and strength training evaluations. As distinct strength qualities exist and muscle performance can be assessed across a dynamic velocity spectrum, isokinetic testing at multiple angular velocities may provide a more comprehensive characterization of muscle function than a single-speed assessment alone. 2.

titre: Best Evidence Summary for Integrated Care Management of Dysphagia in Hospitalized Older Adults.
titre_fr: Best Evidence Summary for Integrated Care Management of Dysphagia in Hospitalized Older Adults.
auteurs: Yang Ruobing, Wu Meiqian, Chen Chunying, Li Baiyu, Li Feifei, Huang Shuangling
resume: To evaluate and summarize the best available evidence on integrated care management of dysphagia in hospitalized older adults, providing an evidence-based reference for clinical practice. Evidence was systematically retrieved from Chinese and international databases, clinical practice guideline repositories, and professional association websites. Eligible publications included best practice recommendations, evidence summaries, clinical practice guidelines, expert consensus statements, and systematic reviews published between January 1, 2015, and January 31, 2026. Two trained researchers independently appraised the methodological quality of included literature using standardized quality assessment tools, graded the evidence using the JBI evidence pre-grading system, and synthesized the extracted findings. A total of 28 documents were included, comprising 3 best practice recommendations, 9 evidence summaries, 3 clinical guidelines, 10 expert consensus statements, and 3 systematic reviews. From this synthesis, 43 recommendations were derived across seven key domains: (I) establishment of multidisciplinary teams, (II) dysphagia screening, (III) comprehensive assessment, (IV) integrated care management, (V) rehabilitation interventions, (VI) prevention and management of complications, and (VII) discharge planning and follow-up. This study provides a comprehensive summary of best evidence for integrated care management of dysphagia in hospitalized older adults, offering a robust evidence base to inform standardized clinical pathways and practice guidelines.

titre: Quality of Movement Assessment after ACL Reconstruction in Youth: A Clinical Framework to Guide Rehabilitation and Return-to-Sport Decision-Making.
titre_fr: Quality of Movement Assessment after ACL Reconstruction in Youth: A Clinical Framework to Guide Rehabilitation and Return-to-Sport Decision-Making.
auteurs: Butler Lauren, Martinez Alexa, Sugimoto Dai, Marrone William, Janosky Joseph, Ulman Sophia
revue: International journal of sports physical therapy
resume: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most common knee injuries requiring surgical intervention in youth athletes. After ACL reconstruction surgery, youth athletes undergo prolonged rehabilitation which often concludes with return-to-sport (RTS) testing to determine the athlete's readiness to resume sports participation. Most rehabilitation and RTS literature have focused primarily on quantitative outcomes to guide these decisions. Given the relationship between trunk and lower extremity biomechanics with ACL injury risk, there has been a call to action for the inclusion of qualitative assessments in rehabilitation and return-to-sport assessments. The purpose of this commentary is to describe quality of movement assessment tools that can guide rehabilitation and RTS decision making in pediatric and adolescent patients following ACL reconstruction. Specifically, it provides a framework for the implementation and interpretation of tools to assess single-leg, double-leg, and change of direction tasks as well as practical strategies and considerations for their use with pediatric and adolescent patients after ACL reconstruction. # Level of Evidence 5.

titre: Force Plate Based Assessment of Maximal and Rapid Isometric Shoulder Strength During the Return-to-Sport Process After Pectoralis Major Repair in a World-Class Female Wrestler: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Force Plate Based Assessment of Maximal and Rapid Isometric Shoulder Strength During the Return-to-Sport Process After Pectoralis Major Repair in a World-Class Female Wrestler: A Case Report.
auteurs: Yamazaki Kazuya, Tanaka Ayano, Aoyagi Masashi, Nakajima Kohei, Takeda Hideki, Yamashita Daichi
revue: International journal of sports physical therapy
resume: Pectoralis major tendon rupture in high-level female wrestlers is extremely rare, and evidence regarding rehabilitation and return-to-sport criteria is limited. The purpose of this case report was to provide detailed information regarding quantitative assessment of postoperative recovery, focusing on maximal and rapid isometric force production following pectoralis major tendon repair in a world-class female wrestler. Case report. A world-class female wrestler in her 20s sustained rupture of the sternocostal and abdominal heads of the right pectoralis major at the humeral attachment and underwent tendon repair six days after injury. Resistance training began at week nine and wrestling-specific drills began at week 14. She returned to competitive training at week 18 and official competition at week 24. Shoulder strength was assessed weekly from postoperative week 6 to 16 using the Athletic Shoulder (ASH) Test with a force plate. Net peak force (NPF) and net force at 200 ms (NF200) were measured in the I-position (180°), Y-position (135°), and T-position (90°). NPF limb symmetry improved by week 11 in the I- and Y-positions, while NF200 recovery lagged behind NPF, particularly in the Y-position. A temporary decrease in NPF and NF200 was observed at week 14, most pronounced in the Y-position. Coefficient of variation for NF200 remained higher on the operated side than on the contralateral side. Training progression and return-to-sport clearance were guided by pain response, shoulder range of motion, exercise and sport-specific tolerance, ASH test findings, and physician assessment. NF200 recovery lagged behind NPF, suggesting that rapid force production may remain impaired after peak force has recovered. Recovery patterns were angle-dependent, supporting multidirectional assessment. Strength decline after wrestling-specific training also supports continued neuromuscular monitoring. In this athlete, repeated ASH testing appeared to assist clinical monitoring by detecting position-specific changes in maximal and rapid force production during the return-to-sport process. 5.

titre: Effectiveness of Low-Level and High-level Laser Therapy for Rotator Cuff-Related Shoulder Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Low-Level and High-level Laser Therapy for Rotator Cuff-Related Shoulder Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Dadkhahfar Sahar, Abbasian Maryam, Hasanzadeh Saba, Omidvar Parsa, Moteshakereh Seyed Mohammadmisagh, Zarei Hooshmand, Nikkhoo Mahsa, Abbasian Mohammadreza
revue: Journal of lasers in medical sciences
resume: Introduction: While photobiomodulation and high-power lasers are common for rotator cuff-related shoulder pain, evidence interpretation is hindered by inconsistent dosimetry and clinical findings. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the effects of low-level (LLLT) and high-level laser therapy (HLLT) on pain, range of motion (ROM), and shoulder function. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered review included randomized controlled trials comparing LLLT or HLLT against sham, no treatment, or conventional care. Two reviewers independently conducted screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Continuous outcomes were synthesized using random-effects models, supplemented by subgroup analyses (LLLT vs. HLLT; laser vs. laser plus exercise) and sensitivity analyses to address heterogeneity. Results: Twenty-three trials (wavelengths 805-1064 nm) were included. Pooled analysis showed that laser therapy significantly reduced overall pain (VAS: MD -5.22; 95% CI -7.56 to -2.88; P<0.001 P<0.001 P<0.001), though improvements in pain at rest, during movement, and at night were not statistically significant. After excluding outliers, modest improvements were noted in active internal rotation (MD 1.14; 95% CI 0.19-2.09; P<0.001 P<0.001 P<0.001) and passive external rotation (MD -1.33; 95% CI -1.92 to -0.73; P<0.001 P<0.001 P<0.001). Subgroup analysis indicated that HLLT yielded superior active-abduction outcomes compared to LLLT (P=0.016 P=0.016 P=0.016). Certainty was limited by heterogeneity, small sample sizes, inconsistent dosimetry, and short follow-up. Conclusion: Laser therapy provides modest, reproducible analgesic benefits, and selective ROM improvements, particularly when HLLT is combined with exercise. Given the limited functional gains and reporting inconsistencies, lasers should be used as an adjunct to structured rehabilitation rather than a standalone treatment. Future trials require standardized dosing and longer follow-ups.

titre: Expert assessment of medical and organizational care for children with congenital ear malformations in the Republic of Kazakhstan: The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
titre_fr: Expert assessment of medical and organizational care for children with congenital ear malformations in the Republic of Kazakhstan: The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
auteurs: Imangaliyeva Assel, Kussainova Dina, Alimbek Akzhan, Kazybayev Nurbol, Kamalov Islam, Kyrgauyl Ulpan, Shakaraliyev Adil
resume: Congenital auditory anomalies are serious conditions ranging from mild hearing loss to complete deafness, with associated speech impairment, social limitations, and disability. Our aim was to evaluate the appropriateness of medical and organizational care interventions for children with congenital ear malformations (microtia and aural atresia) in the Republic of Kazakhstan, using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. A nine-member multidisciplinary expert panel (otorhinolaryngologists, audiologists, pediatricians, and otologic surgeons) rated 93 diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation interventions using a structured 9-point appropriateness scale across two rounds of evaluation. Consensus was defined as a numerical IQR (Q3-Q1) ≤2 score points combined with ≥75% of ratings within the same category. Appropriateness categories were defined as: Appropriate (median 7-9), Uncertain (4-6), and Inappropriate (1-3). Of 93 rated interventions, 43 (46%) reached consensus as Appropriate, 45 (48%) were classified as Uncertain, and 5 (5%) as Inappropriate. Highest appropriateness was assigned to multidisciplinary diagnostic consultations (ENT specialist, audiologist, otologic surgeon) and imaging (high-resolution CT of the temporal bones, MRI). For bilateral aural atresia, bone conduction devices were rated as Appropriate (mean 7.55-7.66). Non-intervention approaches received the lowest ratings (mean 1.11-3.00), indicating strong expert consensus against expectant management. Key organizational barriers were included as explicitly rated items in the questionnaire (items 85-93, Section 4-5 of Appendix A). Delayed or absent patient registration and follow-up (item 86, mean 8.00, median 8, Appropriate) and inadequacies in regulatory frameworks (item 87, mean 7.22, median 7, Appropriate†) were among the highest-rated organizational items, while insufficient funding (item 88, mean 6.22, median 6, Uncertain without consensus) did not reach consensus. This first application of the RAND/UCLA method in Kazakhstan to evaluate care for children with congenital ear malformations identified clear areas of expert consensus and uncertainty. The results support the development of multidisciplinary care pathways and targeted rehabilitation policies. Findings represent structured expert opinion from nine specialist panelists in Kazakhstan and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, or national representativeness.
resume_fr: Congenital auditory anomalies are serious conditions ranging from mild hearing loss to complete deafness, with associated speech impairment, social limitations, and disability. Our aim was to evaluate the appropriateness of medical and organizational care interventions for children with congenital ear malformations (microtia and aural atresia) in the Republic of Kazakhstan, using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. A nine-member multidisciplinary expert panel (otorhinolaryngologists, audiologists, pediatricians, and otologic surgeons) rated 93 diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation interventions using a structured 9-point appropriateness scale across two rounds of evaluation. Consensus was defined as a numerical IQR (Q3-Q1) ≤2 score points combined with ≥75% of ratings within the same category. Appropriateness categories were defined as: Appropriate (median 7-9), Uncertain (4-6), and Inappropriate (1-3). Of 93 rated interventions, 43 (46%) reached consensus as Appropriate, 45 (48%) were classified as Uncertain, and 5 (5%) as Inappropriate. Highest appropriateness was assigned to multidisciplinary diagnostic consultations (ENT specialist, audiologist, otologic surgeon) and imaging (high-resolution CT of the temporal bones, MRI). For bilateral aural atresia, bone conduction devices were rated as Appropriate (mean 7.55-7.66). This first application of the RAND/UCLA method in Kazakhstan to evaluate care for children with congenital ear malformations identified clear areas of expert consensus and uncertainty. The results support the development of multidisciplinary care pathways and targeted rehabilitation policies. titre: Mobility in ICU survivors: A concept analysis.
titre_fr: Mobility in ICU survivors: A concept analysis.
auteurs: Yan Yuhang, Peng Sining, Zhu Jiayan, Qiu Jin, Cheng Linghong, Ge Xiaohua
resume: Mobility limitations are common and clinically important among ICU survivors, yet the concept of mobility remains inconsistently defined and is often conflated with physical capacity, functional status, and activities of daily living. This study aimed to clarify the concept of mobility in ICU survivors using Walker and Avant's concept analysis methodology. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Web of Science from database inception to August 15, 2026. Walker and Avant's eight-step framework guided the identification and synthesis of uses, related concepts, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and empirical referents. Thirty-eight studies were included. One defining attribute of mobility was identified: purposeful transition in body position or spatial location. Antecedents comprised predisposing factors, critical illness-related factors, physical prerequisites and limiting conditions, and contextual and modifying factors. Consequences spanned functional and daily-life, psychosocial and participation, and care and service domains. Mobility-focused task measures were the most conceptually aligned empirical referents, whereas measures of muscle strength, exercise capacity, activities of daily living, disability, participation, and quality of life assessed related but distinct constructs. Mobility in ICU survivors is defined as patient-generated or patient-controlled movement that produces a purposeful transition in body position or spatial location following critical illness. Such transitions may be performed independently or with assistance. This definition distinguishes mobility from enabling physical capacities, passive repositioning, contextual influences, and broader functional and social outcomes. This concept analysis may help nurses and rehabilitation professionals distinguish mobility from physical capacity and broader functional outcomes, supporting more consistent mobility assessment, individualized rehabilitation planning, and the development of nursing-sensitive mobility outcomes.

titre: Determinants of prescribers' recommendations of welfare technologies for people with dementia: a scoping review.
titre_fr: Determinants of prescribers' recommendations of welfare technologies for people with dementia: a scoping review.
auteurs: Tsertsidis Antonios, Rapado Irene
resume: Welfare technologies are increasingly promoted to support people with dementia in living independently and safely. While prior research has primarily focused on user acceptance, usability, and effectiveness, less attention has been paid to the role of professionals who assess, select, and recommend these technologies. This scoping review aims to identify and map the determinants that influence prescribers' recommendations of welfare technologies for people with dementia. The review followed an established scoping review framework and adhered to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed, focusing on empirical studies published between 2016 and 2026. Studies were included if they examined professional practices related to recommending or prescribing welfare or assistive technologies for people with dementia. Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria and were analysed using a descriptive thematic approach. Three categories of determinants were identified: professional, organisational and systemic, and technological and contextual. Professional determinants included knowledge, experience, ethical reasoning, and assessments of user and carer capability. Organisational determinants encompassed time constraints, training, procurement systems, and availability of technologies. Technological determinants related to usability, reliability, and suitability for cognitive impairment. Across studies, recommendation emerged as a sociotechnical process shaped by the alignment between these factors. The findings highlight that access to welfare technologies is mediated by professional recommendation practices and shaped by multi-level conditions. The study contributes a fit-based understanding of recommendation, emphasising the need to address professional, organisational, and technological conditions to improve equitable access to appropriate technologies in dementia care.

titre: Association of Admission Serum Homocysteine with Discharge Neurocognitive Dysfunction after Acute Cerebrovascular Disease in a High-Altitude Setting.
titre_fr: Association of Admission Serum Homocysteine with Discharge Neurocognitive Dysfunction after Acute Cerebrovascular Disease in a High-Altitude Setting.
auteurs: Wang Nan, Sun Jialin, Ji Weizhong
resume: Discharge-phase neurocognitive abnormalities may affect rehabilitation participation, self-management, and discharge safety after acute cerebrovascular disease, but early clinically accessible correlates remain incompletely defined. We examined the association between admission serum homocysteine and clinically adjudicated discharge neurocognitive dysfunction in a high-altitude clinical setting. This single-center retrospective cohort included 227 adults admitted for acute ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or transient ischemic attack. The first available serum homocysteine measurement within 24 h of hospital arrival was analyzed continuously and by cohort-derived tertiles. The primary outcome was neurocognitive dysfunction documented within 24-48 h before discharge and adjudicated independently by two reviewers blinded to homocysteine levels; standardized cognitive instruments were not systematically available. Logistic regression was sequentially adjusted for demographic, renal, neurological, neuroimaging, and cerebrovascular phenotype-related factors. Among 227 patients, 98 (43.2%) had discharge neurocognitive dysfunction. Admission homocysteine was higher in patients with dysfunction than in those without dysfunction (18.3 ± 6.2 vs. 12.4 ± 4.7 µmol/L, P < 0.001), and dysfunction prevalence increased from 22.4% in T1 to 38.5% in T2 and 69.9% in T3 (P for trend < 0.001). In the primary fully adjusted model, each 1 µmol/L increase in homocysteine was associated with higher odds of dysfunction (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.07-1.21, P < 0.001), and T3 versus T1 remained associated with the outcome (OR 4.36, 95% CI 2.00-9.51, P < 0.001). Estimates were similar in prespecified sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of delirium or positive confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU) screening and restriction to acute ischemic stroke. Higher admission homocysteine was associated with discharge-phase neurocognitive dysfunction, supporting prospective evaluation of homocysteine as a potential marker of short-term neurocognitive vulnerability rather than a validated predictor of persistent post-stroke cognitive impairment.

titre: Feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a pilot study.
titre_fr: Feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a pilot study.
auteurs: Hishikawa Norikazu, Toyama Shogo, Sawada Koshiro, Ohashi Suzuyo, Mikami Yasuo
resume: Although resistance training with nutritional intervention is recommended for sarcopenia, effective programs are often difficult to implement in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation (TES) using belt electrodes with nutritional management in patients with RA. This pilot study was conducted as a prospective observational study with a single-arm before-after framework and enrolled outpatients with RA in remission or with low disease activity. Participants received an outpatient rehabilitation program as part of routine clinical practice once or twice weekly over 6 months, including TES applied to the lower limbs using belt electrodes (20 min per session; 20 Hz; maximum tolerable intensity) and the daily intake of an L-leucine-enriched protein-containing nutritional supplement. Feasibility and safety were evaluated based on study completion, TES session frequency, verbally confirmed adherence to nutritional supplementation, adverse events documented during the program, and maintenance of disease activity. Lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were assessed as exploratory clinical outcomes at baseline and after 6 months. Of the 14 recruited outpatients with RA, 10 completed both the 6-month program and the final outcome assessment, corresponding to a study completion rate of 71.4%. Participants received a median of 34.5 TES sessions over 6 months. As exploratory clinical outcomes, the median paired changes in lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were 0.08 kg (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.00 to 0.25; P = 0.043), 1.58 kgf (95% CI, -0.35 to 7.25; P = 0.084), and 0.18 m/s (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.24; P = 0.084), respectively. Disease activity remained within the low disease activity to remission range and did not significantly change during the 6-month observation period (P = 0.214). No joint-related or cardiovascular adverse events were documented. This pilot study provides preliminary information on the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining TES using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with RA. These findings may inform the design of future studies.

titre: Rasch-based classification of post-stroke balance ability: dimensionality and clinical validation of the BESTest and S-BESTest.
titre_fr: Rasch-based classification of post-stroke balance ability: dimensionality and clinical validation of the BESTest and S-BESTest.
auteurs: Winairuk Thitimard, Pang Marco Y C, Sirisup Sirod, Saengsirisuwan Vitoon, Klaykaew Kamolwan K, Boonsinsukh Rumpa
resume: The Balance Evaluation Systems Test (BESTest) and its stroke-specific short version (S-BESTest) are widely used to evaluate balance after stroke. However, clinically meaningful classifications of balance ability derived from these instruments remain unavailable. To examine the dimensionality of the BESTest and S-BESTest and establish Rasch-based classifications of balance ability in individuals with stroke. In this cross-sectional study, 335 individuals with stroke from two tertiary care hospitals completed the BESTest and S-BESTest. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed to identify the underlying factor structure of each instrument. Principal component analysis of Rasch residuals (PCAR) and disattenuated correlations between Rasch person measures were subsequently used to evaluate essential unidimensionality. Rasch analysis using the Andrich Rating Scale Model was then conducted to derive balance ability classifications and corresponding raw-score cutoffs. Known-groups validity of the proposed classifications was examined using lower extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FM-LE) scores. EFA identified a three-factor solution for the BESTest and a two-factor solution for the S-BESTest. However, PCAR and disattenuated correlations demonstrated that both instruments functioned as essentially unidimensional measures of balance ability. Rasch analysis showed acceptable-to-excellent reliability and yielded clinically interpretable balance ability classifications with corresponding raw-score cutoff values. The BESTest was classified into six balance impairment levels, ranging from very severe to very mild impairment, whereas the S-BESTest was classified into four levels, ranging from very severe to mild impairment. FM-LE scores differed significantly across all classification levels for both instruments, supporting good known-groups validity. Although exploratory factor analysis identified multiple factors, the BESTest and S-BESTest functioned as essentially unidimensional measures of balance ability in individuals with stroke. The proposed Rasch-based classifications provide clinically interpretable balance ability levels that may facilitate communication, facilitate individualized rehabilitation planning, and support clinical decision-making.

titre: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
titre_fr: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
auteurs: Pappa Nicholas K, Haritos Christopher, Ardavanis Kyle S, Eckel Tobin, Martin Kevin D
resume: Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading<sup>1,2</sup>. High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery<sup>3,4</sup>. Here, we describe a capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery. The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion. Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief immobilization<sup>5,6</sup>. Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury pattern<sup>2,7,8</sup>. This technique is intended for high-grade turf toe injuries with capsuloligamentous disruption, sesamoid complex insufficiency, and MTPJ instability. Nonoperative treatment may be appropriate in cases of low-grade injury; however, persistent pain, instability, or loss of push-off strength following nonoperative treatment would indicate a higher-grade injury. Compared with isolated repair or plantar plate advancement alone, this technique restores both static and dynamic stabilizers of the hallux MTPJ while addressing associated angular deformity. Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of stability and reliable return to sport. Operative treatment of high-grade turf toe injuries has been shown to result in reliable pain relief, restored stability, and high rates of return to sport<sup>8</sup>. Previous studies have suggested improved function and earlier return to play compared with prolonged nonoperative treatment in appropriate patients<sup>6,7</sup>. Knotless suture anchors reduce implant prominence and eliminate knot-related irritation, while the small insertional diameter of the suture anchors preserves bone stock in the metatarsal head and proximal phalanx. This construct provides immediate stability while allowing controlled motion, facilitating rehabilitation, and reducing postoperative stiffness. Athletes typically return to unrestricted activity within 6 to 9 months, aided by the suture tape augmentation allowing earlier movement through the range of motion. This augmentation reduces the need for long-term spica splinting and bracing and reduces the risk of recurrence. The small anchor diameter and use of suture tape allow easy access without hardware burden.○ Suture choice depends on surgeon preference regarding construct stiffness and on the tissue quality and risk of irritation. We believe that suture tape lays flatter and, if required, knots are smaller.Avoid suture twisting or kinking, which can prematurely lock anchors, compromising fixation.○ After the anchor is placed, we keep the suture tape secured out of the field as we prepare the capsule with absorbable suture. As we load the second anchor, we maintain tension on the tape to prevent twisting.Overtightening the MTPJ capsule may lead to altered biomechanics. RICE = rest, ice, compression, elevationMRI = magnetic resonance imagingBID = twice daily.

titre: USMSIT/NMUSIT Fundamental Guide on Diagnostic and Interventional Elbow Ultrasonography.
titre_fr: USMSIT/NMUSIT Fundamental Guide on Diagnostic and Interventional Elbow Ultrasonography.
auteurs: Tsai Yuan-Yuan, Chang Ke-Vin, Wu Wei-Ting, Chi Shao-Yu, Mezian Kamal, Ricci Vincenzo, Boudier-Revéret Mathieu, Özçakar Levent
resume: Elbow pain arises from diverse tendinous, ligamentous, neural, and bursal disorders involving the lateral, medial, anterior, and posterior compartments. Because clinical symptoms frequently overlap - such as epicondylitis, distal biceps tendon injury, cubital tunnel syndrome, and olecranon bursitis - precise imaging is essential for accurate diagnosis and targeted management. Ultrasonography has become a first-line modality for elbow evaluation due to its high-resolution visualization, dynamic capability, and real-time interventional guidance. This article presents the Ultrasound Musculoskeletal Workshop in Taiwan (USMSIT)/Neuromuscular Ultrasound Workshop in Taiwan (NMUSIT) Fundamental Guide on Diagnostic and Interventional Elbow Ultrasonography, a standardized compartment-based protocol developed within the educational framework of the USMSIT and the NMUSIT. The guide systematically describes probe positioning, key anatomical landmarks, and normal sonoanatomy for assessment of the common extensor tendon, anterior joint recess, distal biceps tendon, common flexor tendon, cubital tunnel, and posterior elbow structures. Representative sonographic features of common pathologies - including tendinopathy, partial tear, joint effusion, ulnar neuropathy, and olecranon bursitis - are outlined, with emphasis on Doppler evaluation and dynamic maneuvers. In addition, step-by-step ultrasound-guided interventional techniques are summarized, including tendon injection, joint aspiration, ulnar nerve hydrodissection, and bursal aspiration. By integrating diagnostic and therapeutic principles within a structured framework, this guide provides a practical and reproducible reference for clinicians performing elbow ultrasonography.
resume_fr: Elbow pain arises from diverse tendinous, ligamentous, neural, and bursal disorders involving the lateral, medial, anterior, and posterior compartments. Because clinical symptoms frequently overlap - such as epicondylitis, distal biceps tendon injury, cubital tunnel syndrome, and olecranon bursitis - precise imaging is essential for accurate diagnosis and targeted management. Ultrasonography has become a first-line modality for elbow evaluation due to its high-resolution visualization, dynamic capability, and real-time interventional guidance. This article presents the Ultrasound Musculoskeletal Workshop in Taiwan (USMSIT)/Neuromuscular Ultrasound Workshop in Taiwan (NMUSIT) Fundamental Guide on Diagnostic and Interventional Elbow Ultrasonography, a standardized compartment-based protocol developed within the educational framework of the USMSIT and the NMUSIT. The guide systematically describes probe positioning, key anatomical landmarks, and normal sonoanatomy for assessment of the common extensor tendon, anterior joint recess, distal biceps tendon, common flexor tendon, cubital tunnel, and posterior elbow structures. Representative sonographic features of common pathologies - including tendinopathy, partial tear, joint effusion, ulnar neuropathy, and olecranon bursitis - are outlined, with emphasis on Doppler evaluation and dynamic maneuvers. In addition, step-by-step ultrasound-guided interventional techniques are summarized, including tendon injection, joint aspiration, ulnar nerve hydrodissection, and bursal aspiration. By integrating diagnostic and therapeutic principles within a structured framework, this guide provides a practical and reproducible reference for clinicians performing elbow ultrasonography.

titre: Designing for implementation: development, delivery, and multi-method evaluation of a clinician training program for a novel technology-based concussion assessment tool.
titre_fr: Designing for implementation: development, delivery, and multi-method evaluation of a clinician training program for a novel technology-based concussion assessment tool.
auteurs: Shore Joshua, Provvidenza Christine, Lovell Andrew, Ingaramoorthy Brintha, Christopoulos Elise, Hickling Andrea, Hutchison Michael, Munce Sarah E P, Schneider Kathryn J, Zemek Roger, Gagnon Isabelle, Biddiss Elaine, Scratch Shannon E
resume: Implementation strategies like user training are often excluded from research activities for digital health technologies (DHTs) or reserved for advanced stages of evidence generation. This may contribute to challenges in clinical translation due to usability, feasibility, fidelity, and scalability issues. Using the example of a concussion assessment tool called R2Play, we demonstrate how clinicians can be engaged in developing training resources for DHTs during early stages of evidence generation and illustrate potential benefits of this approach. (1) Develop a clinician training program for R2Play administration; (2) Deliver the R2Play training program to clinician participants across multiple research sites; (3) Evaluate the training program based on participant reactions and learning using a multi-method approach. The Kern Model for Medical Curricula guided training development, which involved a needs assessment, specifying learning objectives, and selecting education strategies. Training was delivered to clinician participants at four sites in two parts: (1) asynchronous online learning modules (1 h); and (2) live training session to practice R2Play administration tasks (1 h). Evaluation measures based on the Kirkpatrick Model for Training Evaluation included module-embedded knowledge check questions, live training task completion scores, post-training survey, and follow-up interview. Quantitative measures were analyzed descriptively (frequencies, proportions, means), and content analysis was applied to interview data. Eighteen clinicians participated (n = 15 women), primarily physiotherapists (n = 11) and athletic therapists (n = 3). Survey and interview feedback generally indicated positive reactions (satisfaction, relevance, engagement) and learning perceptions (knowledge, skills, confidence). Participants objectively and subjectively experienced most difficulty in learning system set-up, delivering precise assessment level instructions, and explaining assessment scoring metrics. Interview data highlighted topics requiring additional content (navigating software interface, interpreting results, troubleshooting). Suggested improvements included an end-to-end workflow demonstration, mock run-through, and opportunities to observe experienced users. Training programs for DHTs should consider addressing technical proficiency (i.e., system set-up and operation), clinical reasoning (i.e., interpreting data), and communication with care recipients. Early multicenter studies involving end-user training can help enhance the usability of DHTs and identify additional strategies to foster implementation. This work adds to limited empirical literature on how to prepare clinicians for using DHTs through evidence-based practical recommendations.

titre: Seven-day Accelerometer-derived Wrist Activity after Acute Stroke Stratified by Hemiparesis Severity: A Prospective Observational Pilot Study.
titre_fr: Seven-day Accelerometer-derived Wrist Activity after Acute Stroke Stratified by Hemiparesis Severity: A Prospective Observational Pilot Study.
auteurs: Kouda Tsuyoshi, Koizumi Kohei, Mizumura Kakeru, Takahashi Hidetoshi, Hamaguchi Toyohiro
resume: This hypothesis-driven prospective pilot study characterized 7-day trajectories of bilateral wrist activity after acute stroke by baseline Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) severity. We hypothesized that mild impairment would be associated with greater paretic-side activity and more symmetric activity, whereas bilateral balance would change little despite clinical improvement. Patients who began rehabilitation within 3 days after stroke wore bilateral wrist accelerometers for 7 days. Exploratory strata were mild (FMA-UE >45) and severe (≤45), based on an inflection point of 45.3 reported for subacute stroke. Daily vector magnitude (VM) and magnitude ratio [MR = log<sub>10</sub>(paretic VM/non-paretic VM)] were analyzed using sex-adjusted linear mixed-effects models with participant random intercepts. Unannotated walking, care, therapy, and sleep were included; indices therefore represented overall inpatient wrist acceleration. Of 32 enrolled patients, 24 completed monitoring (mild impairment, n = 16; severe impairment, n = 8). At day 1, the severe group had lower paretic VM [β = -468,257 counts/day; 95% confidence interval (CI) -826,564 to -109,949; P = 0.010] and MR (β = -0.348; 95% CI -0.515 to -0.181; P <0.001) than the mild group. In the mild reference group, day coefficients were positive for non-paretic VM (β = 46,589; P <0.001) and paretic VM (β = 34,801; P = 0.002). Group-by-day interactions were nonsignificant, and MR showed no significant day effect. FMA-UE and Action Research Arm Test scores increased in both groups. Wrist activity and bilateral balance differed by baseline severity. MR showed no significant temporal change despite improved clinical motor scores. Bilateral wrist accelerometry may complement clinical assessment but reflects overall wrist acceleration rather than purposeful upper-limb use.

titre: Influencing factors and network analysis of latent profiles of care demands among disabled older adults in integrated medical and nursing care institutions in Shanghai, China: a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Influencing factors and network analysis of latent profiles of care demands among disabled older adults in integrated medical and nursing care institutions in Shanghai, China: a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Ao Xu, Haijing Sun, Hongmei Sun, Lihua Wei, Yanmei Wang
resume: To identify the latent profiles and network structure of care demands among disabled older adults in integrated medical and nursing care institutions, and to provide empirical evidence for service provision. Convenience sampling was used to select 443 disabled older adults from 16 integrated medical and nursing care institutions in Pudong New Area, Shanghai. Face-to-face surveys were conducted using a general information questionnaire and a service demands questionnaire. Latent profile analysis was employed to identify care demand profiles and their influencing factors, while network analysis was applied to construct the demand network and compare network differences across profiles. Latent profile analysis identified three care demand profiles: the "Low-demand expression group" (76.4%), the "Multidimensional high-demand group" (18.5%), and the "Psychological-prominent demand group" (5.1%). Age, gender, pre-retirement occupation, and frequency of children's visits were independent influencing factors for profile membership (P<0.05). The overall network analysis revealed that chronic disease management health education and safety prevention health education served as bridge demands. In both the overall and subgroup network analyses, excretion care and rehabilitation assessment were core demands. Subgroup comparison showed that the strongest edge in the "Low-demand expression group" crossed dimensions, whereas the strongest edge in the "Multidimensional high-demand group" was concentrated within dimensions. The care demands of disabled older adults in integrated medical and nursing care institutions are typologically differentiated and shaped by multiple factors. The association structures among care demands differ fundamentally across demand types. Therefore, institutions should consider both the demand classification and network structures when allocating care resources, rather than determining service priorities based solely on the average scores of individual demand items.

titre: Effects of virtual reality and gamified digital rehabilitation on functional recovery in individuals with Spinal Cord Injury: a systematic review and Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of virtual reality and gamified digital rehabilitation on functional recovery in individuals with Spinal Cord Injury: a systematic review and Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis.
auteurs: Xie Mengnan, Jiao Mingyue, Duan Zelong, Li Jian, Zhu Yueying, Zhang Binbin, Wen Fangfang, Long Jifeng
resume: Virtual reality (VR) and gamified digital rehabilitation can increase task-specific practice and feedback for individuals with Spinal Cord Injury (SCI); however, their incremental effects on functional recovery remain uncertain. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through July 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating VR or gamified digital rehabilitation in adults with SCI. Comparator conditions were classified as active rehabilitation, sham or attention control, or minimal/no intervention. The primary outcome was the Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM). Hedges' g estimates were synthesized using a Bayesian three-level random-effects model that accounted for within-study dependence. We estimated the 95% credible interval (CrI), 95% prediction interval (PI), and posterior probabilities of any benefit (g > 0) and of meeting a distribution-based threshold for clinical importance (g ≥ 0.40). A post hoc sensitivity analysis restricted the SCIM synthesis to trials with active-rehabilitation comparators. Seven secondary outcomes were synthesized separately. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool (RoB 2) and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Thirteen RCTs involving 295 participants were included; comparator conditions were active rehabilitation in ten trials, sham or attention control in two, and no intervention in one. Seven studies contributed 25 eligible SCIM effect estimates. The pooled posterior mean effect favored digital rehabilitation but was small and imprecisely estimated (Hedges' g = 0.24; 95% CrI, -0.12 to 0.61; 95% PI, -1.17 to 1.58). The posterior probabilities of any benefit and of a clinically important effect were 91.8 and 17.4%, respectively. Restricting the synthesis to the six SCIM studies with active-rehabilitation comparators yielded a similar, imprecise estimate (g = 0.28; 95% CrI, -0.20 to 0.75). Posterior mean effects for all seven secondary outcomes favored digital rehabilitation, although each 95% CrI included the null value. Direct posterior comparisons provided no clear evidence of effect modification by intervention category, injury completeness, or intervention duration. The weekly-dose association was uncertain and did not improve predictive performance. Overall risk of bias was rated as some concerns, and certainty was very low for all outcomes. VR and gamified digital rehabilitation may provide small functional benefits relative to the comparator conditions used in the included trials; however, clinically important and reproducible improvements have not been demonstrated. Current evidence is insufficient to prioritize specific technology types, patient subgroups, intervention durations, or weekly training doses. CRD420261458807; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261458807.

titre: Individualized multimodal pain management for chronic perineal pain: A case report.
titre_fr: Individualized multimodal pain management for chronic perineal pain: A case report.
auteurs: Ren Xuemeng, Cong Lixin
resume: Persistent perineal pain is a challenging clinical condition that may substantially impair sleep, urination, daily activities, and psychological well-being. Accurate assessment and individualized multimodal management are essential for improving symptom control and patient participation in care. A 68-year-old woman presented with chronic perineal pain and tenderness that had persisted for 3 years. The pain significantly interfered with her sleep, urination, and daily activities. Clinical assessment suggested chronic perineal pain with neuropathic involvement of the pudendal nerve and lumbosacral or sacral nerve roots. The diagnosis was established based on the patient's clinical manifestations, physical examination findings, and comprehensive evaluation. The patient received a multimodal pain management approach, including oral pregabalin, computed tomography-guided sacral canal catheterization with targeted nerve-root adhesiolysis and ozone injection, continuous pain assessment, psychological support, pelvic floor muscle training, and individualized rehabilitation guidance. At the two-week follow-up, the visual analog scale score decreased from 8/10 to 3/10, and the pain no longer interfered with sleep. Approximately 3 weeks after discharge, the pain temporarily increased to 5/10 and subsequently stabilized at 4/10 at the one-month follow-up while the patient continued oral pregabalin. Individualized multimodal pain management may effectively reduce pain intensity and improve sleep and daily functioning in patients with persistent perineal pain. Continuous assessment, patient participation, psychological support, and rehabilitation strategies are important components of comprehensive pain management.

titre: Clinical and Videostroboscopic Characteristics of Vocal Fold Nodules in Conservatory Students in Georgia: A Case Series.
titre_fr: Clinical and Videostroboscopic Characteristics of Vocal Fold Nodules in Conservatory Students in Georgia: A Case Series.
auteurs: Shengelia Lela, Katsarava Irina, Pavliashvili Natalia, Kekelidze Irina, Gamkrelidze Natia
revue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
resume: Voice disorders are common among professional voice users, particularly singers and vocal students exposed to high vocal demands. Vocal fold nodules are among the most frequent benign vocal fold lesions associated with phonotrauma. However, data on the clinical and functional characteristics of vocal fold nodules among conservatory students, particularly in Georgia, remain limited. This descriptive case series included 10 conservatory vocal students and recent graduates presenting with dysphonia at a specialized otolaryngology clinic in Tbilisi, Georgia. Clinical data were collected retrospectively and included demographic characteristics, vocal background, presenting symptoms, clinical findings, and management. All patients underwent videostroboscopic examination to assess vocal fold structure and function, together with acoustic voice assessment. Participants ranged in age from 17 to 28 years, and 60% were female. Dysphonia was present in all cases (100%), with high-register dysphonia reported in four patients (40%). Videostroboscopic examination demonstrated bilateral, symmetrical nodular lesions located at the junction of the anterior and middle thirds of the vocal folds, with incomplete glottic closure and reduced mucosal wave observed in several cases. Abnormal acoustic parameters were identified in eight patients (80%). Symptoms suggestive of reflux-related laryngeal irritation were reported in four patients (40%), and reflux laryngitis was diagnosed in two patients (20%). All patients underwent phonomicrosurgery because of persistent symptoms despite conservative management and their professional vocal requirements, followed by structured postoperative voice rehabilitation and voice therapy. Four patients (40%) additionally received inhaled corticosteroid therapy. Clinical improvement in dysphonia was observed following surgery. Vocal fold nodules contribute to dysphonia among conservatory vocal students and recent graduates presenting with voice-related complaints. The combined use of videostroboscopy and acoustic voice assessment provides complementary information on vocal fold structure and vocal function. In this case series, phonomicrosurgery followed by structured postoperative voice rehabilitation was associated with clinical improvement in dysphonia among patients with persistent symptoms and substantial professional vocal demands. Larger prospective studies using standardized pre- and post-treatment voice outcome measures are needed to further evaluate treatment outcomes in this population.

titre: Beyond the Rankin Scale: A Patient-Centered Score for Meaningful Recovery After Mechanical Thrombectomy in Older Adults With Pre-Stroke Disability.
titre_fr: Beyond the Rankin Scale: A Patient-Centered Score for Meaningful Recovery After Mechanical Thrombectomy in Older Adults With Pre-Stroke Disability.
auteurs: Inoue Hiroyasu, Oomura Masahiro, Nakamura Yoshitaka, Nishikawa Yusuke, Uchida Yuto, Kusui Shoya, Taishaku Atsuhito, Nozaki Yoshiro, Yamanaka Tomoyasu, Shibata Teishiki, Inoue Yasuhide, Taniguchi Yoko, Madokoro Yuta, Sato Toyohiro, Fujioka Teppei, Mizuno Masayuki, Kawashima Shoji, Mase Mitsuhito, Matsukawa Noriyuki
resume: The benefit of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischemic stroke in patients with pre-stroke moderate-to-severe disability is difficult to evaluate using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) alone. We developed and evaluated the SMILE-Stroke score as a patient-centered outcome measure. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 31 patients with pre-stroke mRS scores of 3-5 who underwent MT. The 10-point SMILE-Stroke score, comprising Speech, Mobility, Ingestion, Lavatory, and Engagement domains, was assessed at discharge; a score ≥ 4 was prespecified as favorable. Interrater reliability, convergent validity with the Barthel Index, associations with discharge disposition and mRS, and pre-stroke SMILE-Stroke scores were evaluated. Twelve patients (38.7%) achieved a favorable SMILE-Stroke outcome. Interrater reliability was excellent for the total score (single-rater intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.957) and dichotomized outcome (Fleiss' κ = 0.863). The score correlated strongly with the discharge Barthel Index (Spearman's ρ = 0.86, p < 0.001) and showed a graded association with discharge disposition (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0012). For distinguishing discharge to home/original residence or rehabilitation hospital from long-term care hospital or death, the SMILE-Stroke score yielded an AUC of 0.82. Notably, 6 of 19 patients (31.6%) with 90-day mRS scores of 4-5 achieved a favorable SMILE-Stroke outcome. The SMILE-Stroke score was feasible, reproducible, and associated with established functional and discharge outcomes in selected MT-treated patients with pre-stroke disability. It may complement the mRS by identifying preserved or regained patient-centered functional domains within poor mRS categories.

titre: Reliability and quality of YouTube exercise videos for people living with lung cancer: a cross-sectional content analysis.
titre_fr: Reliability and quality of YouTube exercise videos for people living with lung cancer: a cross-sectional content analysis.
auteurs: Ergan Mesut, Keskin Tahir, Ünüvar Bayram Sönmez, Başkurt Zeliha
revue: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
resume: To evaluate the characteristics, reliability, and quality of YouTube exercise videos designed for people with lung cancer. Video characteristics (e.g., likes, views, video length, and upload source) were recorded. Information reliability was assessed using the mDISCERN scale, and overall quality was evaluated using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the JAMA benchmark criteria. Exercise-specific quality was additionally rated on a Likert scale focusing on exercise safety, progression/adaptability, and demonstration/instructions. Two physiotherapists independently analyzed the videos. Of 2,158 videos screened, 24 met the final eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. According to the GQS, 54.2% (n = 13) of the videos were classified as high quality and 20.8% (n = 5) as low quality. titre: Concurrent Validity and Agreement of Viewpoint-Dependent Markerless Motion Tracking in Upper-Limb Assessment: A Validation Against Optoelectronic Motion Capture.
titre_fr: Concurrent Validity and Agreement of Viewpoint-Dependent Markerless Motion Tracking in Upper-Limb Assessment: A Validation Against Optoelectronic Motion Capture.
auteurs: Shrestha Suman, Honda Yuichiro, Toda Haruki, Chin Takaaki, Irie Mitsuru
resume: Quantitative upper-limb assessment in rehabilitation traditionally relies on expensive optoelectronic reference tracking. While single-camera markerless systems offer an accessible alternative, their viewpoint-dependent accuracy and depth ambiguity remain critical concerns. This study systematically validates an integrated MediaPipe tracking pipeline (Pose and Hands) against an 8-camera optoelectronic system. Ten healthy males performed four clinical upper-limb tasks, recorded simultaneously across three spatial camera viewpoints (frontal, oblique elevated, and oblique side). To isolate spatial accuracy, validations utilized direct unmodeled geometric tracking vectors rather than clinical joint models. Results demonstrate that agreement and accuracy are systematically dependent on movement geometry and camera perspective. Planar tasks like shoulder abduction exhibited moderate to good peak range-of-motion agreement (ICC = 0.63 - 0.82) and precision (RMSE = 9.00∘ - 11.23∘). For transverse plane movements like shoulder rotation, an oblique elevated perspective improved peak range-of-motion agreement (ICC = 0.68). Out-of-plane tracking and fine distal rotations (forearm pronation) exhibited poor agreement (ICC ≤ 0.34) and substantial trajectory instability (RMSE > 30∘). Ultimately, while single-camera monocular RGB tracking provides sufficient validity for gross range-of-motion screening during planar upper-limb tasks, quantitative assessment of multi-planar and distal rotational kinematics requires multi-view camera fusion, depth sensing, or specialized 2D shape-regression architectures.

titre: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Validation of the Arabic Chronic Venous Insufficiency Quality-of-Life Questionnaire (CIVIQ-20) in Saudi Arabia.
titre_fr: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Validation of the Arabic Chronic Venous Insufficiency Quality-of-Life Questionnaire (CIVIQ-20) in Saudi Arabia.
auteurs: Alabdullateef May S, Gwada Rehab F M, Omar Mohammed T A
resume: Background/Objectives: Chronic venous disease significantly impairs health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Although the Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire (CIVIQ-20) is widely used internationally, a validated Arabic version is lacking. The objectives of this study were to translate and culturally adapt the CIVIQ-20 into Arabic and to examine its reliability, construct, and discriminative validity in Arab patients with chronic venous disease. Methods: Following standardized guidelines, the CIVIQ-20 was translated and cross-culturally adapted. For psychometric evaluation, 139 participants with chronic venous disease were selected. They completed the Arabic version of Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire-20 (CIVIQ-20-Ar) and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). Psychometric evaluation included internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) and test-retest reliability using the two-way random intraclass correlation coefficient ICC (2,1). Minimal detectable change (MDC95) was assessed, along with both convergent validity (using the SF-36 as a comparator) and known-group validity (across CEAP severity stages), using seven predefined hypotheses. Results: The CIVIQ-20-Ar questionnaire had adequate internal consistency and very strong test-retest reliability. As hypothesized, the CIVIQ-20-Ar subscales and global index demonstrated a moderate-to-strong correlation with the SF-36 summary and domain scores (r = -0.42 to -0.79, p < 0.001), with the strongest correlation in the pain subscale (r = -0.79, p < 0.001). Known-group validity was established by significant score discrimination across advancing Clinical-Etiology-Anatomy-Pathophysiology (CEAP) severity stages (p < 0.01). Conclusions: The CIVIQ-20-Ar Questionnaire has adequate psychometric properties. Therefore, vascular surgeons, phlebologists, and rehabilitation specialists can use the CIVIQ-20-Ar in routine clinical practice and research to evaluate health-related quality of life in the Arabic-speaking population with chronic venous disease.

titre: Overcoming Subacromial Impingement, as a Term and Concept: Rationale and Proposals.
titre_fr: Overcoming Subacromial Impingement, as a Term and Concept: Rationale and Proposals.
auteurs: Sonnati Federico, Visonà Enrico, Merolla Giovanni
resume: Background/Objectives: Subacromial impingement syndrome has traditionally been described as pathological contact between the rotator cuff and the anterolateral aspect of the acromion and has long been regarded as a primary cause of shoulder pain and tendon injury. Despite a substantial body of literature questioning the very existence of subacromial impingement as a pathological entity, the diagnosis continues to be widely used in medical and rehabilitation settings as a predominantly biomechanical explanation for shoulder pain. The objective of this review is to determine whether the concept of subacromial impingement should be abandoned in clinical practice, interprofessional communication, and the clinician-patient relationship, and to explore which alternatives may be more appropriate. Methods: This narrative review is based on an appraisal of the most relevant literature on this topic published in recent years using scientific databases. Results: Evidence suggests that narrowing of the subacromial space is a consequence of rotator cuff muscle-tendon unit incompetence rather than its cause. Furthermore, such dysfunction appears to arise primarily from degenerative rather than compressive mechanisms. Advances in shoulder biokinematics have also challenged the validity of the clinical 'special tests' traditionally used to support the diagnosis, as these tests do not appear to accurately identify the presumed target structures. Moreover, surgical decompression of the subacromial space has not proved to be more effective than conservative treatment when performed as a standalone procedure, and it often provides no additional benefit when combined with rotator cuff repair in terms of reducing re-tear rates. Nevertheless, it may still have a role as an adjunctive procedure to improve exposure of the surgical site or in selected cases. Discussion: An inaccurate biomechanical explanation may lead patients to believe that arm elevation is inherently harmful, thereby resulting in disability and increased pain. It may also encourage the selection of invasive treatments over conservative management, despite current international guidelines recommending conservative treatment as the first-line approach for subacromial shoulder pain. Indeed, such an approach has been shown to be effective in a substantial proportion of patients, with lower costs and risks, less time away from work, and the advantage that it does not preclude surgery if subsequently required. Conclusions: The concept of subacromial impingement appears to be flawed, as the biomechanical mechanism on which it is based is not supported by current evidence. This concept should therefore be reconsidered in clinical practice because of its potential nocebo effects on patients and its capacity to divert clinicians from more appropriate clinical assessment and management strategies. Accordingly, this review proposes alternative terminology and conceptual frameworks better aligned with current evidence and contemporary approaches to the assessment and management of subacromial shoulder pain.

titre: Stakeholder Priorities for Strengthening Sports Medicine Services in Kazakhstan: A Cross-Sectional Health-System Survey.
titre_fr: Stakeholder Priorities for Strengthening Sports Medicine Services in Kazakhstan: A Cross-Sectional Health-System Survey.
auteurs: Muzrapova Sabina, Jainakbayev Nurlan, Sapargaliyev Rashid, Umurzakov Murat, Esengarayeva Saule, Baisynov Nurlan
resume: Background/Objectives: Sports medicine systems require evidence-informed prioritization of medical, rehabilitation, preventive, and organizational interventions. This study aimed to assess and rank stakeholders' perceived importance of proposed development domains for sports medicine in Kazakhstan, rather than the current performance or quality of the existing system. Methods: An anonymous cross-sectional survey was conducted between December 2025 and January 2026 among 100 stakeholders involved in medical care, rehabilitation, diagnostics, coaching and training, athletic participation, or sports administration. Twelve development domains were rated on a five-point priority scale, followed by a Top-5 selection task. Because the survey form did not technically enforce selection of exactly five options, the primary Top-5 analysis was restricted to the 47 respondents who completed the task as instructed. Results: Among these 47 respondents, rehabilitation and recovery programs were selected by 30/47 (63.8%), injury prevention by 26/47 (55.3%), and both accessibility of medical support and financing/sustainability by 24/47 (51.1%). The all-questionnaire sensitivity ranking (N = 100) showed strong but incomplete agreement with the primary exact-five ranking (Spearman's ρ = 0.889; Kendall's τ = 0.762). The 12-domain ratings showed a pronounced ceiling/invariant-response pattern, and subgroup analyses were treated as exploratory because of small and compositionally unequal subgroups. Conclusions: The findings describe perceived priorities within the surveyed non-probability stakeholder sample. Given the purposive, snowball-assisted recruitment strategy and the lack of full psychometric validation of the study-specific questionnaire, they should not be interpreted as nationally representative estimates of service quality, current shortages, or national policy priorities.

titre: Early detection of oropharyngeal dysphagia in rehabilitation and long-term care sectors: the EDOR-Care cross-sectional study protocol.
titre_fr: Early detection of oropharyngeal dysphagia in rehabilitation and long-term care sectors: the EDOR-Care cross-sectional study protocol.
auteurs: Krethlow Giulia, Oestreicher Valentin, Leuchter Igor, Burgniard Léa, Ménétré Eric, Graf Christophe, Roulin Marie-José
resume: Oropharyngeal dysphagia (OD), or difficulty swallowing, is a common yet frequently underdiagnosed condition that can lead to serious complications, reduced quality of life and increased healthcare costs. Early identification of at-risk patients is therefore essential. Although screening tools such as the Volume-Viscosity Swallow Test (V-VST) are widely used, they remain time-consuming, require trained staff and are often validated only in specific populations (eg, patients who had a post-stroke). This study aims first to establish the prevalence of OD risk in rehabilitation and long-term care units; second, to quantify the agreement between bedside nurses and specially trained nurses using the same institutional screening tools; and third, to estimate the criterion validity of two institutional tools less time-consuming and easier to use against the V-VST, used as the comparator standard. Clinical risk factors and patient characteristics associated with OD will be identified to develop a simple, rapid and reliable predictive risk score. Designed for use by non-specialised staff at admission, this tool should support early detection and optimise resource allocation across diverse care settings. This cross-sectional study will screen for OD all adult inpatients admitted to rehabilitation units and long-term care sectors of the Departments of Clinical Neurosciences and Rehabilitation & Geriatrics, that is, an expected total of 457-487 patients recruited consecutively and exhaustively without random sampling. The primary outcome is the prevalence of OD, which will be compared with published estimates. Secondary outcomes will include identifying risk factors and clinical characteristics, assessing the agreement between bedside nurses and specially trained nurses, validating two institutional screening tools against the V-VST and developing a predictive risk score for early detection at admission. Analyses will comprise proportions with 95% CIs, multivariable logistic regression, percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios, and development of a points-based risk score with internal validation by bootstrapping. The study has received ethics committee approval (2025-00401). This manuscript reports the study protocol: at the time of submission, no participant had been screened, and no data had been collected. Inclusions are planned from 4 January 2027 to 30 June 2027. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed scientific journals and conferences. If internally validated, the predictive score could inform early identification of patients at risk of OD within the study institution; any broader clinical use would require independent external validation and compliance with the applicable medical device regulations.

titre: How consistent is the determination of the anaerobic threshold among members of the same cardiac rehabilitation team?
titre_fr: How consistent is the determination of the anaerobic threshold among members of the same cardiac rehabilitation team?
auteurs: Minagawa Nanaho, Kondo Kazuo, Nishijima Hirotaka, Mori Yusuke, Ikota Takeo
resume: Consistency in the anaerobic threshold (AT) determination is essential for cardiac rehabilitation teams comprising multiple professionals who conduct cardiopulmonary exercise tests (CPETs) and interpret their results. The effect of years of experience on interpreting CPET results, including the AT, has been examined. However, consistency in the AT determination among members of the same institution with experience beyond the training period has not been reported. We evaluated consistency in the AT determination among four members at a cardiovascular hospital (three full-time physical therapists and one part-time consultant physician) with 4 to 30 years of experience with CPETs. Another full-time physical therapist acted as the controller and did not participate in the AT reading. This retrospective study used 260 blinded and randomized CPET data files from 130 patients (130 data pairs comprising inpatient and outpatient data). All observers determined the AT twice using the modified V-slope method. The mean AT values showed significant interobserver differences (p<0.001) driven by a slightly but significantly lower value determined by the consultant physician. No significant differences in the values determined by the three full-time staff members were observed. Despite interobserver differences during inpatient and outpatient phases, the longitudinal change in the AT did not differ significantly (p=0.58). The intrarater reliability of four observers was good [intraclass correlation coefficient (1,1) = 0.87-0.94], with limits of agreement of 103.6 to 185.0 mL/min. The inter-rater reliability was also good [intraclass coefficient (2,1) = 0.87], with limits of agreement of observer pairs of 139.2 to 220.5 mL/min. Reliability was not associated with years of experience. Good consistency in the AT determination is achievable in a clinical setting. Adherence to a single standardized method across the team likely facilitates this consistency and provides a reliable objective measure for monitoring exercise tolerance.
