titre: Assessing the Clinical Value of the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory - Computerized Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT) in Measuring Self-Reported Disability in Youth Undergoing Intensive Interdisciplinary Pain Treatment (IIPT).
titre_fr: Assessing the Clinical Value of the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory - Computerized Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT) in Measuring Self-Reported Disability in Youth Undergoing Intensive Interdisciplinary Pain Treatment (IIPT).
auteurs: Damice Brittany, Smith Allison, Savage Avery, Fragala-Pinkham Maria, Temelkoff Erika, Zurakowski David, Sethna Navil, Shulman Julie
resume: This study investigated the clinical utility of the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory - Computerized Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT), adapted as a self-report measure of disability among youth with chronic pain. Participants (N=199) completed the PEDI-CAT Daily Activities and Mobility subtests and biopsychosocial questionnaires at intensive interdisciplinary pain treatment (IIPT) admission and discharge. First, we conducted cognitive interviews (N=5) to understand participants' interpretation of the items when administered via self-report. Then, we evaluated 1) responsiveness of the PEDI-CAT subtests, 2) convergent validity of PEDI-CAT admission T-scores, and 3) factors associated with average (i.e., recovered) PEDI-CAT T-scores at discharge. Cognitive interviews supported using the PEDI-CAT as a self-reported outcome in youth with chronic pain. PEDI-CAT Daily Activities T-scores significantly correlated with all outcomes at admission except pain intensity and body coordination. Mobility T-scores significantly correlated with outcomes of functioning and risk for poor prognosis on the PPST but did not correlate with psychological outcomes or pain intensity. Daily Activities and Mobility T-scores significantly improved after IIPT (P<0.001). Mean Daily Activities T-scores were average at admission and discharge. Most participants reported below average Mobility T-scores at admission and discharge. Multivariable logistic regression showed less anxiety, younger age, higher admission scores, and shorter length of stay increased odds of reporting average (i.e., recovered) Mobility at discharge. The PEDI-CAT adapted for self-report measured meaningful improvements in disability in youth with chronic pain undergoing IIPT. Further evaluation of the PEDI-CAT psychometrics in youth with chronic pain is warranted.

titre: Nociplastic Pain: A Contemporary Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Clinical Assessment, Controversies, and Management.
titre_fr: Nociplastic Pain: A Contemporary Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Clinical Assessment, Controversies, and Management.
auteurs: Chu Chin-Chen, Lin Yao-Tsung, Wang Jhi-Joung
resume: Nociplastic pain was introduced by the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) in 2017 as a third mechanistic descriptor alongside nociceptive and neuropathic pain, denoting pain from altered nociception without unambiguous tissue damage or somatosensory lesion. Fibromyalgia is its prototypical example; nociplastic mechanisms have also been proposed to contribute, often alongside nociceptive or neuropathic components, to irritable bowel syndrome, temporomandibular disorders, chronic primary headache, and much chronic musculoskeletal and visceral pain. This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between January 2016 and June 2026 on the mechanisms, clinical assessment, controversies, and management of nociplastic pain, integrating recent (2024-2026) conceptual debates with mechanistic and clinical data. We aimed to clarify the distinctions among central sensitization (a mechanism), nociplastic pain (a clinical-mechanistic descriptor), and chronic primary pain (a diagnosis) in a clinically usable form, to appraise the recent validation evidence for the 2021 IASP clinical criteria, and to identify research priorities for the domains in which those criteria remain unvalidated. The descriptor reflects central sensitization, deficient descending modulation, neuroimmune/glial activation, and maladaptive plasticity, plus increasingly recognized peripheral contributions. The 2021 IASP criteria show acceptable reliability in trained raters but uncertain performance in primary care and non-musculoskeletal domains. Management prioritizes, as first line, exercise, psychological therapy, pain neuroscience education, and multidisciplinary rehabilitation, together with centrally acting agents, although the pharmacological evidence derives largely from fibromyalgia trials; opioids and anti-inflammatory drugs are largely ineffective in predominantly nociplastic pain. Nociplastic pain is a clinical-mechanistic descriptor, not a diagnosis, and is best applied as a continuous component of complex pain rather than a fixed diagnostic label. Priorities include validation of criteria beyond the musculoskeletal system, objective biomarkers, and phenotype-stratified trials.

titre: Evaluating artificial intelligence-generated clinical guidance for patellar dislocation: accuracy, readability and qualitative appraisal of DeepSeek-R1 responses.
titre_fr: Evaluating artificial intelligence-generated clinical guidance for patellar dislocation: accuracy, readability and qualitative appraisal of DeepSeek-R1 responses.
auteurs: Liu Shuo, Sun Xiyang, Ma Yunfei, Yang Zhenzhong, Zhang Hanyuan, Mao Hongbo, Xu Bin
resume: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to answer patient questions, but the readability and information quality of patellar dislocation guidance remain unclear. A series of clinical questions covering etiopathogenesis, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, complications, and postoperative rehabilitation of patellar dislocation were posed to DeepSeek-R1 v2.3.1 and ChatGPT-4o. Readability was assessed using the Flesch Reading Ease score (FRES), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Automated Readability Index (ARI), SMOG Index, and Gunning Fog Score (GFS). Three sports medicine surgeons rated responses using DISCERN. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests compared models; Inter-rater reliability (IRR) for DISCERN was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Additionally, we analysed DeepSeek's responses based on the current literature and therapeutic standards. Readability favored ChatGPT-4o across all indices (between-model P < 0.05): DeepSeek-R1 vs. ChatGPT-4o medians (Q1-Q3) were ARI 15.62 (13.90-16.60) vs. 12.54 (10.15-13.41), FKGL 14.39 (12.38-15.24) vs. 11.27 (9.44-12.76), GFS 18.25 (15.20-19.43) vs. 14.55 (13.73-16.53), SMOG 11.02 (9.72-12.18) vs. 9.55 (8.14-10.67), and FRES 9.50 (6.75-25.00) vs. 33.00 (19.75-41.50). Both models exceeded the NIH-recommended sixth-grade reading level (all P < 0.05). DISCERN scores were similar [median (Q1-Q3)] for DeepSeek-R1 vs. ChatGPT-4o: 49.17 (40.25-59.17) vs. 50.33 (38.92-58.42), corresponding to "Fair" quality (P = 0.767). DISCERN agreement was high (single-measure ICC 0.860-0.950). Although both AI platforms can generate clinically relevant responses of moderate quality, they should be regarded as adjunctive information rather than stand-alone clinical guidance, particularly given the high incidence of patellar instability and developmental characteristics of children and adolescents. Exploratory qualitative assessment of DeepSeek-R1 responses identified strengths in clinical explanation and reasoning, while also revealing limitations in citation reliability and readability. Future work should incorporate multi-turn, multi-generation frameworks, more samples with repeated sampling and longitudinal assessment, enforced citation standards, and expanded evaluation to better quantify both clinical utility and reliability.

titre: Beyond Pain Intensity: A Patient-Informed Framework for Documenting Burden in Small Fiber Neuropathy.
titre_fr: Beyond Pain Intensity: A Patient-Informed Framework for Documenting Burden in Small Fiber Neuropathy.
auteurs: Hochman Guy
resume: Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is a sensory-autonomic neuropathy of thinly myelinated Aδ and unmyelinated C fibers that can produce neuropathic pain and multisystem autonomic symptoms. Although diagnostic criteria and confirmatory testing have improved recognition, SFN burden may remain underrecognized even after diagnosis. This narrative review identifies two complementary documentation failures. The translation problem arises when symptom labels and intensity ratings do not capture effects on sustainable function, cognitive workload, emotional well-being, and participation. The fragmentation problem arises when specialties assess multisystem symptoms without preserving their temporal pattern, co-occurrence, shared triggers, treatment trade-offs, and recovery costs. Reverse availability bias is proposed as a conceptual mechanism that may intensify both failures: symptoms or mechanisms not represented in clinicians' mental models may be overlooked in consideration and documentation. The review proposes an SFN Burden Integration Framework (SFN-BIF) that separates symptom presence, burden, and causal attribution and combines validated measures with six core documentation fields: temporal pattern, triggers and relievers, co-occurrence, recovery cost, functional consequences, and cognitive-emotional consequences. Longitudinal patient-reported information is integrated with neurological examination, skin biopsy, quantitative sensory testing, autonomic or organ-specific testing, and cognitive or functional assessment when indicated. Better integration may inform diagnosis and referral, treatment selection and trade-offs, rehabilitation and psychological care, disability assessment, phenotyping, and clinical trial outcome selection while preserving diagnostic rigor. The framework remains conceptual and requires prospective evaluation of validity, feasibility, clinical utility, and administrative burden.

titre: Neurobehavioral Profiles and Clinical Consequences of MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Insights From the Brain Gene Registry.
titre_fr: Neurobehavioral Profiles and Clinical Consequences of MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Insights From the Brain Gene Registry.
auteurs: Granadillo Jorge L, Kaster Levi, Lanzotti Virginia, Grewal Daleep, Schreiber Allyson, Abbacchi Anna M, Gurnett Christina A, Kroll Kristen L, Baldridge Dustin, Hazlett Heather C, Dawalt Leann, Constantino John N, Gupta Aditi, Dougherty Joseph D
revue: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
resume: MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder (MYT1L-NDD) is a rare autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, autism, and obesity. Despite growing recognition, prospective and systematic clinical phenotyping remains limited. Here, we present an exploratory analysis of data from 25 individuals with MYT1L-NDD enrolled in the Brain Gene Registry (BGR), a national platform integrating genetic, neurobehavioral, and clinical data. Neurobehavioral assessments were conducted using the Rapid Neurobehavioral Assessment Protocol (RNAP), including virtual adaptations of the Shipley, Developmental Profile-4, ASEBA Child Behavior Checklist, and Vineland-3. Diagnostic and medication data were extracted from structured electronic health records (EHR). MYT1L-NDD participants were compared to the broader BGR cohort. MYT1L-NDD participants exhibited pronounced impairments in nonverbal cognition and adaptive functioning, particularly in motor tasks, communication, and daily living skills. Behavioral assessments revealed elevated rates of autism symptoms, ADHD symptoms, behavioral conduct problems, oppositional defiance, and anxiety. EHR diagnosis data were available for 10 MYT1L-NDD participants. It showed frequent diagnoses of developmental delays, speech and language disorders, intellectual disability, gastrointestinal problems, and obesity. Medication data on five participants indicated common prescription of alpha-2 adrenergic agonists and laxatives. This study provides the first prospective, multi-source characterization of MYT1L-NDD. Findings expand our understanding of MYT1L-NDD phenotypes in a quantitative and systematic manner and support the value of registry-based approaches for understanding rare neurodevelopmental disorders. Larger, longitudinal, age-stratified studies are needed to further define MYT1L-NDD natural history and inform clinical care.

titre: Lipid requirements for brain development and function: what we can learn from Drosophila melanogaster.
titre_fr: Lipid requirements for brain development and function: what we can learn from Drosophila melanogaster.
auteurs: He Karen, Dee Madeleine Margaret, Simmonds Andrew J
resume: Lipids are required for brain development and function. Impaired lipid metabolism is associated with various neurodevelopmental conditions. Recent work in Drosophila has begun to reveal the cellular and molecular basis of the role of lipids in this process. Here, we focus on the requirement of lipids in the neuroblasts, neurons, and glia of the Drosophila brain. Specifically, we discuss their role in neuroblast proliferation and fate determination, cellular morphology, neuronal fueling, and phagocytosis. We conclude by reviewing lipid profiling techniques and discuss the implications of these roles on neurodevelopment and disease.

titre: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism-Like Behaviors via the CCL5-CCR1/5-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
titre_fr: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism-Like Behaviors via the CCL5-CCR1/5-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
auteurs: Duan Yang-Yang, Jiao Lin-Fei, Liu Pei-Pei, Duan Chun-Hui, Li Xiao, Zhang Zi-Han, Zhang Yue-Qi, Ouyang Xin-Li, Du Hong-Zhen, Liu Sha, Tang Yi, Teng Zhao-Qian, Liu Chang-Mei
resume: The prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective therapeutic drugs, has been rising worldwide. Missense mutations in Polybromo 1 (Pbrm1), a core component of the SWI/SNF (switch/sucrose non-fermentable) chromatin remodeling complex, have been identified as a risk factor for ASD; however, whether PBRM1 loss of function contributes to the pathogenesis remains elusive. Here we provide direct evidence that microglial PBRM1 deficiency leads to altered microglial clusters, excessive neurogenesis, and ASD-like behaviors in mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that PBRM1 directly binds to the Ccl5 promoter and represses the expression of CCL5. Elevated CCL5 promotes the proliferation and neuronal differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs) via the CCR1/5-β-catenin signaling pathway. Importantly, pharmacological blockade of CCR1/5 ameliorates behavioral deficits in Pbrm1 cKO mice. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized microglia-NSPC communication mechanism linking PBRM1 dysfunction to aberrant neurodevelopment and suggest the CCL5-CCR1/5 axis as a potential therapeutic target for ASD.

titre: Breast Milk Macronutrients and Child Growth and Neurodevelopment in a Lactation Cohort in Rural Bangladesh.
titre_fr: Breast Milk Macronutrients and Child Growth and Neurodevelopment in a Lactation Cohort in Rural Bangladesh.
auteurs: North Krysten, Driker Sophie, Khanam Rasheda, Ahmed Salahuddin, Andrews Chloe, Belfort Mandy B, Cherkerzian Sara, Chowdhury Nabidul H, Hasan Tarik, Rahman Sayedur, Paladhi Unmesha Roy, Esteban Amy Lopez, Monthe-Dreze Carmen, Tofail Fahmida, Baqui Abdullah, Sen Sarbattama, Lee Anne Cc
resume: Limited data exist on the relationship between breast milk macronutrient/energy concentrations and child outcomes in settings with high maternal undernutrition. This study aims to determine associations of breast milk macronutrient (protein, fat, carbohydrate) and energy concentrations with child growth and neurodevelopment. In this observational lactation cohort of 99 mother-infant dyads from Sylhet, Bangladesh, mothers provided hand-expressed breast milk samples at 2 and 5 mo postpartum. Infant anthropometrics were obtained at birth, 3, 6, 12, and 24 mo; neurodevelopment was assessed at 24 mo using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-III. Macronutrient concentrations were measured using midinfrared spectroscopy. Associations with growth and neurodevelopment z-scores were estimated using mixed models and linear regression, adjusted for a priori confounders. Primary outcomes were length-for-age z-score (12 mo) and cognitive z-scores (24 mo) in relation to 2-mo protein concentration. Breast milk samples were provided at 2 (n = 98) and 5 mo (n = 87). We found no significant associations between 2-mo protein and 12-mo length-for-age z-scores or 24-mo cognitive z-scores. Higher 2-mo fat (g/dL) was associated with lower weight-for-age z-scores at 3 mo [b: -0.12 (95% confidence interval (CI): -0.24, -0.005)] and lower head circumference-for-age z-scores at 3 [-0.20 (-0.32, -0.09)], 6 [-0.19 (-0.31, -0.08)], and 12 mo [-0.17 (-0.29,-0.06)]. Similarly, 2-mo energy (kcal/dL) was inversely associated with 3-mo weight-for-age z-scores [-0.01 (-0.03, -0.001)] and head circumference-for-age z-scores at 3 [-0.02 (-0.04, -0.01)], 6 [-0.02 (-0.03, -0.01)], and 12 mo [-0.02 (-0.03, -0.01)]. Higher 2-mo carbohydrate (g/dL) was associated with higher motor z-scores [1.08 (0.06, 2.09)], and higher 5-mo carbohydrate with higher cognitive z-scores [1.10 (0.15, 2.05)]. Protein concentrations were not associated with linear or cognitive outcomes in this cohort. Our findings suggest that future studies targeting infant outcomes may optimally be designed to account for factors beyond macronutrient concentration, such as daily milk volume intake, that may impact infant growth and development.

titre: Brain folding as a Fourier series yields a developmental clock.
titre_fr: Brain folding as a Fourier series yields a developmental clock.
auteurs: Goldschmidt Ezequiel
resume: The human fetal cortex begins as a smooth spheroid and progressively folds into a stereotypical sulcal pattern. I show that the spherical-harmonic expansion - the closed-surface generalisation of Fourier's series - reproduces this developmental sequence in reverse on the group-average atlas: truncating the fully formed cortex at low maximum harmonic degree L_max recovers a younger fetal brain; progressively higher L_max recovers the primary, secondary and tertiary folds in the order in which they emerge. From this I derive a closed-form 23-dimensional log-fractional spectral descriptor. On atlas templates (17 Harvard CRL + 16 dHCP weekly templates) it predicts gestational age at MAE 0.13 and 0.38 wk across cohorts after a single supervised linear alignment, and 1.07 and 1.51 wk without. On 28 Yale-Wayne State longitudinal pairs it advances predicted GA in every subject, without cohort matching. On 80 FeTA scans (31 neurotypical, 49 pathological) off-trajectory distance discriminates pathology at AUC 0.80, and unsupervised clustering yields three internally stable, biometrically concordant subgroups - an exploratory finding requiring external validation. Individual-scan gestational-age accuracy is not the descriptor's competitive use (MAE 2.25 wk on FeTA-NT); its individual-scan value is the shape of the residual around the normative trajectory. The framework separates two spatial-scale regimes of folding onto distinguishable spectral bands and is complementary to existing measures of fetal cortical maturation.

titre: A Novel De Novo Heterozygous Missense Variant in CTNNB1 (c.2215A>C, p.Met739Leu) Underlying Neurodevelopmental Disorder With Spastic Diplegia and Visual Defects (NEDSDV): A Case Report.
titre_fr: A Novel De Novo Heterozygous Missense Variant in CTNNB1 (c.2215A>C, p.Met739Leu) Underlying Neurodevelopmental Disorder With Spastic Diplegia and Visual Defects (NEDSDV): A Case Report.
auteurs: Ibrahim Omar Jamal, Rajabi Ali, Bonyadi Mortaza, Barzegar Mohammad
resume: We report a 7-year-old male with microcephaly, spasticity, strabismus, dysmorphism, autistic behaviors, and moderate ID due to a novel de novo likely pathogenic CTNNB1 variant (c.2215A>C, p.Met739Leu). This case underscores Whole Exome Sequencing's diagnostic utility for early detection of rare monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.

titre: Modifiers of Genetics in ASD Etiology.
titre_fr: Modifiers of Genetics in ASD Etiology.
auteurs: Chau Kelly H, LaSalle Janine M
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex and heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with a multifactorial genetic architecture, with risk arising from the interplay between genetic and environmental factors. Although there is a strong heritable component, identified genetic variants explain only a proportion of its susceptibility. Mutations in individual genes or copy number variants (CNVs) each account for less than 1% of cases, while collectively, rare de novo mutations and CNVs are estimated to contribute to approximately 20% of ASD cases. This incomplete explanation of ASD risk through identified genetic variants suggests that additional mechanisms, including gene by environment (G×E) interactions, may contribute to ASD risk.Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, provide an intermediate molecular phenotype through which genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures converge to influence neurodevelopment. Furthermore, consideration of sex by environment (S×E) interactions may help elucidate sex-related differences in ASD prevalence and molecular phenotypes. This chapter synthesizes current evidence for epigenetic mechanisms underlying ASD, with a focus on how genetic susceptibility, prenatal environmental exposures, and biological sex may interact to shape epigenomic patterns relevant to neurodevelopment and ASD risk.

titre: Insulin-mediated ciliary remodeling in the choroid plexus epithelium.
titre_fr: Insulin-mediated ciliary remodeling in the choroid plexus epithelium.
auteurs: Trapp Marleen, Ritter L Aurica, Döking Greta, Cleland James, Hill Anthony D, Patrizi Annarita
revue: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
resume: The choroid plexus (ChP) epithelium plays a crucial role in cerebrospinal fluid production and brain homeostasis. ChP is mainly composed of multiciliated epithelial cells that exhibit a noncanonical ciliary organization whose function is still debated. Insulin signaling is known to be important for central nervous system function, but its role in ChP function and ciliary organization has not been elucidated yet. To investigate how prolonged insulin exposure modulates ChP cells, we treated primary murine choroid plexus epithelial cells (pCPECs) with insulin for up to six days and used a combination of immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization, single cell analysis and Western Blot to explore underlying molecular mechanisms. We demonstrated that prolonged insulin treatment significantly increased the percentage of multiciliated clustered pCPECs and their axoneme length. Prolonged insulin treatment selectively induced translocation of IFT20, a key component of the intraflagellar transport system, to the ciliary axoneme by increasing the cytoplasmatic surface area covered by IFT20. To note, the expression of insulin receptors (IRs) in ex vivo ChP epithelial cells started during late embryogenesis and localized predominantly to the apical membrane, but not in the cilium. Our study suggests that insulin signaling may promote ciliary remodeling in choroid plexus epithelial cells, most likely by modulating intraflagellar transport dynamics involving IFT20. These findings reveal a novel role of insulin signaling in ChP cilia organization and function, with potential implications for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) regulation and neurodevelopmental processes.

titre: Low-to-Moderate Arsenic Exposure and DNA Methylation: A Review of Life-Course Evidence and Mechanistic Insights.
titre_fr: Low-to-Moderate Arsenic Exposure and DNA Methylation: A Review of Life-Course Evidence and Mechanistic Insights.
auteurs: Xiao Han, Peshkova Yana, Wang Li, Rodrigues Lima Fernando, Guidez Fabien
resume: Arsenic exposure affects an estimated 94 to 220 million people worldwide, yet most research has centered on high-dose endemic settings, leaving the epigenetic effects of environmentally relevant exposures undercharacterized. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from 68 studies on DNA methylation alterations associated with low-to-moderate arsenic exposure, integrating human epidemiological, animal, and in vitro data. Gene-specific findings were stage-patterned across the life course, whereas global and repetitive-element methylation findings were heterogeneous. Prenatal exposure perturbs mitochondrial biogenesis, growth and endocrine regulation, vascular development and neurodevelopment. Childhood evidence rests on two studies, implicating mitochondrial, growth-regulatory and mismatch repair genes. In adults, oxidative stress response, cancer and cardiovascular pathways, and metabolic dysfunction are most often affected. Experimental models corroborate several of these processes and show that methylation alterations can persist after exposure ceases. Although CpG-site replication across cohorts remains limited, pathway convergence across independent populations supports biological plausibility. Notably, methylation alterations are detectable at or below the WHO guideline of 10 μg/L, particularly during sensitive developmental windows, although whether these changes lead to disease has not been established. Beyond the nuclear genome, mitochondria are a plausible target for arsenic-induced epigenetic disruption through their roles in one-carbon metabolism and redox regulation. This review critically evaluates mitochondrial DNA methylation findings against five methodological quality criteria and proposes a framework for future investigations, addressing a field where biological rationale has outpaced technical validation. Research priorities include longitudinal designs that link methylation biomarkers to clinical outcomes and intervention trials that assess reversibility to inform regulation.

titre: Developmental vulnerability in infants and toddlers following esophageal atresia repair: A parent-reported functional assessment using WIDEA-FS.
titre_fr: Developmental vulnerability in infants and toddlers following esophageal atresia repair: A parent-reported functional assessment using WIDEA-FS.
auteurs: Coronado Juliana, Doucet Katherine Merritt, Zurakowski David, Zendejas Benjamin, Bajic Dusica
resume: To characterize early adaptive and functional neurodevelopment after esophageal atresia (EA) repair using the Warner Initial Developmental Evaluation of Adaptive and Functional Skills (WIDEA-FS) compared with healthy controls. WIDEA-FS assessments were obtained from preterm (n = 18) and term-born (n = 19) children following repair of short-gap (n = 23) or long-gap EA (n = 14), with or without tracheoesophageal fistula, and from healthy term-born controls (n = 19), between 11 and 40 months of age. Total and domain scores (self-care, mobility, communication, social cognition) were compared using general linear modeling and age-stratified analyses according to gestational age (term-born vs. preterm) and surgical subtype (shot-gap vs. long-gap EA). Functional vulnerability was classified using published WIDEA-FS reference criteria and compared with clinician-documented developmental concerns. Early intervention utilization was also characterized in the patient cohort. Total and domain-specific scores increased significantly with age across all groups (p < 0.001). Children following EA repair demonstrated lower total and self-care scores than healthy controls, irrespective of gestational age or surgical subtype (p < 0.05). No group differences emerged for mobility, communication, or social cognition scores. Classification using published WIDEA-FS reference criteria identified a subset of children with communication and social-cognitive vulnerabilities, with communication-related vulnerability observed exclusively among children with EA. WIDEA-FS scoring demonstrated moderate concordance with clinician-documented concerns (sensitivity 75%, specificity 77%, negative predictive value 97%). The majority of children with EA (86%) received early intervention services, most commonly physical and feeding therapy. Overall, children demonstrated age-appropriate adaptive functioning after EA repair. However, a subset exhibited domain-specific functional vulnerabilities, particularly in communication and social cognition. The high utilization of early intervention services likely contributed to favorable functional outcomes, potentially underestimating the underlying developmental vulnerability in this population. These findings support continued neurodevelopmental surveillance and highlight the potential utility of parent-reported measures for early identification of children who may benefit from targeted developmental interventions.

titre: Postnatal corpus callosum microstructural deviations are linked to neurobehavioral outcomes in preterm infants.
titre_fr: Postnatal corpus callosum microstructural deviations are linked to neurobehavioral outcomes in preterm infants.
auteurs: Wang Wei, Yang Liyuan, Wu Ke, Li Shanqi, Peng Shaoling, Gong Gaolang
resume: The neonatal period surrounding term represents a critical window for corpus callosum (CC) maturation, when axonal growth, pre-myelination, and fiber organization rapidly advance to support emerging motor and cognitive functions, yet preterm birth disrupts this process with unclear mechanisms and long-term consequences. To address this gap, we employed a normative modeling framework, based on a large term-born cohort, to characterize segment-specific CC developmental trajectories and then quantify individual deviations in preterm infants at term-equivalent age (TEA). Preterm infants exhibited selective CC microstructural abnormalities-most pronounced in the genu, anterior body, and splenium-while midsagittal area remained within normative limits. Using partial least squares correlation, we examined associations with neurobehavioral outcomes during toddler period and identified a multivariate brain-behavior coupling unique to the preterm cohort. Specifically, higher gross motor and cognitive scores but lower fine motor score were linked to a coordinated CC profile of increased anisotropy, higher splenial neurite density, reduced diffusivity, and lower genu orientation dispersion. This relationship was absent in term-born controls. These findings suggest that microstructure-informed deviation mapping at TEA may be sensitive to subtle CC alterations that are not apparent on macrostructural measures and are associated with later functional outcomes. This sensitivity to subtle and outcome-related variation highlights the value of this approach as a complement to conventional imaging, and lays the groundwork for future efforts to characterize early white matter development and identify preterm infants at elevated neurodevelopmental risk.

titre: Medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among children and adolescents with disabilities: Lessons from South Korea.
titre_fr: Medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among children and adolescents with disabilities: Lessons from South Korea.
auteurs: Jo Sungbae
resume: This cross-sectional secondary analysis examined medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among Korean children and adolescents with registered disabilities, using a two-stage access framework that distinguished entry into medical-institution rehabilitation from out-of-region use after entry. We analyzed public-use data from the 2023 National Survey on Persons with Disabilities, restricting the sample to respondents younger than 19 years (n = 399; weighted national estimate, 88,611). Weighted descriptive statistics and modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors were used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Overall, 50.0% had no medical-institution rehabilitation use, 31.5% used in-region rehabilitation, and 18.6% used out-of-region rehabilitation; among rehabilitation users, 37.1% reported out-of-region care. In stage 1, non-developmental disability type was associated with higher medical rehabilitation use (PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.28-2.03), whereas eup/myeon residence was associated with lower use (PR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.46-0.94). In stage 2, province residence (PR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.38-3.27) and non-developmental disability type (PR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.13-2.69) were associated with out-of-region use, while male sex was associated with lower out-of-region use (PR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.42-0.92). The most common reason for non-use was use of non-medical facilities (27.4%); better treatment and absence of nearby medical institutions were leading reasons for out-of-region care. Pediatric medical rehabilitation access involves challenges to both non-use and out-of-region use, with implications for local entry support, regional capacity-building, and cross-sector service integration.

titre: LISA failure and school-age motor impairment in very preterm infants: a retrospective cohort study.
titre_fr: LISA failure and school-age motor impairment in very preterm infants: a retrospective cohort study.
auteurs: Portheine Sascha, Swinkels Floor Pm, Vugs Brigit, Dieleman Jeanne P, van Pul Carola, Andriessen Peter, Niemarkt Hendrik
resume: Background Less invasive surfactant administration (LISA) reduces the need for early invasive mechanical ventilation in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome. However, LISA failure (LISA-F), defined as the need for mechanical ventilation within 72 hours of life, occurs in a substantial proportion of cases. While the short-term complications of LISA-F are well described, the impact on long-term neurodevelopment remains unclear. Methods This retrospective cohort study included preterm infants born between 24+0 and 29+6 weeks' gestation who received surfactant therapy in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit. Infants were classified into three groups: LISA success (LISA-S), LISA-F, or primary intubation (PI). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 5.5 years of age using WPPSI-IV-NL for cognition and mABC-2 for motor function. Multivariate analyses were adjusted for gestational age, birth weight z-score, antenatal corticosteroid exposure and severe intraventricular hemorrhage. Results Among 295 infants, 225 (76.3%) received LISA; 32% experienced LISA-F. Follow-up data were available for 168 of 246 survivors (68.3%). LISA-F was independently associated with lower motor scores than LISA-S (adjusted β -2.1; p=0.004), but not with cognitive outcomes. Infants who underwent primary intubation had significantly lower cognitive scores than those in the LISA-S group (adjusted β -5.1; p=0.038). Invasive mechanical ventilation within the first 72 hours was independently associated with motor developmental delay (aOR:3.9; 95% CI 1.2-13.2; p=0.028) Conclusion LISA-F is associated with adverse motor outcomes at school age. Our findings suggest that the early respiratory trajectory after LISA is more relevant to long term motor development than the initial surfactant administration technique itself.

titre: Preterm Risk Factors, Epigenetic Age, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes.
titre_fr: Preterm Risk Factors, Epigenetic Age, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes.
auteurs: Christensen Rhandi, Konwar Chaini, Zhuang Beryl C, MacIsaac Julia, Chau Vann, Cizmeci Mehmet N, Ly Linh G, Guo Ting, Branson Helen, Kobor Michael S, Grunau Ruth E, Miller Steven P
resume: Studies examining biological factors associated with neurodevelopment in the preterm population are limited. It was previously demonstrated that epigenetic age acceleration was associated with better neurodevelopmental outcomes among children born preterm. It is unclear whether this association is modified by clinical and environmental preterm risk factors. To examine whether the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopmental outcomes is modified by preterm brain injury and socioeconomic status. This was a prospective cohort study of children born at 24 to 32 weeks' gestation, recruited from 2 neonatal intensive care units from 2015 to 2019 and followed up to January 2026. The cohort was well characterized with clinical data, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and neurodevelopmental assessments (Bayley-III cognitive and motor domains) at 3 years. Participants with buccal epithelial cell DNA collected at 3 years were included. Epigenetic age (in weeks) at 3 years was determined using the pediatric buccal epigenetic clock and corrected for chronological age to give epigenetic age difference. Primary analyses used linear regression to examine the association between epigenetic age difference, preterm risk factors (any brain injury, severe brain injury, maternal educational level), and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years. Secondary analyses examined whether brain injury and maternal education level modified the associations between epigenetic age difference and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years. A total of 102 study participants (median gestational age, 27.0 weeks [IQR, 25.6-28.9 weeks]; 54 female [53%]) were included. Higher maternal educational level (β = 11.65; 95% CI, 3.55-19.76; P = .005) and epigenetic age acceleration (β = 0.07; 95% CI, 0.01-0.14; P = .04) were associated with higher cognitive scores. Epigenetic age acceleration was also associated with higher motor scores (β = 0.16; 95% CI, 0.06-0.27; P = .003), while extreme prematurity (β = -5.66; 95% CI, -10.85 to -0.46; P = .03) and severe brain injury (β = -10.99; 95% CI, -21.32 to -0.66; P = .04) were associated with lower motor scores. Severe brain injury modified the association between epigenetic aging and motor outcomes (β = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.08-0.74; P = .02), and children with epigenetic age acceleration in the presence of severe brain injury had higher motor scores. In this prospective preterm cohort study, epigenetic aging, severe brain injury, and socioeconomic status were associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes. Children with severe brain injury along with epigenetic age acceleration had higher motor scores. These findings suggest the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopment is context dependent and can vary based on the presence of preterm risk factors.

titre: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
titre_fr: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
auteurs: Tran Phuong, MacBeth Morgan, Wolfe Kelly, Vichayavilas Piyagarnt, Olson Kaitlin E, Leahy Ryan, Stone Matthew, SooHoo Megan
resume: Ductal stenting and surgical systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting (surgical shunt) are alternative strategies to establish pulmonary blood flow in infants with ductal-dependent circulation. The impact of palliation strategy on feeding, nutrition, and neurodevelopment remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 100 infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow (2017-2024) undergoing surgical shunt (n = 57) or ductal stenting (n = 43). Outcomes included feeding, nutrition, hospital course, and neurodevelopment. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with gastrostomy tube (GT) placement. Baseline demographics were similar except for cardiac anatomy. Ductal stent patients reached target enteral feeds post-procedurally sooner (3 vs. 6 days, p < 0.001), had higher discharge weight-for-age z-scores (- 1.30 vs. -1.98, p = 0.02), and smaller declines in growth during hospitalization (p = 0.007). GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting (26% vs. 51%, p = 0.011), but palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.14-1.24, p = 0.12). Oral feeding or breastfeeding within 5 days following palliation was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.81, p = 0.03). Ductal stent patients also had shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU stays and required less vasoactive-inotropic support. Total hospital length of stay, need for reintervention, suspected or diagnosed necrotizing enterocolitis, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Ductal stenting was associated with improved early post-procedural recovery, faster feeding progression, and better preservation of growth compared with surgical shunt palliation. Although GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting in unadjusted analysis, palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment. Early post-procedural oral feeding was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement but may also reflect feeding readiness and clinical recovery.

titre: Target Versus Modified-Standard Fortification of Human Milk and Growth of Very Low Birth Weight Infants: A Double-Blind Randomized Trial.
titre_fr: Target Versus Modified-Standard Fortification of Human Milk and Growth of Very Low Birth Weight Infants: A Double-Blind Randomized Trial.
auteurs: Gebauer Corinna M, Ascherl Rudolf G, Stamm Nadine, Wiegand Julia, Stopsack Marina, Blaeser Annett, Rochow Niels, Fusch Christoph, Mihatsch Walter A, Thome Ulrich H
resume: Background/Objectives: Individualized ("target") fortification of human milk is promoted to improve growth and subsequent neurodevelopment in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants, because standard fortifiers may not provide sufficient protein given the considerable intra- and interindividual variability of human-milk composition. We compared modified-standard fortification (MSF), an optimized high-protein standard regimen, with high-protein target fortification (TFO). Methods: In a single-center, double-blind randomized trial, VLBW infants (24 + 0 - 31 + 6 weeks) receiving 100 mL/kg/d of standard fortified human milk were randomized to MSF (protein and medium-chain triglycerides added to standard fortifier) or TFO until 36 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA). The primary outcome was weight-gain velocity from randomization to 36 weeks PMA; the trial was powered to detect a difference of 0.666 standard deviations. titre: Maternal n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid During Pregnancy and Lactation: Linking Brain Lipid Biology to Cognitive Outcomes.
titre_fr: Maternal n-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid During Pregnancy and Lactation: Linking Brain Lipid Biology to Cognitive Outcomes.
auteurs: Muñoz Carvajal Yasna, Palacios-Avendaño Nicolás, Álvarez Daniela, Ortiz Macarena, Montiel Juan F, Valenzuela Rodrigo, Maliqueo Manuel
resume: Adequate maternal nutrition during pregnancy and lactation is essential for fetal and infant brain development. Among dietary lipids, n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs), particularly docosahexaenoic acid (C22:6n-3, DHA), are of major biological relevance because this FA is preferentially transferred from the mother, accumulates rapidly in the developing brain, and contributes to membrane organization, neuronal differentiation, synaptic maturation, and lipid-mediated signaling. This review integrates current evidence on maternal n-3 PUFA metabolism during pregnancy and lactation, placental and blood-brain barrier transport of DHA, and the mechanisms linking cerebral n-3 PUFA availability to neurodevelopment and cognitive function. Attention is given to selective DHA transport, brain lipid remodeling, synaptic plasticity, neuroimmune regulation, and the translation of experimental findings into human developmental outcomes. Across experimental and human studies, the clearest functional signal emerges under developmental n-3 PUFA deficiency or defined biological challenge, whereas supplementation above nutritional adequacy produces smaller and less consistent cognitive effects. These findings support a context-dependent model in which the functional consequences of n-3 PUFA availability are shaped by baseline nutritional status, developmental timing, brain region, biological challenge, and the assessed cognitive domain. Accordingly, DHA is best understood as an essential component of normal brain development rather than as a nutrient whose supplementation necessarily enhances cognition above nutritional adequacy.

titre: Cooking Oil-Derived Aldehydes: Overlooked Components of the Western Diet with the Potential to Disrupt Fetal Brain Development.
titre_fr: Cooking Oil-Derived Aldehydes: Overlooked Components of the Western Diet with the Potential to Disrupt Fetal Brain Development.
auteurs: Shanahan Catherine, Grootveld Martin
resume: Dietitians routinely recommend refined high polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content culinary oils such as soybean, corn, canola, rapeseed and sunflower oils to pregnant women. Unfortunately, these PUFAs readily undergo peroxidation (especially at high frying or cooking temperatures), generating toxic lipid oxidation products, including reactive aldehydes and oxidized lipid mediators with established biological activities that may negatively impact fetal brain development. This hypothesis-driven perspective paper proposes a conceptual framework linking the maternal consumption of oils contaminated with lipid oxidation products to fetal neurodevelopmental vulnerability. We also identify key research priorities, including improved exposure assessments, the development of reliable aldehyde and other oxylipin biomarkers, and controlled dietary intervention studies. Such investigations will help clarify whether these commonly consumed culinary oils meaningfully contribute to the increasing rates of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes.

titre: Placental Insulin-like Growth Factor Signaling and Neurodevelopment: Emerging Evidence from the Placenta-Brain Axis.
titre_fr: Placental Insulin-like Growth Factor Signaling and Neurodevelopment: Emerging Evidence from the Placenta-Brain Axis.
auteurs: Carver Annemarie J, Williamson Eleanor G, Stevens Hanna E
resume: The field of neuroplacentology is a growing area that focuses on the influence of placental function on brain development. This field has expanded our understanding of the placenta's crucial role in proper neurodevelopment as well as placental anomalies that increase the risk of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Neuroplacentology studies have revealed distinct roles of placentally provided hormones and nutrients in neurodevelopment whose disruption by perinatal problems, including inflammation, can increase the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder and ADHD. Placental insulin-like growth factor signaling significantly influences brain growth in animal model studies and is tightly linked with human neurodevelopmental outcomes. Insulin-like growth factor signaling is well-established as a regulator of placental function and is fundamental in fetal brain cell developmental processes and plays a role in inflammation. Placental insulin-like growth factor signaling underlies the placental production and delivery of hormones and nutrients that are necessary for fetal neural cell proliferation, differentiation, and growth. It is especially important to study this pathway in the placenta due to aberrant insulin-like growth factor signaling found in conditions such as preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, gestational diabetes, and obesity. All these conditions are linked to a greater risk for neurodevelopmental disorders, neuroinflammation, and other anomalies. This research subfield has also revealed sex differences in the insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway that will contribute to understanding the etiologies of these conditions. This area of study has and will continue to identify specific mechanisms, many currently in model systems, which could eventually be leveraged in preventative and interventive care to improve neurodevelopmental outcomes.

titre: Simultaneous Bilateral Cochlear Implantation in a Child with Warsaw Breakage Syndrome and Normal Cochlear Morphology: A Case Report and Focused Literature Review.
titre_fr: Simultaneous Bilateral Cochlear Implantation in a Child with Warsaw Breakage Syndrome and Normal Cochlear Morphology: A Case Report and Focused Literature Review.
auteurs: Samara Pinelopi, Athanasopoulos Michail, Markatos Nikolaos, Koudoumnaki Evangelia, Athanasopoulos Ioannis
resume: Background and Clinical Significance: Warsaw Breakage Syndrome (WABS), also termed DDX11-related cohesinopathy, is an exceptionally rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in DDX11. Sensorineural hearing loss is a recurrent manifestation and has frequently been reported together with structural abnormalities of the cochlea or cochlear nerve. Published experience with cochlear implantation in WABS remains extremely limited. Case Presentation: A 2.5-year-old boy was referred because of absent spoken-language development and limited responses to environmental and speech sounds. Newborn hearing screening had not been performed. After treatment of bilateral middle-ear effusions, comprehensive audiological assessment showed absent transient-evoked otoacoustic emissions and cochlear microphonics, no reproducible auditory brainstem response waveforms at the maximum tested level of 90 dB nHL, and auditory steady-state response estimates in the severe-to-profound range bilaterally. Clinical examination revealed microcephaly, short stature, and global developmental delay, raising suspicion of an underlying syndromic disorder. High-resolution computed tomography demonstrated normal cochlear morphology, while magnetic resonance imaging showed bilaterally visualized cochlear nerves without aplasia or marked hypoplasia. Whole-exome sequencing identified a pathogenic frameshift variant in DDX11 in apparent homozygosity, supporting the molecular diagnosis of WABS. Simultaneous bilateral cochlear implantation was performed at 3 years of age without complications. Longitudinal auditory development, assessed with the LittlEARS Auditory Questionnaire, improved from 0/35 at activation to 10/35 at 8 months, 21/35 at 20 months, and 33/35 at 24 months of auditory age. At approximately 30 months of auditory age, structured language assessments demonstrated further receptive and expressive communication gains, although language development remained influenced by the underlying neurodevelopmental disorder. At 33 months of auditory age, functional auditory performance assessed with PEACH-GR was 90% in quiet, 80% in noise, and 85% overall, while Greek-standardized language testing demonstrated persistent language difficulties relative to chronological-age expectations. Conclusions: Severe-to-profound prelingual sensorineural hearing loss in WABS may occur despite normal cochlear morphology and bilaterally visualized cochlear nerves. In this patient, simultaneous bilateral cochlear implantation was technically uncomplicated. During subsequent bilateral device use, programming, rehabilitation, and maturation, quantitatively documented progressive auditory development and functional communication gains were observed. Comprehensive audiological, radiological, genetic and developmental assessment is essential for individualized implant candidacy and realistic family counseling.

titre: Motor, Postural, and Communicative Phenotype in SHQ1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Dystonia and Seizures: An Interdisciplinary Case Report and Hypothesis-Generating Physiotherapy Framework.
titre_fr: Motor, Postural, and Communicative Phenotype in SHQ1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Dystonia and Seizures: An Interdisciplinary Case Report and Hypothesis-Generating Physiotherapy Framework.
auteurs: Polczyk Artur, Banaszek-Hurła Natalia, Wolańska Ewelina, Wawrzyniak Joanna, Purpurowicz-Miękus Natalia, Winczewska-Wiktor Anna, Steinborn Barbara, Śmigiel Robert
resume: Background: Biallelic variants in SHQ1 (SHQ1 homolog; H/ACA small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein assembly factor) cause neurodevelopmental disorder with dystonia and seizures (NEDDS), but descriptions of spontaneous motor organization, functional communication, and rehabilitation-relevant abilities remain limited. Case: We present a boy with infantile-onset epileptic encephalopathy, dystonia, cerebellar atrophy, and asymmetric spasticity in whom trio WES identified two heterozygous SHQ1 variants in trans: the maternally inherited c.5T>C (p.Leu2Pro) variant and the paternally inherited c.828_831del (p.Asp277SerfsTer27) variant. Both SHQ1 variants remain classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) under ACMG criteria. Based on the available genetic evidence, including segregation in trans, and the close phenotypic concordance, SHQ1-related NEDDS is considered the most likely clinical diagnosis; however, the molecular findings do not independently establish the diagnosis. At 5 years and 4 months, assessment combined neurological and physiotherapeutic examination, Vojta-derived Locomotion Stages, and an adapted, descriptive item-level Bayley-4 assessment conducted outside the normative age range. The child independently expressed LS 3 creeping, brief ineffective homologous lower-limb attempts, supported kneeling with goal-directed upward reaching, and intentional tablet-based augmentative and alternative communication despite severe expressive and motor limitations. Observed task performance during the adapted Bayley-4 assessment was heterogeneous and was interpreted solely descriptively because chronological age exceeded the normative range and administration required accommodations. After adjunctive cannabidiol was introduced, prolonged nocturnal tonic seizures requiring rescue medication became less frequent and subsequently ceased, whereas focal seizures persisted during wakefulness and overall daily seizure frequency did not show a comparable reduction. Because this was a single, unblinded observation with concomitant antiseizure-medication changes and no prospectively predefined, directly comparable observation windows, no quantitative or causal treatment effect can be inferred. The available rehabilitation exposure was reconstructed retrospectively from parental report; detailed treatment progression and standardized longitudinal outcomes were not recorded prospectively. Conclusions: The present case broadens the functional phenotype of SHQ1-related NEDDS and shows that standardized developmental testing alone may underestimate communicative intentionality and functionally expressed abilities when motor output is severely constrained. Integrated functional assessment can refine phenotyping and identify individualized rehabilitation and assistive mobility targets. The assessment-informed physiotherapy framework is clinical and hypothesis-generating; it was not prospectively evaluated and should not be interpreted as evidence of treatment efficacy.

titre: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Walle Agmasie Damtew, Bargshady Ghazal
resume: Background: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by persistent symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity that can affect individuals throughout childhood and adulthood. Accurate and timely detection is important for appropriate support and management, but current assessment relies heavily on behavioural observations, clinical assessments, and information from multiple sources, which can be time-consuming and may be influenced by subjective judgement. These challenges have increased interest in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches that can analyse multiple physiological and behavioural data sources. Multimodal AI approaches may provide a more comprehensive and objective way to detect ADHD by combining complementary information from different data types. Objectives: This systematic review aimed to examine the use of ML and DL methods for ADHD detection using multimodal physiological and behavioural biomarkers, with particular attention to data sources, modelling approaches, multimodal fusion strategies, and reported diagnostic performance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines to identify studies published from 2015 to 2026 that applied machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) methods to multimodal data for ADHD detection. We selected studies using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and extracted and synthesised data from eligible studies. The review included 25 studies. The multimodal data sources examined included neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); physiological signals, including electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and electrodermal activity (EDA); behavioural assessments; and wearable or Internet of Things (IoT)-based measures. We also assessed the included studies for methodological quality and model performance to identify current evidence, limitations, and future research needs. Results: The included studies varied substantially in design and sample size, with participant numbers ranging from 22 to 15,883. Most studies used cross-sectional designs. Early multimodal fusion approaches frequently reported diagnostic accuracies above 80%, demonstrating the potential value of combining complementary physiological and behavioural information. Reported informative biomarkers included frontal brain activity, heart rate patterns, and oculomotor behaviour. However, substantial differences in data sources, acquisition procedures, feature extraction, modelling techniques, and evaluation protocols limited direct comparison across studies. Small sample sizes and a lack of standardised data collection and methodological protocols also challenged the generalisability and reliability of the reported findings. Conclusions: Multimodal machine learning and deep learning approaches show considerable potential for improving ADHD detection by integrating complementary physiological and behavioural information. However, substantial heterogeneity in data collection, devices, datasets, validation procedures, and reporting limits comparability and generalisability across studies. Future research should prioritise standardised data-collection protocols, larger and more diverse datasets (including children, adolescents, and participants from different cultural backgrounds), leakage-safe validation, and independent multi-site testing. Fusion strategies should be selected based on modality compatibility and study objectives. Improving model interpretability alongside predictive performance will also support clinical trust and real-world adoption.

titre: Prenatal Exposure to Delta 9-Tetrahydrocannabinol and Child Neurodevelopment: A Critical Windows Analysis.
titre_fr: Prenatal Exposure to Delta 9-Tetrahydrocannabinol and Child Neurodevelopment: A Critical Windows Analysis.
auteurs: Moore Brianna F, Crume Tessa, Wilkening Greta, Mueller Noel T, Dabelea Dana, Sempio Cristina, Klawitter Jost, Christians Uwe
resume: To identify critical windows of prenatal exposure to delta 9-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC) and child neurodevelopment. We followed 460 mother-child pairs participating in the Healthy Start study through age 5 years. Δ9-THC and its metabolites were measured at about 17 weeks' gestation (n=460) and about 27 weeks' gestation (n=434) in maternal serum, and at birth via cord blood (n=238). At age 5 years, behavior was assessed via Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) and cognition was assessed via NIH Toolbox. For each outcome, we fit a generalized estimating equation model with a Δ9-THC exposure variable, a timepoint variable, and an exposure-by-timepoint interaction term. Δ9-THC exposure prevalence was 8% at 17 weeks, 6% at 27 weeks, and 5% at delivery. Associations of Δ9-THC with most neurobehavioral outcomes were dependent on timing, with generally stronger signals for exposure at delivery. For instance, Δ9-THC exposure at delivery was associated with higher T-scores for attention problems (β=5.2, 95% CI: 2.3, 8.0), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder symptoms (β=2.4, 95% CI: 0.9, 3.8), and pervasive developmental problems (β=3.9; 95% CI: 0.8, 7.1), compared with children with no exposure at delivery. Δ9-THC exposure in late gestation showed particularly strong associations with adverse behavioral outcomes in early childhood. Our study suggests that it is never too late to quit cannabis use during pregnancy to limit adverse effects on child neurodevelopment.

titre: Interpretation of genome sequencing results in children with complex neuromotor phenotypes.
titre_fr: Interpretation of genome sequencing results in children with complex neuromotor phenotypes.
auteurs: Friedman Jan M, Lehman Anna, Guimond Colleen, Mwenifumbo Jill, Boelman Cyrus, Birch Patricia, Couse Madeline, Demos Michelle, Gibson William T, Horvath Gabriella, Lopez-Rangel Elena, Mulpuri Kishore, Patel Millan S, Rajan-Babu Indhu-Shree, Selby Kathryn, Ha Zong Yi, van Karnebeek Clara D M
resume: Although genetic diseases cause at least 30% of neuromotor disorders, genome sequencing is not routinely used for diagnosis in such patients. We assessed the diagnostic value in children with complex neuromotor phenotypes. We performed trio genome sequencing in 108 children with complex neuromotor phenotypes in 100 families. Genetic disease was diagnosed by a multidisciplinary clinical research team on the basis of each child's complete medical history, clinical course, family history, physical examination, imaging studies, and all other laboratory test results, as well as the findings on genome sequencing. Genetic variants that were suspected of being disease causing were subjected to orthogonal confirmation in a clinically accredited laboratory, which classified the variants it reported according to the ACMG/AMP guidelines. We diagnosed genetic diseases that explained the neuromotor phenotype in 53 of the 100 families studied. Almost all of these children had intellectual disability, a seizure disorder, and/or autism spectrum disorder in addition to neuromotor impairment. An important factor contributing to this high diagnostic rate was the use of each patient's complete clinical phenotype, instead of a "molecular diagnosis" based only on the ACMG/AMP variant classification. Our findings demonstrate that complex neuromotor phenotypes in children are usually manifestations of a more generalized neurodevelopmental disorder and that the ACMG/AMP classification alone is insufficient to establish or exclude a causal relationship between a genomic variant and a suspected genetic disease. Canadian Institutes of Health Research, British Columbia Children's Hospital Foundation, and Michael Smith Health Research BC.

Our findings demonstrate that complex neuromotor phenotypes in children are usually manifestations of a more generalized neurodevelopmental disorder and that the ACMG/AMP classification alone is insufficient to establish or exclude a causal relationship between a genomic variant and a suspected genetic disease. titre: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice.
titre_fr: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice.
auteurs: Reyes-Ramírez Lucía de Los, Ciaran-Alfano Laura, Reixachs-Solé Marina, Bergadà-Martínez Araceli, Galera-López Lorena, Martínez-Torres Sara, Navarro-Romero Alba, Maldonado Rafael, Eyras Eduardo, Ozaita Andrés
resume: Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most frequent heritable cause of intellectual disability and autism, involves impaired cognition and synaptic plasticity. Preclinical studies show that inhibition of the cannabinoid type-1 receptor (CB1R) restores key phenotypic traits in Fmr1 knockout (FX) mice. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain undefined. We analyzed the hippocampal synaptoneurosomal transcriptome and confirmed that synaptoneurosomes are an accurate representation of synaptic composition and function. Then, we analyzed this transcriptome after pharmacological CB1R inhibition in male FX mice and found that rimonabant had limited impact at the gene expression level. Notably, detailed in silico analysis of alternative splicing (AS) revealed that rimonabant reverts numerous AS events in FX mice to wild-type levels. These changes in synaptoneurosomal AS landscape suggest a novel mechanism by which CB1R targeting may restore specific AS patterns. Altogether, our results reveal new molecular alterations in FXS context that are sensitive to pharmacological treatment related to cognitive alleviation.

titre: Predictors of Aggression in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
titre_fr: Predictors of Aggression in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
auteurs: Yang Yahui, Wang Fang, Zhang Wei, Chen Aiguo, Zhu Fengshu
resume: Aggression is a common and impairing co-occurring behavior among children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), negatively affecting developmental outcomes, family functioning, and social participation. Although numerous studies have examined factors associated with aggression in ASD, findings remain inconsistent, limiting efforts to improve early identification and intervention. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on predictors of aggression in children and adolescents with ASD. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023416081). A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception to 4 April 2024. Eligible studies were evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for cross-sectional designs and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies, and findings were narratively synthesized. Thirteen studies met inclusion criteria and were of generally satisfactory methodological quality. Across studies, six categories of predictors were identified: demographic, caregiver, core symptom, comorbidity, psychological, and biological factors. Social communication deficits and poor sleep quality showed relatively consistent associations with aggression, although these findings were based on only three and two studies, respectively, whereas evidence for other factors-including age, IQ, caregiver characteristics, and sensory or biological markers-was mixed. Overall, aggression in ASD appears to arise from interacting individual, familial, and contextual influences. These findings highlight the importance of assessing communication skills and sleep problems when evaluating aggression risk and suggest that interventions targeting these domains may reduce aggressive behavior. Future research should employ longitudinal and cross-cultural designs to clarify developmental pathways and strengthen the evidence base for personalized intervention strategies.

titre: Classroom-based observation and intervention of executive function for special education teachers working with preschoolers with Autism.
titre_fr: Classroom-based observation and intervention of executive function for special education teachers working with preschoolers with Autism.
auteurs: Aonsri Chanada, Siritaratiwat Wantana, Mongput Korrawan, Mato Lugkana, Chatprem Thiwaphon, Vincent Claude
resume: Executive function (EF) related behavioral challenges are frequently observed in preschool children with autism spectrum disorder. However, structured, classroom-based observation of these behaviors by teachers remains difficult, resulting in limited practical assessment and recommendations for classroom-based support. This study aimed to examine the feasibility of teacher-administered EF assessment in special education centers and to formulate preliminary, expert-informed recommendations for autistic children with varying communication abilities. A mixed-methods sequential design was used. A total of 793 children with autism aged 3-6 years were assessed by trained teachers. Multidisciplinary expert consultation was conducted to formulate preliminary recommendations for classroom activities based on age and communication profiles. Teachers achieved at least 85% accuracy in score conversion and interpretation, supporting the feasibility of its use in a special education classroom. Patterns of EF-related behavioral challenges observed in 793 children aged 3-6 years were integrated with existing evidence and multidisciplinary expert consensus to inform preliminary recommendations for classroom activities. Working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility were most evident, especially in children with limited verbal communication and those requiring intensive classroom support. Expert-informed classroom activities, including structured play, rule-changing games, memory-based exercises, emotional reflection tasks, and narrative planning, were subsequently suggested with increasing complexity across age groups and levels of communication ability. The findings provide preliminary support for the teacher-administered MU.EF-102 of the classroom use and informed age- and communication-responsive, expert-informed classroom activity recommendations. The effectiveness of these recommendations requires evaluation in future intervention studies.

titre: Sex-dependent effects of imperatorin on autistic-like behaviors and BDNF signaling in rats prenatally exposed to valproic acid.
titre_fr: Sex-dependent effects of imperatorin on autistic-like behaviors and BDNF signaling in rats prenatally exposed to valproic acid.
auteurs: Mohamadian Marjan, Barzi Fatemeh, Jalalian-Javadpour Marzieh, Fallah Hamed, Khaledian Mahdi, Tavakoli Saeed, Vaseghi Salar
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is defined by cognitive impairments such as learning and memory decline, and social interaction and communication deficits. This study investigated the potential effects of Imperatorin (IMP), a furocoumarin and a phytochemical isolated from the leaves of Ferulago trifida on valproic acid (VPA)-induced behavioral and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) alterations in a rat model of ASD. Open field test (locomotion, anxiety), grooming test, marble burying test (OCD-like behavior), novel object recognition memory test, and real-time PCR (BDNF levels) were conducted to collect data. The results showed increased locomotion in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP restored it in males and decreased it in females. Anxiety was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females; IMP had no effect. Grooming was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP restored it in males and decreased it in females. Marbles buried was increased in ASD-like rats in both sexes, while IMP decreased it in males. Memory was impaired in ASD-like rats in both sexes; IMP had no effect. BDNF was decreased in ASD-like rats in both sexes with greater effect in females, while IMP increased it in both sexes. In conclusion, our findings showed hyperlocomotion, anxiety-like behavior, OCD-like behavior, memory deficit, and BDNF downregulation as ASD-related features, with evidence of sex-specific patterns and partial therapeutic effects of IMP.

titre: Extended-Release Guanfacine Hydrochloride is Safe and Effective as Mono- and Adjunctive Therapy in Children and Adolescents with ADHD: A Naturalistic, Multi-Center, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures-Based Study.
titre_fr: Extended-Release Guanfacine Hydrochloride is Safe and Effective as Mono- and Adjunctive Therapy in Children and Adolescents with ADHD: A Naturalistic, Multi-Center, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures-Based Study.
auteurs: Kutuk Meryem Ozlem, Tufan Ali Evren, Kilicaslan Fethiye, Tastepe Neslihan, Imrek Yasemin, Adiguzel Akman Oznur, Alsen Guney Sevay, Baykara Huseyin Burak, Bayraktar Fadime, Akay Pekcanlar Aynur, Korkmaz Gulenay, Ozcan Seda, Ozbaran Nazlı Burcu, Aksu Gülen Guler, Toros Fevziye, Uzun Cakir Aylin Deniz, Cakir Burak, Koksal Merve, Oz Hansa Betul, Kara Aziz, Ozkan Yekta, Celikkol Sadic Cagla, Gercek Hacer Gizem, Polat Tuysuz Berna, Kilic Guder Ayse Nur, Mutlu Caner, Eray Camli Safak, Turan Serkan, Onal Bedia Sultan, Yitik Tonkaz Gulsum, Cobanoglu Osmanli Cansu, Sahin Berkan, Unver Hatice, Tekeoglu Ugur, Naralan Yuksel Sumeyra, Kabukcu Basay Bürge, Basay Omer, Buber Ahmet, Furkan Tanir Muhammed, Gumussoy Ahmet Sefa, Cimen Irem Damla, Yildiz Gundogdu Ozlem, Yildirim Demirdogen Esen, Bozkurt Abdullah, Akinci Mehmet Akif, Buran Burcin Seyda, Ozyurt Gonca, Ozdag Veysel, Sahin Nilfer, Karagoz Duygu, Turan Bahadir, Hosoglu Esra, Korkmaz Ifakat Sule, Gunduz Cilci Yagmur, Esnafoglu Erman, Ikiz Esra Nazli, Subasi Turgut Fatma, Ozturk Masum, Kayis Hakan, Benk Durmus Fatma, Comertoglu Arslan Semiha, Altun Hatice, Ogutlu Hakan, Avcil Sibelnur, Bilgic Berrin, Dincer Mustafa, Gur Kurcaloglu Neslisah, Bozatli Leyla, Aykutlu Hasan Cem, Budagova Gunay, Bilginer Cilem, Cansiz Mehmet Akif, Kandemir Hasan, Gokcen Cem, Inal Neslihan, Ercan Eyup Sabri
resume: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is characterized by impairing and age-inappropriate inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Extended-release guanfacine hydrochloride (GXR) is a selective α2A-adrenergic agonist approved as mono- and adjunctive therapy to psychostimulant medications for ADHD. This multicenter retrospective study aimed to assess patients with ADHD initiating treatment with GXR as mono- and adjunctive therapy in a non-Western, real-world clinical setting. The study was designed as a naturalistic, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs)-based, clinic-based, multi-center study; thirty-two child and adolescent psychiatry clinics from 26 cities located in seven geographical regions of Türkiye were included. Clinicians evaluated ADHD symptom severity at baseline and at the end of the 6th month with Clinical Global Impressions (CGI)-Severity, Improvement, and Adverse Effect scales while parents evaluated symptoms with the DSM-IV-Based Screening Scale for Disruptive Behavior Disorders. Adverse effects after GXR treatment were determined from patient records. Dose equivalents for stimulants, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and mood stabilizers used concurrently with GXR were calculated. Univariate and bivariate analyses along with linear mixed models were used to model change. Logistic regression was used to evaluate predictors of treatment response in sensitivity analysis. Five hundred and sixty-seven patients (n = 437, 77.1% male) with a mean age of 11.2 (SD = 2.8) years were enrolled. Comorbid diagnoses were common (82.4%) along with combination therapy (85.0%). GXR at a median dose of 2.0 to 3.0 mg/day was associated with improvement and the rate of adverse effects was low. GXR showed differential symptom-domain effects, with greater improvement in hyperactive-impulsive (HI) compared to inattentive (IA) symptoms. Children with comorbid autism spectrum disorder (ASD; n = 175, 30.0% of the sample) showed notable clinical improvement. Response was modified by baseline symptom severity. GXR may be a viable treatment option for children and adolescents with ADHD and various comorbidities among Turkish youth in real-world clinical populations, with baseline symptom severity as a potential modifier of response. The differential response favoring HI symptoms and notable effectiveness in comorbid ASD represent clinically important findings of this naturalistic, PROM-based study.

titre: A Preliminary Study of Mobile-Based CBT for Anger Management in Individuals With ASD Without Intellectual Disability.
titre_fr: A Preliminary Study of Mobile-Based CBT for Anger Management in Individuals With ASD Without Intellectual Disability.
auteurs: Choi So Yeong, Chung Kyong-Mee
resume: This study examined the preliminary efficacy of HARU ASD, a mobile-based cognitive behavioral therapy program (mCBT), for anger management in adolescents and young adults with autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability. Thirty participants (intervention group n = 16, waitlist control group n = 14) and twenty-five caregivers (intervention group n = 14, waitlist control group n = 11) were included in the final analysis. Self-report, caregiver-proxy questionnaires (9 subscales each), and direct behavioral observations (5 domains) were administered before and after the intervention. After Holm-Bonferroni correction, only the caregiver-proxy reported direct anger-out remained significant, suggesting reduced direct verbal and behavioral anger expression in the intervention group. These findings suggest the limited effectiveness of the HARU ASD for managing anger among individuals with ASD without ID, although larger trials with prespecified primary outcomes are needed.Clinical trial registration: CRIS (https://cris.nih.go.kr), KCT0009760.

titre: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function.
titre_fr: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function.
auteurs: Li Heng, Choi Jennifer Ja-Yoon, Huang Eric J, Xu Baoji
resume: Silencing of the FMRP-encoding FMR1 gene results in fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common inheritable intellectual disability and autism. FMRP regulates various neuronal functions but clinical trials targeting neurons have failed, suggesting unrecognized disease mechanisms. We find that mice with selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia exhibit audiogenic seizures (AGS) and parvalbumin (PV) neuron loss, recapitulating two key phenotypes observed in FXS (Fmr1<sup>-/y</sup>) mice. By combining snRNA-Seq and RNA immunoprecipitation, we identify several lysosomal mRNAs as FMRP binding targets. FMRP promotes lysosomal protein expression and its deficiency disrupts lysosomal function in microglia. Notably, FMRP depletion reduces Grn-encoded secretory progranulin and increases PV neuron apoptosis in immature brains. PV neuron density is decreased similarly in Grn<sup>+/-</sup>, Fmr1<sup>-/y</sup>, and Grn<sup>+/-</sup>;Fmr1<sup>-/y</sup> mice, and progranulin overexpression rescues AGS and PV neuron loss in Fmr1<sup>-/y</sup> mice. Thus, our study identifies microglia and progranulin as critical regulators of FXS pathogenesis and potential targets for FXS therapy.
