titre: Comparative effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on cognitive domains in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Comparative effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on cognitive domains in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Zheng Miao, Liu Shuning, Wei Yan, Li Yiying, Wu Yutong, Wang Qiyue, Fang Xin, Li Shufang, Zeng Yajing, Liu Chang
resume: This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to compare the effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on attention, working memory, comprehensive executive function, and social-emotional cognition in children with autism spectrum disorder. Five databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 2005-12 April 2026. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses and frequentist network meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias and confidence in network estimates were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and CINeMA, respectively. Thirty-six reports met the eligibility criteria, and 35 reports involving 1694 children contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Non-pharmacological interventions produced a statistically significant moderate overall improvement in cognitive outcomes (standardized mean difference = 0.54, 95% confidence interval 0.36-0.71), with significant benefits for working memory (0.61, 0.09-1.13) and social-emotional cognition (0.47, 0.30-0.65). Social-emotional cognition was the only domain with a sufficiently connected network for comparisons across intervention categories; social-behavioral and technology- and robot-assisted interventions showed the clearest benefits relative to active controls. Evidence networks for attention, working memory, and comprehensive executive function were sparse or disconnected. Confidence was moderate for selected social-emotional cognition comparisons but low or very low for most estimates. Non-pharmacological interventions may improve selected cognitive outcomes in children with autism spectrum disorder, but effects appear domain specific. More adequately powered head-to-head trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

titre: Predicting individual differences in social functioning from functional connectomes in children with autism spectrum disorder.
titre_fr: Predicting individual differences in social functioning from functional connectomes in children with autism spectrum disorder.
auteurs: Li Aqian, Zhang Jie, Yu Chulan, Tan Liming, Yi Aiwen, Xiao Yaqiong
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by profound heterogeneity in social functioning. While previous studies using group-level comparisons and predefined regions of interest have identified neural correlates of social deficits in ASD, the neural basis of individual differences in social functioning remains unclear. Here, we applied connectome-based predictive modeling to resting-state functional MRI data from 65 children with ASD aged 1.5-8 years (mean age = 4.23 years) to predict individual differences in social functioning assessed by the personal-social subscale of the Griffiths Development Scales (GDS). Results showed that whole-brain functional connectivity significantly predicted personal-social scores. The positive predictive network was dominated by connections within the default mode network, with the left precuneus emerging as a core hub. In contrast, the negative predictive network mainly involved inter-network connections, particularly between the frontoparietal and sensorimotor networks. In an independent cohort of 27 children with ASD aged 1.25-8 years (mean age = 3.31 years), the positive-edge model showed a significant association with personal-social scores, whereas the negative-edge and combined models did not. These findings suggest that intrinsic large-scale brain network organization is associated with individual differences in social functioning in children with ASD, highlighting the potential of network-level approaches for characterizing neurodevelopmental heterogeneity and supporting future precision-oriented research.

titre: Mental health outcomes in Prader-Willi Syndrome: An Australian cohort study.
titre_fr: Mental health outcomes in Prader-Willi Syndrome: An Australian cohort study.
auteurs: Baker Emma K, Chellew Tayla, Bui Minh, Rogers Carolyn, Field Michael J, Williams Katrina, Amor David J, Godler David E
resume: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is an imprinting disorder associated with complex cognitive, physical, and behavioral features, as well as high rates of mental health conditions. Understanding mental health conditions in individuals with PWS and their association with behavioral characteristics is an essential step towards better supporting individuals with PWS. Thirty individuals with PWS (14 deletion, 16 non-deletion) aged 3-45 years participated in this study to examine associations between mental health conditions (Prader-Willi Syndrome Mental Health Questionnaire), intellectual functioning (Wechsler Intelligence Scales), autistic traits (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule-2), and challenging daytime behaviors (Prader-Willi Syndrome Behavior Questionnaire; Aberrant Behavior Checklist). 73% of individuals with PWS had at least one parent-reported mental health condition. Anxiety (65%) was the most common, followed by obsessive compulsive disorder (43%) and depression (40%). While reports of any mental health condition and depression were more common in individuals with a deletion compared to their non-deletion counterparts, these differences were primarily driven by the fact that the deletion group was significantly older than the non-deletion group. Those with PWS and mental health conditions had lower verbal IQ (p = .003), greater autistic traits (p < .001), greater food seeking (p = .004) and oppositional behaviors (p = .021), and increased maladaptive behaviors (p = .001) compared to those without a mental health condition. This study highlighted elevated rates of mental health conditions and additional cognitive and behavioral challenges among individuals with PWS, including in young children with PWS. Age-related factors were a primary factor relating to differences between molecular classes on mental health presentations, highlighting the need for earlier supports and interventions that may improve mental health prognoses in individuals with PWS.
resume_fr: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is an imprinting disorder associated with complex cognitive, physical, and behavioral features, as well as high rates of mental health conditions. Anxiety (65%) was the most common, followed by obsessive compulsive disorder (43%) and depression (40%). Those with PWS and mental health conditions had lower verbal IQ (p = .003), greater autistic traits (p < .001), greater food seeking (p = .004) and oppositional behaviors (p = .021), and increased maladaptive behaviors (p = .001) compared to those without a mental health condition. titre: OPHN1-related neurodevelopmental disorders: clinical and genetic findings with novel variants.
titre_fr: OPHN1-related neurodevelopmental disorders: clinical and genetic findings with novel variants.
auteurs: Bolat Hilmi, Aydın Hilal, Genç-Akdağ Dilan, Kalay İrem, Öztürk Murat, Sapmaz Büşra, Oktay Yavuz, Sönmezler Ece, Aytaç Adil, Manav-Yiğit Zehra, Ünsel-Bolat Gül
revue: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
resume: Pathogenic variants in the OPHN1 gene are associated with X-linked intellectual developmental disorder, Billuart type (OMIM #300486), characterized by intellectual disability, distinctive facial features, cerebellar abnormalities, ventriculomegaly, epilepsy, and variable neuropsychiatric manifestations. In this study, four male individuals from four unrelated families presenting with intellectual disability and developmental delay were evaluated. Comprehensive clinical, neuroimaging, and molecular genetic data were collected. Genetic analyses were performed using whole-exome or clinical exome sequencing. Hemizygous OPHN1 variants were identified in all individuals. Two variants, a nonsense variant, c.226del (p.Leu76Ter), and a frameshift variant, c.226_227del (p.Leu76AspfsTer2), were predicted to introduce premature termination codons resulting in loss of protein function and were classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Additionally, two intronic splice-site variants (c.1527-3 C > G and c.2158 + 5G > A) were classified as variants of uncertain significance; however, in silico analyses strongly supported their potential to disrupt normal splicing. The clinical features observed in the affected individuals, including developmental delay, intellectual disability of variable severity, characteristic facial features, and cerebellar and ventricular abnormalities, were consistent with previously reported OPHN1-associated phenotypes. Neuropsychiatric features, including autism spectrum disorder and hyperactivity, were also observed, highlighting phenotypic variability. This study reports the first OPHN1-related cases from Türkiye and expands the molecular and phenotypic spectrum of OPHN1-associated neurodevelopmental disorders by identifying three novel variants. Our findings support the pathogenic relevance of both loss-of-function and splice-site variants and contribute to improved genotype-phenotype correlation and diagnostic evaluation.

titre: Barriers and enablers shaping autistic college students' pathways into advanced manufacturing careers.
titre_fr: Barriers and enablers shaping autistic college students' pathways into advanced manufacturing careers.
auteurs: Newbutt Nigel, Fan Yujiao, Kang Hyo, Orlando Ann-Marie, Asadizanjani Navid, Nazef Adam
resume: Autistic college students are strongly represented in STEM disciplines, yet continue to experience disproportionately poor employment outcomes after graduation. This study explores their lived experiences navigating educational and career pathways into advanced manufacturing, a high-demand sector facing persistent workforce shortages and substantial public investment, yet largely absent from autism and employment scholarship to date. Sixteen autistic STEM undergraduates (current or previous) from across the US participated in three 90-minute focus groups conducted via Zoom. Sessions examined students' career aspirations, job search experiences, perceived barriers, and support needs, and were analysed using thematic analysis to identify enablers and systemic barriers shaping participants' transitions from education to industry. Participants demonstrated proactive engagement in developing technical skills through coursework, self-directed learning, and hands-on experiences. However, they encountered opaque hiring processes, unclear interview expectations, limited access to prior industry experience, workplace sensory challenges, and fragmented institutional support, often relying on informal networks and AI-based tools to compensate. Participants emphasized inclusive, sensory-aware learning environments, structured career preparation, and autism-informed mentorship as critical bridges between academic training and workforce expectations. Employment disparities reflect systemic misalignment rather than individual deficits, underscoring the need to redesign education-to-work pathways that recognize and leverage autistic strengths.

titre: Differences in autism features and adaptive functioning between adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and social communication disorder.
titre_fr: Differences in autism features and adaptive functioning between adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and social communication disorder.
auteurs: Park Seong Hee, Cho Sung Ja, Kang Naok, Joung Yoo-Sook
resume: This study aimed to characterize adolescents with social communication disorder (SCD) in comparison with those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) across two dimensions: autism features and adaptive functioning. SCD shares social communication difficulties with ASD, resulting in unclear diagnostic boundaries and raising concerns about its clinical utility given that existing research and resources remain largely ASD-oriented. Data from 76 adolescents with ASD and 44 with SCD (ages 10-18 years) were analyzed. Lifetime and current autism features were assessed using the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Social Responsiveness Scale, Second Edition (SRS-2), respectively, and adaptive functioning using the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition. Propensity score matching was performed using age and Full-Scale Intelligence Quotient, and group differences were compared before and after matching. Exploratory interaction analyses additionally examined potential moderators of group differences. After matching, adolescents with SCD showed less severe lifetime autism features across the core ADI-R domains, with large effect sizes (ds = .98-1.34, all p <.001). Current autism features showed smaller group differences, which remained significant across all SRS-2 subscales except Social Motivation (ds = .46-.68, p = .004-.046). Adolescents with SCD showed better adaptive functioning than those with ASD, although group differences in Communication (p = .085) and Socialization (p = .144) were no longer statistically significant after matching. Psychiatric comorbidity moderated group differences in Communication, Socialization, and overall adaptive functioning, while attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder showed a similar but less robust pattern for Communication, which did not remain significant after correction. Overall, accounting for age and intellectual ability, the distinction between ASD and SCD remained evident at the symptom level, whereas functional differences were partly influenced by these factors. These findings suggest that diagnostic classification alone may not fully capture the functional needs of adolescents with ASD and SCD, highlighting the importance of a multidimensional approach that considers symptom profiles, adaptive functioning, developmental and intellectual factors, and psychiatric comorbidity.

titre: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia.
titre_fr: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia.
auteurs: Huang Keduo, Zuo Pengxiang, Luo Xuemei, Ji Chun, Yang Fang, Huang Yuhao, Wang Xiaole
resume: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and developmental dyslexia (DD) are highly comorbid, yet objective differentiation from individual disorders remains challenging due to the lack of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model leveraging multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development (TD). Ninety children (27 ADHD-DD, 40 ADHD, 23 TD) underwent EEG during a VSWM task. Five feature categories were extracted: event-related potentials, time-frequency characteristics, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic metrics, and nonlinear dynamics. Three feature-processing strategies and nine classifiers were compared within a nested cross-validation framework. Feature contribution was quantified by coefficient back-projection of the optimal PCA-LR mode. Sensitivity and permutation analyses were performed. The PCA-LR model achieved a balanced accuracy of 80.5%, a Macro-F1 of 0.799, and a Macro-AUC of 0.912. Class-wise AUCs were 0.905 for ADHD-DD, 0.904 for ADHD, and 0.927 for TD. Left temporal α-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature in both disorder groups. ADHD-DD was distinguished by widely distributed cross-regional connectivity spanning θ and α bands and by P200 amplitude. ADHD was characterized primarily by α-band network metrics and α-ERD, whereas TD relied mainly on θ and α bands functional connectivity and graph-theoretic metrics. Our findings suggest that multidimensional task-state EEG features may help differentiate children with ADHD-DD comorbidity from those with ADHD or typical development. They also indicate that machine-learning approaches may be useful for identifying neurodevelopmental comorbid conditions.

titre: Beyond heartbeats: re-thinking interoception in autism through virtual reality and computational modelling.
titre_fr: Beyond heartbeats: re-thinking interoception in autism through virtual reality and computational modelling.
auteurs: Savickaite Sarune, Li Ruichen, Nagai Yukie
resume: Interoception, the sensing and interpretation of internal bodily signals, is increasingly invoked to explain heterogeneity in autism, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. A major reason is methodological: the field remains cardio-centric and relies heavily on heartbeat counting tasks and trait questionnaires, which are vulnerable to cognitive strategies, attention, expectancy effects, and confounds such as alexithymia and anxiety. Autism research further indicates that interoception is multidimensional (accuracy, sensibility, metacognitive awareness) and developmentally dynamic, with evidence for dissociations across components and compensation across the lifespan. We argue that progress requires reframing interoception as an inference problem: the brain estimates hidden physiological states from noisy sensory evidence under context-dependent precision weighting (predictive processing/active inference). Building on this framework, we propose a participatory, multimodal research program for autism that integrates (i) lived experience as hypothesis-shaping data, (ii) virtual reality (VR) as an experimental testbed to manipulate embodiment, sensory load, agency cues, and feedback, and (iii) computational physiological modelling to estimate latent cardiovascular-respiratory and autonomic-control parameters, which could subsequently constrain separately specified models of perceptual inference.

titre: ADHD-related neurodiversity and innovation in marketing teams: a grounded theory framework of customer-oriented boundary-spanning.
titre_fr: ADHD-related neurodiversity and innovation in marketing teams: a grounded theory framework of customer-oriented boundary-spanning.
auteurs: Alipour Sima, Rastgar Abbas Ali, Sorooshian Shahryar
resume: This study explores how ADHD-related neurodiversity is experienced within marketing teams, particularly in customer-oriented and boundary-spanning work. Using a grounded theory approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 35 marketing managers, frontline employees, and freelancers/consultants, including 19 participants with a formal ADHD diagnosis and 16 participants with direct professional experience working with colleagues with ADHD. The analysis generated three theoretical codes: Neurodiverse Cognitive Synergy, Mediated Empathy in Boundary-Spanning, and Resilient Organizational Adaptation. The findings indicate that ADHD-related characteristics, including divergent thinking, creativity, intense focus, and adaptability, may be experienced as resources. At the same time, impulsivity, distraction, stress, communication difficulties, and social isolation may create challenges. These outcomes appear to depend on task demands, role fit, interpersonal relationships, and organizational support. The study develops an exploratory, data-grounded framework that explains how organizational and relational conditions may shape how ADHD-related characteristics are engaged in customer-oriented marketing work, without assuming a direct or causal relationship between ADHD and innovation.

titre: Predictors of body appreciation in mothers of children living with ASD: the role of physical activity, self-compassion, and emotional eating.
titre_fr: Predictors of body appreciation in mothers of children living with ASD: the role of physical activity, self-compassion, and emotional eating.
auteurs: Pierote Marina Reuter, Rocon Isabela Pereira, da Silva Gabriela Grillo, Soares Fabíola Lacerda Pires
resume: Mothers of children living with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often experience high levels of emotional overload, which can negatively impact their eating behaviors and body image. In this context, body appreciation-a key facet of positive body image-serves as an important protective factor. However, evidence regarding the determinants of body appreciation among caregivers of children with ASD remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the sociodemographic, clinical, lifestyle, and psychological factors associated with body appreciation in mothers of children living with ASD. This cross-sectional study evaluated 143 mothers of children with ASD residing in Espírito Santo, Brazil. Data were collected online through self-administered questionnaires assessing sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, nutritional status, lifestyle habits, self-compassion, emotional eating, and body appreciation. Multiple linear regression analysis was conducted using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP, version 0.18.0) to identify predictors of body appreciation. Multiple regression analysis demonstrated that higher body appreciation was significantly predicted by engagement in physical activity (β = 0.293; p = 0.044), child's age over six years (β = 0.329; p = 0.016), and higher self-compassion (β = 0.440; p < 0.001). High Body Mass Index (BMI) (β = -0.034; p = 0.005) and emotional eating (β = -0.010; p < 0.001) were inversely associated with body appreciation. Self-compassion and physical activity emerged as key positive correlates of body appreciation, whereas elevated BMI and emotional eating were identified as negative predictors in this population. Given the cross-sectional design, longitudinal studies across diverse geographical settings are needed to confirm causality and support generalizability. Identifying these predictors provides actionable insights for designing targeted interventions aimed at promoting positive body image and mitigating dysfunctional eating behaviors in mothers of children with ASD.

titre: Experience in action: Using art-science activities to explore experiences of movement and the body in Parkinson's and autism.
titre_fr: Experience in action: Using art-science activities to explore experiences of movement and the body in Parkinson's and autism.
auteurs: Poliakoff Ellen, Hall Antony, Edmonds Eve, Baimbridge Peter, Copitch Gary, Hanks Graham, Sullivan Matthew, Gowen Emma
resume: To explore possible new directions for sensorimotor research, we created experiential workshops for people with lived experience. Seven people with Parkinson's and six older autistic adults attended artist-led drop-in art-science workshops, designed with advisors with lived experience. Open-ended activities based on sensorimotor experiments provoked spontaneous and unexpected conversations between visitors and researchers about their experiences of movement and the body. We invite others to apply this informal playful approach, which was both enjoyable and effective in generating future research ideas.

titre: "Our Principal Makes It Happen": The Role of Implementation Leadership in Supporting Evidence-Based Practices With Autistic Children in Inclusive Settings.
titre_fr: "Our Principal Makes It Happen": The Role of Implementation Leadership in Supporting Evidence-Based Practices With Autistic Children in Inclusive Settings.
auteurs: Kang Sungeun, Ghosh Choudhuri Priyanka, Sridhar Aksheya, Landa Yasmín, Kim Emily S, Locke Jill
revue: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
resume: With the growing inclusion of autistic children in general education settings, the need for effective use of evidence-based practices (EBPs) in schools has become increasingly important. Leadership behaviors by principals and administrators that support educators' use of EBPs with autistic children play a crucial role in promoting and sustaining these practices. This study aims to understand implementation leadership in schools quantitatively and qualitatively. In this mixed-methods study, participants included 161 general education teachers, 138 special education teachers, and 62 paraeducators (N = 361). Participants completed the School Implementation Leadership Scale (SILS), which assesses the degree to which their school leader is knowledgeable, supportive, proactive, perseverant, communicative, centered on the school's vision/mission, and available. Eighty-two participants were randomly selected for an interview to discuss their high or low EBP implementation. Quantitative analysis via aggregated mean scores on the SILS subscales (Total M = 2.4) shows educators rate their school's leadership qualities in the moderate range. Qualitative analysis provides insights into the educators' expressed needs and desires when it comes to support from their leadership. The results highlight the importance of strong leadership to improve the implementation of EBPs for autistic children in general education settings. Authors discuss implications and recommendations to support educators' EBP use.Lay AbstractAs more autistic children are included in general education classrooms, it is increasingly important for schools to use research-supported strategies known as evidence-based practices (EBPs). School leaders, such as principals and administrators, play a crucial role in helping teachers implement these practices consistently and effectively. This study aims to understand the perspectives of 361 educators, including 161 general education teachers, 138 special education teachers, and 62 paraeducators, regarding the support they receive from school leadership in using EBPs with autistic children. Participants completed a survey called the School Implementation Leadership Scale, which included questions about various leadership qualities, such as being knowledgeable, supportive, proactive, perseverant, communicative, aligned with the school's vision and mission, and available to support the use of EBPs. On average, educators rated their school leadership as moderately supportive. To further explore educators' experiences, selected participants were also invited to participate in interviews. These interviews provided deeper insights into what educators find most helpful from school administrators when implementing EBPs for autistic children. The results emphasize the importance of strong, supportive leadership in building a positive and inclusive school environment and helping educators use EBPs. The authors offer practical recommendations to help school administrators better support their staff in using EBPs.

titre: Why Do You Think You're More Likely to be Queer? Exploring Autistic Perspectives on the Intersection Between Autism and Sexual Minority Identities.
titre_fr: Why Do You Think You're More Likely to be Queer? Exploring Autistic Perspectives on the Intersection Between Autism and Sexual Minority Identities.
auteurs: Pemberton Elle, Milne Elizabeth, Fox John R E
revue: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
resume: Autistic individuals are more likely to be sexual minorities (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual, asexual). While several theories have been posited to explain this overlap, the voices of autistic sexual minorities are missing from this conversation. Moreover, there is limited qualitative research exploring the intersection between their dual identities. The co-creation of research by autistic sexual minorities is, therefore, an ethical imperative. This research used semi-structured interviews, facilitated by the shared lived experience of the lead researcher. Fourteen autistic sexual minorities were asked why they think they're more likely to be sexual minorities and how they experience the intersection between their two identities. Reflexive thematic analysis identified four themes: (a) my identities are interconnected, for better or worse, (b) resisting the influence of social norms on sexual orientation, (c) the intersection between autism and a-spec (asexual and aromantic) identities and (d) being autistic within the LGBTQIA+ community. These findings validate intersectionality as a framework for understanding autistic sexual minority identities and suggest that an indifference to social norms is key to autistic sexual minority identities. Recommendations are provided to facilitate inclusive, LGBTQIA+ spaces and develop educational resources to help autistic sexual minorities navigate attraction, intimacy and consent.Lay AbstractAutistic people are more likely to be sexual minorities (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual, asexual). Several theories have attempted to explain why this is; however, the actual voices of autistic sexual minorities are missing from this conversation. In addition, there is very little research exploring how their two identities intertwine. As such, a researcher who is part of this community interviewed 14 autistic sexual minority adults to find out why they think they're more likely to be sexual minorities and how their autistic and sexual minority identities influence one another. Through analysing these conversations, four main themes were identified: (a) my identities are interconnected, for better or worse, (b) resisting the influence of social norms on sexual orientation, (c) the intersection between autism and a-spec (asexual and aromantic) identities and (d) being autistic within the LGBTQIA+ community. These findings suggest that autistic and sexual minority identities combine to produce a unique lived experience. Participants suggested that they may be more likely to be a sexual minority because they don't care about following typical social norms. Recommendations are given to create more inclusive LGBTQIA+ spaces and develop educational tools to help autistic people navigate the complexities of attraction, intimacy and consent.

titre: Past, present, and future of non-pharmacological interventions for autism spectrum disorder: A global bibliometric and thematic analysis (2001-2025).
titre_fr: Past, present, and future of non-pharmacological interventions for autism spectrum disorder: A global bibliometric and thematic analysis (2001-2025).
auteurs: Feng Xiaowei, Song Yu, Li Xuecheng, Yang Yibei, Zhang Dong, Zhang Yanfeng, Zhao Shanguang
resume: Non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) have become increasingly important in addressing the complex and heterogeneous needs of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), particularly in light of the limitations associated with pharmacological treatments. This study aimed to systematically map the global research landscape and thematic evolution of NPIs for ASD from 2001 to 2025 using bibliometric approaches. A total of 341 English-language articles were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Microsoft Excel and Biblioshiny were employed to perform descriptive analysis, co-authorship network mapping, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and thematic evolution analysis based on Keywords Plus. The findings indicate a sustained increase in research output, particularly after 2011, with publication volume peaking in 2024 and citation impact continuing to rise. Music therapy, applied behavior analysis, and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation emerged as the most influential intervention approaches. The United States led in both publication volume and academic impact, followed by China and the United Kingdom. Thematic evolution analysis revealed a gradual shift from behavior-oriented frameworks toward mechanism-informed and context-sensitive approaches, with increasing attention to early intervention, population heterogeneity, and family involvement. Research on NPIs for ASD is undergoing a transition toward more integrative, individualized, and evidence-based paradigms. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal designs, cross-cultural validation, and the translation of mechanistic insights into scalable, real-world interventions.

titre: Altered glymphatic system measures and functional network connectivity in autism spectrum disorder: A longitudinal study examining associations with prognosis.
titre_fr: Altered glymphatic system measures and functional network connectivity in autism spectrum disorder: A longitudinal study examining associations with prognosis.
auteurs: Zhang Manxue, Luo Tingting, Zhao Shengnan, Li Lei, Jiang Yuchu, Duan Xiaoxia, Situ Mingjing, Huang Yi
resume: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by social deficits and repetitive behaviors, yet prognostic biomarkers remain elusive. This study investigated the interplay between glymphatic function and functional network connectivity (FNC) in ASD and their longitudinal associations with clinical outcomes. This combined cross-sectional and two-year prospective longitudinal study included 50 ASD children and 50 controls. Glymphatic function was assessed using the along the perivascular space (ALPS) index and global blood-oxygen-level-dependent to cerebrospinal fluid (gBOLD-CSF) coupling, alongside FNC analysis. Cross-sectionally, ASD participants showed significantly reduced ALPS index, gBOLD-CSF coupling, and widespread FNC reductions. Longitudinally, among the 40 ASD participants who completed follow-up, glymphatic function increased over time. Greater increases in ALPS were correlated with greater reductions in ADOS-CSS. In the symptom-improved subgroup, four FNC connections (including DMN-DAN) increased over time. In contrast, no consistent pattern was found in the non-improved group. Baseline inter-network connectivity measures were associated with ADOS-CSS reduction in univariate analyses, but the multivariate model was not significant. Mediation analysis showed an indirect association between baseline gBOLD-CSF coupling and long-term ADOS-CSS reduction via DMN-DAN FNC reduction (indirect effect = -0.22, 95% CI [-0.42, -0.07]). These findings indicate that glymphatic function and FNC are altered cross-sectionally and improve longitudinally in parallel with symptom changes in ASD and suggest that baseline gBOLD-CSF coupling is indirectly associated with long-term clinical improvement through DMN-DAN connectivity. Together, these results highlight the potential of glymphatic and functional connectivity measures as prognostic imaging markers in ASD.

titre: Association between sensory processing and motor performance in children aged 6 to 11 years: a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Association between sensory processing and motor performance in children aged 6 to 11 years: a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Silva Maia Ana Clara, Duque Weber Meyene, Tudella Eloisa
resume: For motor responses to be appropriately adapted to the task, effective sensory processing is required. Our aim was to characterize sensory processing patterns and their association with motor performance in children aged 6 to 11 years. This cross-sectional study included children aged 6 to 11 years, of both sexes, from public and private schools in a Brazilian municipality. The caregivers completed a sociodemographic questionnaire for characterization purposes and the Short Sensory Profile 2 (SSP2) to assess sensory processing. Children's motor performance was evaluated using the Movement Assessment Battery for Children - 2nd Edition. Children were divided into two groups: the typical group, composed of children with typical sensory processing, and the atypical group, composed of children with at least one atypical sensory processing pattern. The final sample comprised 605 children (50.2% female; mean age 8.05 ± 1.38 years). The atypical group included 483 children, representing 79.8% of the sample. Sensory avoiding and sensory sensitivity were the most prevalent patterns, both predominantly classified within the "less than others" scoring category. There was no statistically significant association between motor performance and sensory processing groups. However, the sensory seeking pattern was identified as associated with higher odds for low motor performance, with children classified as "more" having 2.26 times higher odds of low motor performance compared with those classified as "typical." In contrast, the sensory avoidance pattern, being classified as "less," reduced the odds of low motor performance by 64% ([1 - 0.36] × 100) compared with the "typical" category. Additionally, male sex was associated with higher odds of low motor performance, whereas higher gestational age was associated with lower odds of low motor performance. Although a large proportion of children presented at least one atypical sensory processing pattern, the most frequent score across all patterns was "typical." Moreover, sensory seeking emerged as associated with higher odds for low motor performance, while sensory avoidance was associated with lower odds for low motor performance. Further studies are needed to investigate the potential associations between sensory processing patterns and motor performance in children.

titre: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
titre_fr: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
auteurs: Khodayari Negin, Sedghy Farnaz, Ranjbar Mehdi, Pashazadeh Azari Pouya, Houshmand Fatemeh, Shahrokhi Raeini Azadeh, Mahmoodi Merat, Bashiri Hamideh, Kheirandish Reza
resume: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n=12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

titre: Cultural Context Matters: Development of South African Reference Values for the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-second edition (Ages 6-12 Years).
titre_fr: Cultural Context Matters: Development of South African Reference Values for the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-second edition (Ages 6-12 Years).
auteurs: Smits-Engelsman Bouwien, Coetzee Dané, Pienaar Anita E, Verbecque Evi
resume: The Movement Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (MABC‑2), is widely used internationally to identify motor coordination difficulties. However, reliance on "imported" Western European norms for score interpretation in culturally and socio‑economically diverse contexts remains a significant challenge. This study aimed to quantify the magnitude of normative divergence and to establish contextually representative benchmarks, using a large sample of South African children as a model for local norm development. Local reference values were developed using anonymized data from 2064 South African children aged 6-12 years, stratified by socioeconomic level and sex. Raw scores were converted to scaled scores to generate percentile ranks and age‑band cut‑off values. Comparative analyses examined differences in score distributions between the imported Dutch/Flemish norms and the newly derived local reference values. All MABC‑2 items showed statistically significant differences between imported and locally derived reference values (p < 0.001), with item‑level effect sizes (Hedges' g) ranging from 0.49 to 2.12. Applying the Dutch/Flemish norms to this cohort resulted in 29% of children scoring below the 5th percentile, compared with the expected 5% under the local normative distribution. These findings demonstrate that motor performance benchmarks are not globally interchangeable. Reliance on imported norms leads to substantial shifts in classification rates, increasing the risk of over‑identification of motor difficulties in non‑Western contexts. Establishing local reference values provides a more equitable framework for clinical interpretation and supports the need for culturally and contextually appropriate motor assessment practices worldwide.

titre: Small-for-gestational-age and suspected developmental coordination disorder in preschool children:A national cross-sectional study highlighting vulnerability in full-term births.
titre_fr: Small-for-gestational-age and suspected developmental coordination disorder in preschool children:A national cross-sectional study highlighting vulnerability in full-term births.
auteurs: You Haizhen, Pan Hao, Cai Samuel, Huang Fangfang, Li Huizhen, Zhou Huiyu, Wang Lin, Hua Jing
resume: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) birth has been associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. However, its relationship with suspected developmental coordination disorder (DCD) in preschool children remains unclear. We therefore examined whether SGA was independently associated with suspected DCD risk in a national population-based sample. We analyzed CNCMD data from 101,505 preschool children aged 3-5 years. Birthweight-for-gestational-age status was classified using national sex- and gestational-age-specific standards, and suspected DCD was assessed using the Chinese version of the Little Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire (LDCDQ-CH). Multivariable models adjusted for child, family, and maternal characteristics, with subgroup analyses evaluating potential effect modification. Among 101 505 children, 9 222 (9.1%) were SGA and 7 531 (7.4%) had DCD. SGA was associated with lower LDCDQ-CH scores (β = -0.50, 95% CI -0.69 to -0.32; p < 0.001) and higher odds of DCD (OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.03-1.21; p = 0.008). Associations of SGA with DCD were similar across sex, exclusive breastfeeding, and maternal-education, but were strongest among full-term births (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.15-1.43; p interaction = 0.003). Adjusted risks were 7.35% (95% CI 7.14-7.56) in AGA and 8.11% (7.55-8.67) in SGA, corresponding to an adjusted RD of +0.76 percentage points (0.19-1.33). This translates to 7.6 additional cases per 1000 children. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness. SGA was associated with suspected DCD, with the association most evident among children born at full term. These findings extend understanding of early-life factors associated with preschool motor development beyond prematurity alone.

titre: After the Trip: A Qualitative Study of Healthy Individuals' Motor Experiences Following Different Doses of Psilocybin.
titre_fr: After the Trip: A Qualitative Study of Healthy Individuals' Motor Experiences Following Different Doses of Psilocybin.
auteurs: Luo Ruiqi Rachel, Berlowitz David J, Bryson Alexander, Carter Olivia, Bhagavan Chiranth, Kanaan Richard
resume: Psilocybin is a naturally occurring classic psychedelic associated with widespread changes in brain function and promising therapeutic outcomes in several neuropsychiatric disorders. Complementing these findings, qualitative studies following psilocybin administration have revealed diverse and highly individual effects across multiple domains of subjective experience. However, little is known about its impacts on individuals' subjective motor experiences. With the tendency of individuals to stay stationary during psilocybin's effects, investigating qualitative motor experiences following low-to-moderate doses of psilocybin may offer novel considerations regarding safety and quality of individuals' psychedelic experiences. We aimed to explore healthy individuals' subjective experiences after receiving three different doses of psilocybin and conducting motor activity. Following the study procedure previously published, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 participants who had completed sessions of motor tasks at different doses of psilocybin, which were then transcribed and thematically analyzed. Four major themes were developed, each containing sub-themes: two motor themes, (1) mixed motor messages, including altered motor coordination, control, speed, and reaction time; (2) interacting influences on motor performance, including dose-dependent effects; and two non-motor themes, (3) transcendence, altered consciousness, and transformative "mysticism"; and (4) dynamic and enhanced psychological and sensory experiences. This work contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of psilocybin's multifaceted effects and their relevance to safety, therapeutic potential and future research in motor disorders. The findings will inform a broader dose-finding study and the design of proposed research on psilocybin-assisted physiotherapy for refractory motor functional neurological disorder. ANZCTR number: ACTRN12621000560897.

titre: Translational Toxicology of N-Isopropylbutylone: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Assessment of a New Synthetic Cathinone.
titre_fr: Translational Toxicology of N-Isopropylbutylone: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Assessment of a New Synthetic Cathinone.
auteurs: Bassi Marta, Bilel Sabrine, Corli Giorgia, Cocita Nicole, Masoli Asia, Bernardi Tatiana, Odoardi Sara, Mestria Serena, Biosa Giulia, Strano-Rossi Sabina, Marti Matteo
resume: The novel psychoactive substance (NPS) phenomenon represents a major global problem. Despite the methodical inclusion of new analogues in lists of controlled drugs, new compounds continue to circulate, frequently resulting in fatal intoxications. The emergence of N-isopropyl butylone (NiPB) in 2024, found as an adulterant in methamphetamine-based products, underscores the rapidly evolving landscape of NPSs. Despite its structural similarity to potent monoamine transporter inhibitors, specific pharmacological data and information on its effects in consumers are currently lacking. This study aims to characterize the acute physiological, behavioural, and sensorimotor effects of NiPB (0.1-60 mg/kg; i.p.) in male mice, complemented by in silico pharmacokinetic modelling (ADMET Predictor<sup>®</sup>). NiPB is predicted to undergo N-dealkylation, cleavage of the 3,4-methylendioxy moiety, and N-glucuronidation. Computational profiling predicted high BBB permeability, Vd = 4.37 L/kg, fup > 50%, CYP2D6 and OCT2 inhibition, and hERG blockade (pIC50 = 4.888). In vivo, NiPB induced dose-dependent locomotor stimulation without affecting motor coordination and provoked tachypnoea and visual reflex alterations, while tactile and acoustic responses, as well as thermoregulation, were preserved. In conclusion, this study defines the preliminary toxicological profile of NiPB, indicating that acute exposure may trigger central psychostimulant toxicity in vivo. Furthermore, based on the in silico profiling, targeted experimental studies are required to determine the actual cardiotoxicity and risks of drug-drug interactions associated with NiPB.

This study aims to characterize the acute physiological, behavioural, and sensorimotor effects of NiPB (0.1-60 mg/kg; i.p.) in male mice, complemented by in silico pharmacokinetic modelling (ADMET Predictor<sup>®</sup>). NiPB is predicted to undergo N-dealkylation, cleavage of the 3,4-methylendioxy moiety, and N-glucuronidation. Computational profiling predicted high BBB permeability, Vd = 4.37 L/kg, fup > 50%, CYP2D6 and OCT2 inhibition, and hERG blockade (pIC50 = 4.888). In vivo, NiPB induced dose-dependent locomotor stimulation without affecting motor coordination and provoked tachypnoea and visual reflex alterations, while tactile and acoustic responses, as well as thermoregulation, were preserved. In conclusion, this study defines the preliminary toxicological profile of NiPB, indicating that acute exposure may trigger central psychostimulant toxicity in vivo. Furthermore, based on the in silico profiling, targeted experimental studies are required to determine the actual cardiotoxicity and risks of drug-drug interactions associated with NiPB.

titre: Anxiolytic Potential of Selected Essential Oils and Their Impact on Motor Function.
titre_fr: Anxiolytic Potential of Selected Essential Oils and Their Impact on Motor Function.
auteurs: Sá Filho Alberto Souza, Ogbu John Ihayi, Olusola Ayobami J, Afolabi Saheed Olanrewaju, Pedrino Gustavo Rodrigues, Ferreira-Neto Marcos Luiz, Aprigliano Vicente, do Couto Renê Oliveira, Carvalho Lucas Barbosa Ribeiro de, Borges Leonardo Luiz, da Silva Mirely Vitória Farias, da Silva-Júnior Edeildo Ferreira, Aguiar Antônio Sérgio Nakao de, Fajemiroye James Oluwagbamigbe
resume: Plant essential oils (EOs) exhibit promising anxiolytic activity, but their application may be constrained by adverse motor effects arising from interactions with neural circuits controlling movement. Here, we investigated the anxiolytic-like effects and motor impairment liability of EOs from Pimenta pseudocaryophyllus, Melissa officinalis, Matricaria chamomilla, Lippia alba, Salvia rosmarinus, Ocimum basilicum, Spiranthera odoratissima, and Cymbopogon citratus, integrating computational target prediction with behavioral pharmacology. Prioritized EO constituents were subjected to target prediction, molecular docking, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations to identify molecular mechanisms potentially associated with motor impairment. Male and female Swiss mice received oral vehicle 10 mL/kg, EOs (10, 100, or 500 mg/kg) or diazepam (DZP 1 or 5 mg/kg), followed by the evaluation of anxiolytic-like behavior and motor coordination in the elevated plus maze and rotarod test, respectively. In silico analyses involving docking and molecular dynamics simulations of computationally prioritized EO constituents identified candidate targets within M1 and M2 receptors. All EOs exhibited anxiolytic-like activity at the intermediate dose. Motor impairment varied markedly among EOs. Integrating computational target prediction with behavioral assessment identified distinct motor liability profiles among EOs.

titre: Neurobehavioural outcomes after term IUGR from adolescence to adulthood: a cross-species scoping review.
titre_fr: Neurobehavioural outcomes after term IUGR from adolescence to adulthood: a cross-species scoping review.
auteurs: Chincarini Ginevra, Gilchrist Courtney P, Coyle Meaghan E, Walker David W, Tolcos Mary, Cumberland Angela
resume: Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is associated with long-term neurobehavioural alterations. This scoping review mapped evidence on neurobehavioural outcomes following IUGR in term-born humans and preclinical animal models. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases were searched from January 1985 to February 2025. Clinical studies were included if they assessed motor, cognitive, or anxiety outcomes in adolescents or young adults born at term with IUGR, small for gestational age (SGA), or low birth weight (LBW). Preclinical studies were included if IUGR was induced via placental insufficiency and behavioural outcomes evaluated at equivalent developmental stages. Data were charted and synthesised narratively. Twenty-eight studies (16 clinical, 12 preclinical) were included. Motor and cognitive outcomes were frequently assessed; anxiety-related behaviours were examined in fewer clinical studies despite frequent assessment in preclinical models. Motor coordination and memory outcomes were reported in both human and animal studies, though inconsistent diagnostic criteria and heterogeneous outcome measures limited cross-species comparisons. Most clinical studies classified participants as SGA or LBW; only two applied antenatal criteria to confirm IUGR. This evidence map reveals broad coverage of motor and cognitive domains but limited examination of anxiety outcomes in clinical populations. Standardising diagnostics and aligning behavioural assessments across species are priorities for translational comparability. This review was originally registered in PROSPERO (CRD42020197400) as a systematic review. The protocol has since been adapted to a scoping review framework; the PROSPERO registration reflects the original systematic review methodology, as PROSPERO does not accept scoping review registration. The adapted methodology is described in the Methods section below. Available from: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42020197400 . IMPACT: This is the first scoping review to map both clinical and preclinical evidence on neurobehavioural outcomes following IUGR beyond childhood into adolescence and young adulthood. Motor and cognitive outcomes are widely studied across species, but anxiety domains remain under-examined, particularly in human cohorts. Diagnostic inconsistency (SGA/LBW used as proxies for IUGR) and narrow species representation in preclinical studies are major barriers to translational alignment.

titre: C/EBPβ Drives Ischemia-Induced Microglial Inflammatory Reprogramming Through Transcriptional Activation of ATF3 and Exacerbates Brain Injury.
titre_fr: C/EBPβ Drives Ischemia-Induced Microglial Inflammatory Reprogramming Through Transcriptional Activation of ATF3 and Exacerbates Brain Injury.
auteurs: Zhang Zhongkai, Zhuo Feinan, Ouyang Houqian, Chi Chuang, Zhang Fu, Chi Yiye, Lin Zhongxiao
resume: Microglial activation contributes substantially to secondary brain injury after ischemic stroke, but the transcriptional mechanisms governing this response remain poorly defined. Here, we identified CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ) as a key regulator of ischemia-induced microglial inflammation. RNA sequencing of microglia isolated from mice subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming, characterized by activation of inflammatory pathways, including chemokine, TNF, IL-17, and efferocytosis signaling, as well as cell-cycle programs, together with suppression of homeostatic processes involved in synaptic regulation and neuronal support. Network analysis identified Cebpb as a highly connected hub across multiple inflammatory pathways. C/EBPβ expression was markedly increased in peri-infarct microglia after tMCAO and in primary microglia exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Microglia-selective Cebpb knockdown reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, CCL2, and CD16 expression, increased IL-4, IL-13, and ARG1 expression, and attenuated ischemia-induced morphological remodeling. Consistent effects were observed in primary microglia and BV2 cells, supporting a central role for C/EBPβ in microglial pro-inflammatory activation under ischemic conditions. Mechanistically, C/EBPβ directly bound the Atf3 promoter and activated its transcription, while ATF3 partially mediated C/EBPβ-dependent Il1b induction. In vivo, microglial Cebpb knockdown reduced acute ischemic lesion volume, neuronal apoptosis in the striatum and cortex, and long-term cerebral atrophy. These histopathological improvements were accompanied by sustained recovery of neurological function, somatosensory performance, motor coordination, recognition memory, and spatial learning and memory. Collectively, these findings establish the C/EBPβ-ATF3 axis as a transcriptional pathway that promotes microglial inflammation and secondary neuronal injury after cerebral ischemia. Targeting microglial C/EBPβ may therefore limit ischemic brain damage and improve long-term neurological recovery after stroke.

titre: Temporal dynamics between the whisker sensorimotor cortex and the olivocerebellar module in awake mice.
titre_fr: Temporal dynamics between the whisker sensorimotor cortex and the olivocerebellar module in awake mice.
auteurs: Cheron G, Caballero-Tapia A, Ristori D, Márquez-Ruiz J, Cebolla A M, Ris L
resume: The precise timing of the long-range bidirectional connections between the cerebral cortex and the cerebellum remains a critical factor in elucidating their respective and integrated functions. The key role of the cerebellum in both motor and non-motor domains is exerted through numerous cerebro-cerebellar closed loops that sustain different forms of motor coordination, in which the response timing of the various types of cerebellar neurons may constitute a significant component of neural computation. In this study, we investigated the cerebral sensorimotor cortex and the corresponding cerebellar region (Crus I) of the murine whisker system during electrical stimulation of the whisker pad. In addition, the firing of Golgi cells, Purkinje cells (PC), deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neurons, and inferior olive (IO) neurons was analyzed during electrical stimulation of the whisker pad (Wh), the somatosensory (wS1) and motor (wM1) cortices. We demonstrated that, although peripheral Wh stimulation evoked cortical, cerebellar and IO responses at the same early latency (~3 ms), the transmission within the olivocerebellar circuit was slower when the signal was elicited by wS1 stimulation than by peripheral input, and even slower when wM1 was stimulated. We discussed the different possibilities regarding the transmission of the efference copy and the forward dynamic model within these circuits, and we speculated that the relative slowing of wM1 input into the olivo-cerebellar circuit reflects the increased computational demand associated with the elaboration of the final motor command.

titre: The Factor Structure of the Little Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire and Its Associations with Internalizing and Externalizing Difficulties and Prosocial Behavior in Preschool-Age Children in Italy.
titre_fr: The Factor Structure of the Little Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire and Its Associations with Internalizing and Externalizing Difficulties and Prosocial Behavior in Preschool-Age Children in Italy.
auteurs: Micci Ylenia, Sette Stefania, Caravale Barbara, Di Norcia Anna
resume: Early identification of motor difficulties is crucial, as motor competence represents a foundational developmental skill that supports children's participation in everyday activities and influences broader socio-emotional adjustment. Within this framework, this study examined the factor structure of the Italian version of the Little Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire (LDCDQ-IT) and its associations with socio-emotional functioning. Parents of 429 preschool children (223 boys, 52.0%; 206 girls, 48.0%), aged 33-76 months (M = 48.77, SD = 8.43), in Italy completed the Little Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire (LDCDQ-IT) and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). An Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) suggested one principal factor of motor competence. Then, a Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) confirmed the unidimensional structure of the LDCDQ-IT, with a good model fit. Multigroup confirmatory factor analyses revealed configural, metric, and scalar invariance of the scale between two age groups (33-47 months and 48-76 months). A multivariate regression analysis revealed that higher motor competence was associated with increased prosocial behavior and fewer internalizing and externalizing difficulties. These findings support the unidimensional factor structure of the LDCDQ-IT and highlight the role of motor competence in early socio-emotional development. Overall, the study underscores the value of early screening and the integration of motor and socio-emotional assessment tools in preschool settings.

titre: Purinergic P2X7 Receptor Antagonism Impairs Aerobic Capacity without Detectable Effect on Cardiac Adaptation to Exercise in Mice.
titre_fr: Purinergic P2X7 Receptor Antagonism Impairs Aerobic Capacity without Detectable Effect on Cardiac Adaptation to Exercise in Mice.
auteurs: Santos Naiara de Souza, Fabro Izabel Feltrin, Pinto de Araújo Ana Paula, Dos Santos Beatriz Carminati, Nery Tatyana, Ramos Sávio de Almeida, Guedes da Rosa Izabely, Felipetti Francielly Andressa, Bastos-Pereira Amanda Leite, Aguiar Aderbal S
resume: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) signaling through the P2X7 receptor is an emerging determinant of mitochondrial energy metabolism and physical fitness, and the receptor is increasingly targeted pharmacologically for its role in inflammation. Whether systemic P2X7 antagonism affects aerobic capacity and the structural adaptation of the heart to exercise is unknown. Adult male Swiss mice were studied in a 2 × 2 factorial design crossing physical conditioning (sedentary or exercised) with treatment (saline or the P2X7 antagonist Brilliant Blue G, BBG; 50 mg/kg). Exercised animals trained on a treadmill on alternate days over approximately 4 weeks; maximal oxygen uptake (V̇O<sub>2</sub>max) and power were measured by incremental treadmill ergospirometry, and myocardial cardiomyocyte volume density (Vv) was quantified by design-based stereology. Aerobic training increased V̇O<sub>2</sub>max and cardiomyocyte Vv. BBG reduced V̇O<sub>2</sub>max and peak power independently of training and produced a deficit that widened progressively with workload across the incremental test, indicating a demand-dependent limitation of oxidative performance. Critically, BBG did not detectably alter the exercise-induced increase in cardiomyocyte Vv and showed no interaction with training; motor coordination, locomotor and exploratory behavior, blood lactate, and body mass were also unaffected. P2X7 antagonism thus impairs aerobic capacity without detectable blunting of the structural response of the heart to exercise. This functional-structural dissociation points to a metabolic process, plausibly mitochondrial, rather than to cardiac remodeling, although the present sample size bounds rather than excludes an effect on cardiac adaptation, and indicates that P2X7-directed therapies may reduce exercise capacity without producing overt cardiac structural change.

titre: Screening for medicine and food homologous ingredients targeting ALDH2 to alleviate acute ethanol-induced liver injury.
titre_fr: Screening for medicine and food homologous ingredients targeting ALDH2 to alleviate acute ethanol-induced liver injury.
auteurs: Lu Yuan, Li Zibin, Gao Pan, Liu Yushan, Han Lin, Bian Ji, Wang Min
resume: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health burden with limited therapeutic options. Aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) plays a critical role in alcohol metabolism, and ALDH2 deficiency exacerbates alcohol-induced hepatic injury. This study aimed to identify and validate natural ALDH2 activators from medicine and food homologous sources for alleviating acute ethanol-induced liver injury. A literature-based screening revealed 18 candidate compounds. In vitro enzyme kinetics, molecular docking, and isothermal titration calorimetry were employed to identify four potent ALDH2 activators from these 18 candidates. The hepatoprotective effects of the four candidates were validated in vivo using serum biochemical analyses, oxidative stress measurements, and histopathological examinations in the Gao-binge ALD mouse model. Puerarin, sophoricoside, quercetin, and daidzin were preliminarily identified as mixed-type ALDH2 activators, which increased the acetaldehyde dehydrogenation rate catalyzed by ALDH2. These compounds significantly improved motor coordination, reduced blood ethanol and acetaldehyde levels, attenuated hepatic steatosis, normalized transaminase activities, restored antioxidant capacity, and ameliorated liver histopathological damage in the mouse model. Several natural ALDH2 activators from medicine and food homologous sources with potent hepatoprotective effects were identified, providing the scientific basis for developing healthy foods and dietary supplements to alleviate acute ethanol-induced liver injury.

titre: Motor-cognitive integrated training improves executive function and gross motor skills in children with developmental coordination disorder: a pilot RCT.
titre_fr: Motor-cognitive integrated training improves executive function and gross motor skills in children with developmental coordination disorder: a pilot RCT.
auteurs: Chen Ji-Wei, Ma Guan-Li, Du Wen-Qian, Zhang Xu, Sun Bo, Zhang Bin, Zhu Kun
resume: To evaluate a school-based pilot intervention combining fundamental movement skills (FMS) training and action observation and motor imagery (AOMI) for gross motor skills and executive function in developmental coordination disorder (DCD). In this pilot randomized controlled trial, 20 children with DCD were randomized to an experimental group (FMS plus AOMI, n = 10) or an active control group (FMS plus video-based physical activity education). Both groups completed sessions three times per week for 10 weeks. Gross motor skills were assessed using the Test of Gross Motor Development-3. Executive function was evaluated using the More-Odd Shifting, Stroop, and Spatial Working Memory tasks. Motor skills improved in both groups, with larger gains observed in the experimental group. For executive function, the experimental group showed greater improvements mainly in reaction time and inverse efficiency scores, whereas accuracy improvements were limited and significant only in selected conditions. Compared with FMS combined with video-based physical activity education, FMS combined with AOMI may be associated with additional improvements in motor skills and executive function-related behavioural performance in children with DCD. Given the small pilot sample, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary rather than definitive evidence of efficacy or superiority. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07486856. Children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) commonly present with both motor coordination deficits and executive function difficulties. Existing interventions mainly focus on motor skills, whereas motor-cognitive integrated approaches remain insufficiently tested in school settings. This pilot randomized controlled trial provides preliminary evidence that a school-based programme combining fundamental movement skills training with action observation and motor imagery may be associated with larger improvements than an attention-matched active control condition involving fundamental movement skills training and video-based physical activity education.

titre: Toward early dyslexia screening through handwriting: A trustworthy XAI-enhanced deep learning framework.
titre_fr: Toward early dyslexia screening through handwriting: A trustworthy XAI-enhanced deep learning framework.
auteurs: Matthias Sturm Leo, Lau Justin, Tang Yuk Ming, Geda M W
resume: Dyslexia, a prevalent learning disorder, significantly impairs children's ability to process written language, often leading to challenges such as letter reversals, inconsistent spacing, and scrambled writing sequences. Early detection is critical for timely intervention, yet traditional diagnostic methods such as behavioral assessments and neuroimaging-are either time-consuming, subjective, or prohibitively expensive. Recent advances in deep learning offer promising alternatives, particularly through handwriting analysis, which is non-invasive and scalable. However, the "black-box" nature of many deep learning models raises concerns about interpretability, a key requirement for clinical and educational adoption. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework combining a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), and an Attention mechanism to detect dyslexia from handwriting samples. The study uses handwriting samples from adolescents aged 12-15 with an established dyslexia diagnosis and a control group. It therefore provides a proof-of-concept for handwriting-based classification and a foundation for early screening, rather than a validated early screening tool. The CNN extracts spatial features, while GRUs model temporal patterns in writing sequences. The Attention mechanism highlights the most discriminative regions for screening. To enhance transparency, Explainable AI (XAI) techniques such as Grad-CAM, LIME, and feature scatter plots are added to provide visual explanations of the model's decisions. Evaluated on a dataset of 3170 handwriting images from dyslexic and non-dyslexic students, the model achieved 99.5% accuracy using leave-one-out cross validation, outperforming pre-trained models like ResNet-50. Ablation studies confirmed the CNN's pivotal role while GRUs and Attention provided complementary improvements. These findings demonstrate technical feasibility; however, the model has not yet been evaluated in younger, undiagnosed children, and conclusions about early screening utility should therefore be interpreted with caution. XAI visualizations, such as Grad-CAM and LIME, offer interpretable saliency maps, and the results show that the predictions made by the model depend on the regions where known dyslexic characteristics, such as irregularities in letter curvature, spacing, and alignment, often occur.

The CNN extracts spatial features, while GRUs model temporal patterns in writing sequences. The Attention mechanism highlights the most discriminative regions for screening. To enhance transparency, Explainable AI (XAI) techniques such as Grad-CAM, LIME, and feature scatter plots are added to provide visual explanations of the model's decisions. Evaluated on a dataset of 3170 handwriting images from dyslexic and non-dyslexic students, the model achieved 99.5% accuracy using leave-one-out cross validation, outperforming pre-trained models like ResNet-50. Ablation studies confirmed the CNN's pivotal role while GRUs and Attention provided complementary improvements. These findings demonstrate technical feasibility; however, the model has not yet been evaluated in younger, undiagnosed children, and conclusions about early screening utility should therefore be interpreted with caution. XAI visualizations, such as Grad-CAM and LIME, offer interpretable saliency maps, and the results show that the predictions made by the model depend on the regions where known dyslexic characteristics, such as irregularities in letter curvature, spacing, and alignment, often occur.

titre: Scholarly Writing Development: A Descriptive-Interpretive Study of Nurse Faculty.
titre_fr: Scholarly Writing Development: A Descriptive-Interpretive Study of Nurse Faculty.
auteurs: Elliott Brenda, Frank Nancy J, Gale Anna
resume: The aim of this study was to examine how nurse educators develop as scholarly writers. To broaden the body of knowledge used to inform practice, nurses need to develop scholarly writing skills. However, writing skill acquisition is inconsistent, resulting from wide variation in or absence of deliberate writing development across all levels of nursing education. A descriptive-interpretive design underpinned by naturalistic inquiry using semistructured interviews of nursing faculty (N = 16) was used. Five stages of writing skill acquisition emerged from the data: foundational, beginner, proficient, advanced proficient, and mastery. Nursing students and nurses need intentional practice at all stages of their academic preparation to develop scholarly writing skills. Ongoing professional development is essential to support nurse educators' progressive skill acquisition and, ultimately, continued advancement of nursing science and practice.

titre: Reliability-Guided Dynamic Fusion for Few-Shot Writer-Specific Stroke-Width Estimation in Offline Handwriting Biometric Sensing.
titre_fr: Reliability-Guided Dynamic Fusion for Few-Shot Writer-Specific Stroke-Width Estimation in Offline Handwriting Biometric Sensing.
auteurs: Liu Jihan
resume: Offline handwriting functions as a practical biometric sensing modality for identity verification and controlled stress testing of recognition pipelines, yet recovering writer-specific stroke appearance from only a few enrollment samples remains difficult. In trajectory-based rendering used to probe such sensing systems, stroke width is often fixed or only weakly adapted, so the sensed thickness cue fails to reflect individual writing habits. The key obstacle is an operational reliability imbalance: a learned width estimator and handcrafted geometric priors disagree in trustworthiness across writers and even along a single stroke, which makes a constant fusion rule brittle for few-shot personalization. We propose a confidence-guided dynamic fusion framework whose primary method is a deterministic confidence-to-β map (not a learned gate): point-wise pseudo-label confidence from reference images sets per-point blending weights between learned and rule-based widths, with "reliability" denoting this operational blending prior. On 73 HWDB writers under a strict writer-disjoint protocol with 240 adaptation runs, dynamic fusion reduces writer-level variance and cross-seed instability relative to fixed fusion while retaining competitive point-wise accuracy. A security-oriented sensing analysis further contrasts detector responses under generic versus writer-adapted rendering, showing that the framework can serve as a controllable probe of verification sensitivity. The method plugs into existing trajectory generators and supports reproducible evaluation of personalization fidelity and biometric sensing robustness.

titre: Temporal Processing and Literacy Skills in Children With Hearing Aids.
titre_fr: Temporal Processing and Literacy Skills in Children With Hearing Aids.
auteurs: Güngör Feyza Nur, Meral Çetinkaya Merve
revue: Language, speech, and hearing services in schools
resume: The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between temporal processing and literacy performance in children with hearing aids. The study included a total of 45 children, comprising 21 with typical hearing and 24 who used hearing aids, all of whom were attending the second, third, or fourth grades of primary school. Temporal processing skills were evaluated using the Frequency Pattern Test and the Duration Pattern Test (DPT), whereas reading and writing abilities were assessed through the Literacy Assessment Battery. Children using hearing aids demonstrated statistically significantly lower performance in the DPT and in the test assessing writing skills compared to their typically hearing peers. A positive, significant correlation was found between temporal processing skills and literacy skills. Moreover, temporal processing and literacy performance were observed to be negatively correlated with the age at which the child's first amplification was provided and positively correlated with the duration of auditory rehabilitation. This study found that in children using hearing aids, performance on temporal pattern tests was significantly correlated with reading and writing skills. Furthermore, these findings suggest that early amplification and consistent auditory rehabilitation may be correlated with better temporal processing and literacy skills.

titre: Gait and graphology changes after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: an exploratory pilot study.
titre_fr: Gait and graphology changes after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: an exploratory pilot study.
auteurs: Petrella Gianpaolo, Aureli Lorenzo, De Felice Milena, Gagliano Mariasole, Taddei Graziano, Palmieri Mauro, Kola Martina, Schirinzi Tommaso, Salvati Maurizio, Pompucci Angelo, Pesce Alessandro
revue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
resume: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a potentially reversible neurological syndrome characterized by gait impairment, cognitive decline, and urinary dysfunction. While gait improvement after ventriculoperitoneal shunting (VPS) is well established, postoperative changes in handwriting-related graphomotor function remain poorly investigated. This exploratory pilot study aimed to evaluate whether a multidimensional motor-oriented assessment, including clinical gait scores, instrumental gait analysis, and handwriting-related graphomotor features, may capture postoperative responsiveness after shunting. This single-centre observational pilot study included 14 patients with iNPH who underwent standardized preoperative work-up, including neuroimaging and lumbar infusion testing, followed by ventriculoperitoneal shunting (VPS) placement and longitudinal postoperative reassessment. Clinical evaluation included the Tinetti Performance-Oriented Mobility Assessment and neuropsychological scales such as MMSE, FAB, and MoCA. Instrumented gait analysis assessed spatiotemporal parameters. An exploratory graphological evaluation examined organization, graphomotor movement, cohesion, pressure, dimensions, and alignment on the line. To summarize overall handwriting change, a directional composite score of favourable graphological features was developed. Paired baseline/postoperative comparisons were analysed using non-parametric tests. The most robust postoperative effect was observed in gait-related functional performance. Median Tinetti score improved significantly from 15.0 at baseline to 24.5 at the first postoperative evaluation (p = 0.0088) and remained improved at last follow-up (22.5; p = 0.0137). Instrumental gait parameters showed favourable trends, with reduced gait duration and increased walking velocity, although without statistical significance. No consistent significant changes emerged in neuropsychological scales. Individual graphological domains were mostly stable, but the composite analysis suggested an overall favourable postoperative shift, reaching significance at last follow-up (p = 0.041) and in the exploratory best-postoperative sensitivity analysis (p = 0.025). In this exploratory pilot cohort, ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus was associated with significant improvement in gait-related functional performance and a possible favourable shift in graphomotor features. These preliminary findings suggest that graphomotor assessment may represent a feasible adjunctive exploratory measure of postoperative motor recovery in iNPH. Larger prospective, controlled, and blinded studies are required before graphological parameters can be considered validated outcome measures.
