titre: Appraisals of life transition events and associations with quality of life at 3- and 12-months post-discharge following spinal cord injury.
titre_fr: Appraisals of life transition events and associations with quality of life at 3- and 12-months post-discharge following spinal cord injury.
auteurs: Yi Joyce, Hogan Christy, Brough Rachel, Bray Emily, Mitchell Jessie, Jones Rachel, Kendall Melissa, Amsters Delena, Geraghty Timothy, Ownsworth Tamara
resume: This study examined the occurrence of life transition events during the first 12-months post-discharge after spinal cord injury (SCI) and determined whether appraisals of the impact and coping related to these events were associated with quality of life (QoL). Recruited at discharge, adults with SCI completed telephone-based or online surveys at 3-months (n = 47) and 12-months (n = 39) post-discharge. Participants completed the Sentinel Events Questionnaire regarding the occurrence (Yes/No) of life transitions, including core events (i.e., return-to-work, return to driving, home independence, independence in the community) and other stressors, and rated the positive impact, negative impact, and coping for core events. QoL was measured using the EUROHIS-QoL-8. At 3-months post-discharge, the occurrence of each core event was associated with more positive appraisals of impact (p < 0.01). At 12-months, return-to-work and driving were more positively appraised than resuming home or community independence (p < 0.05). Across events, coping appraisals were consistently and positively associated with QoL, after controlling for event occurrence (sr2 = 8-22%, p < 0.05). The finding that more positive appraisals of impact and coping regarding core events are associated with better QoL highlights the importance of understanding the subjective meaning of life transition events to inform person-centred interventions.

titre: Upper extremity motor outcomes during paired vagus nerve stimulation in chronic ischemic stroke: a retrospective single-health-system cohort study.
titre_fr: Upper extremity motor outcomes during paired vagus nerve stimulation in chronic ischemic stroke: a retrospective single-health-system cohort study.
auteurs: Benitez Ronald, Darling Michelle, Zaorski Paige, Galligan Quinn, Maurer Jack, McNamara Nicole, Doherty Shannon J
resume: Persistent upper extremity (UE) impairment after stroke is a major cause of long-term disability, and treatment options in the chronic phase are limited. In randomized trials, vagus nerve stimulation paired with task-specific rehabilitation (Paired VNS) produced greater improvement in UE function and activity than the same rehabilitation with sham stimulation, leading to FDA approval in 2021. We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of adults with chronic stroke and persistent UE deficits who underwent Vivistim implantation and participated in a Paired VNS program delivered across 5 outpatient clinics within our health system. The primary outcome was change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) from baseline (Paired VNS therapy initiation) to end of the intended Paired VNS therapy protocol (18 sessions). A ≥6-point improvement defined a clinically meaningful response. Adverse events were a secondary safety outcome, ascertained from routine clinical documentation and not systematically collected beyond early postoperative follow-up. 32 patients underwent device implantation; 28 (88%) completed the intended protocol within the health system and had paired FMA-UE assessments available for the primary analysis. Ages ranged from 34 to 81 years (mean 62.1) and the median time since stroke was 3.0 years (IQR 1.7-4.2). FMA-UE scores improved for all 28 local completers. The mean increase of 9.43 points was statistically significant (95% CI 7.20-11.66; p < 0.001), the median increase was 8.0 points (IQR 5.0-13.25) and 20 patients (71.4%; 95% CI 52.9-84.7%) achieved a clinically meaningful response. Chart-derived clinical notes provided illustrative context regarding individual changes in daily activities that accompanied UE motor improvement in selected cases. Among the 32 implanted patients, one postoperative hematoma resolved without intervention and one device was explanted after 410 days due to chest tingling. In this retrospective single-health-system cohort, Paired VNS was associated with significant improvement in FMA-UE scores among 28 local completers. The findings are directionally consistent with prior trial evidence.

titre: Case Report: Flossing intervention for chronic upper limb spasticity after childhood-onset stroke.
titre_fr: Case Report: Flossing intervention for chronic upper limb spasticity after childhood-onset stroke.
auteurs: Sasaki Shuichi, Takahira Naonobu, Ono Yuzo, Aoki Keiichiro, Kurosaki Sora, Moteki Marina, Fujita Risa, Kenmoku Tomonori
resume: Upper limb spastic paralysis after stroke often limits functional use of the affected hand and restricts activities of daily living, particularly in cases with long-standing impairment following childhood-onset stroke. Although various interventions for spasticity have been reported, many require specialized equipment or invasive procedures, which may limit long-term and home-based use. Flossing intervention, which involves compressive wrapping with an elastic band combined with movement, has recently been introduced in musculoskeletal practice; however, its application for post-stroke spasticity remains unclear. An adolescent girl in her teens (female, Asian) presented with long-standing right upper limb spastic paralysis following childhood-onset cerebral infarction associated with moyamoya disease. At baseline, she demonstrated marked distal spasticity, limited active wrist extension, and restricted functional use of the affected hand. A flossing intervention was applied to the distal forearm and elbow region, consisting of compressive wrapping followed by passive twisting and active movements. The intervention was performed both in outpatient therapy and as a home-based program. After 6 months of continuous intervention, Modified Ashworth Scale scores decreased, upper limb motor function assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment improved, and real-world use of the affected hand assessed using the Motor Activity Log increased. Active wrist extension range of motion improved from -20° to 40°, and functional bilateral hand use, including button fastening, became possible. The patient reported improved ease of hand movement and high satisfaction, and functional gains were maintained during follow-up. This case suggests that flossing intervention may be a feasible, non-invasive, and home-based treatment option for improving upper limb function in patients with long-standing post-stroke spastic paralysis following childhood-onset stroke. Further studies are required to clarify its efficacy and appropriate indications.

titre: Home-based geriatric rehabilitation after shortened inpatient rehabilitation: cost-effectiveness analysis of the "Better@Home" multicentre prospective cohort study with a matched historical control group.
titre_fr: Home-based geriatric rehabilitation after shortened inpatient rehabilitation: cost-effectiveness analysis of the "Better@Home" multicentre prospective cohort study with a matched historical control group.
auteurs: Gamble C J, Groen W G, de Waal M W M, Pol M C, Vanvan DamIsselt E F, Hiligsmann M, Gabrio A, Zwakhalen S M G, van Haastregt J C M
revue: The European journal of health economics : HEPAC : health economics in prevention and care
resume: Geriatric rehabilitation (GR) is facing increased demand due to population ageing. Home-based GR could reduce reliance on resource-intensive inpatient care. However, evidence is limited regarding the cost-effectiveness of home-based GR. The aim of this study is to assess the cost-effectiveness of home-based GR following shortened inpatient GR, compared to conventional inpatient GR. Eight GR facilities in the Netherlands implemented the Better@Home program, in which home-based GR following shortened inpatient GR is compared to a historical control group receiving conventional inpatient GR. The effect measure was independence in activities of daily living (ADL), assessed by the Barthel Index (BI). Costs were measured as healthcare and societal resource use. Data was gathered at GR-admission- and GR-discharge through semi-structured interviews, registration forms, and electronic patient files. Costs and effects were analyzed using linear mixed effects (LMM) and generalised linear (GLM) regression models, combined with multiple imputation and non-parametric bootstrapping. The primary analysis was conducted from a healthcare perspective valued using national unit sources. A total of 350 participants were included (intervention n = 110; control n = 240). The adjusted incremental effect was 0.44 BI-points (95% CI - 0.44 to 1.31), and incremental costs of - €722,63 (95% CI - €2.693,68 to €1.248,43). Uncertainty assessments using non-parametric bootstrapping demonstrated an average mean incremental effect of 0.44 BI-points (95% CI 0.27 to 0.61) and incremental costs of - €654,72 (95% CI - €1.035,66 to - €267,48), indicating a probabilistic pattern favouring the Better@Home program. The Better@Home program achieved levels of independence in ADL comparable to conventional inpatient GR while showing lower mean costs, suggesting that the program may be cost-effective.

titre: Efficacy of personalized yoga rehabilitation on quality of life in survivors of extensive burns: A pilot matched case-control study.
titre_fr: Efficacy of personalized yoga rehabilitation on quality of life in survivors of extensive burns: A pilot matched case-control study.
auteurs: Wang Yiran, Mao Shulei, Liu Jia, Jiang Jing, Wu Junmei, Yang Shiyun, Wang Rongjuan, Zhang Yuanhai, Han Chunmao, Wang Xingang, Zhang Jianfen
revue: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
resume: Extensive burn survivors often face severe joint dysfunction, hypertrophic scarring, and psychological trauma, which seriously compromise their quality of life. This pilot study evaluated outcomes associated with adding a personalized, phased yoga rehabilitation program to standard rehabilitation care. This study enrolled survivors of extensive burns (TBSA ≥ 50%) who received rehabilitation at our institution between January 2022 and June 2025. Participants were categorized into a "Yoga Group" or a "Standard Care Group" based on whether they received yoga rehabilitation. Outcomes included joint range of motion (ROM), Barthel Index (BI), Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), PTSD Checklist-Civilian Version (PCL-C), and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Within-group improvements were analyzed for the Yoga Group. For inter-group comparison, 1:1 case-control matching was performed based on Cutaneous Functional Unit (CFU) scores and time post-injury. A total of 64 patients were included (Yoga: 13; Standard Care: 51). In addition to standard rehabilitation, the Yoga Group received a median of 6.0 months (IQR: 5.5-9.0) of the personalized yoga rehabilitation program. Post-yoga, significant within-group improvements were observed in major joint ROM (shoulder flexion: 101.25° ± 58.35° vs. 149.17° ± 26.10°, P = 0.009; hip flexion: 73.33° ± 37.44° vs. 110.83° ± 23.14°, P = 0.011), scar condition (POSAS score: 80 ± 20 vs. 55 ± 14, P < 0.001), activities of daily living (Barthel Index: 35 [25, 40] vs. 95 [90, 100]), balance function (BBS: 1 [0, 21] vs. 56 [56, 56], P < 0.001), and mental health status. After case-control matching, the Yoga Group demonstrated significantly superior scar recovery compared to the Standard Care Group (POSAS score: 57 [54.5, 58.5] vs. 71 [64.5, 85.5], P = 0.021), as well as significantly lower BDI-II scores (8 [3.5, 11.5] vs. 16 [13, 19], P = 0.015) and higher BBS scores (56 [56, 56] vs. 56 [44.5, 56], P = 0.095). In this pilot study, participation in a personalized, phased yoga rehabilitation program was associated with better scar quality and fewer depressive symptoms in matched comparisons. The program may provide a feasible adjunct to standard rehabilitation by addressing both the physical and psychological dimensions of recovery.

titre: Thirty-Five Years of Change: Shifts in Demographic and Injury Profiles of Traumatic Brain Injury Cases Enrolled in the Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems (1988-2024): A NIDILRR TBIMS National Database Study.
titre_fr: Thirty-Five Years of Change: Shifts in Demographic and Injury Profiles of Traumatic Brain Injury Cases Enrolled in the Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems (1988-2024): A NIDILRR TBIMS National Database Study.
auteurs: Ketchum Jessica M, Tefertiller Candace, Beaulieu Cynthia L, Bodien Yelena G, Callender Librada, Dams-O'Connor Kristen, Giacino Joseph T, Hammond Flora M, Hanks Robin, Ivanhoe Cindy B, Pinto Shanti M, Zhang Jenny J
revue: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
resume: To characterize long-term changes in demographic and injury profiles among individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI) admitted to inpatient rehabilitation and enrolled in the TBI Model Systems (TBIMS) National Database (NDB). Twenty-three inpatient rehabilitation hospitals participating in the TBIMS program. 20 990 persons 16 years and older with TBI who received inpatient rehabilitation and enrolled in the TBIMS NDB between 1988 and 2024. Repeated cross-sectional analysis of a prospectively collected longitudinal database across 7 admission cohorts. Sociodemographic characteristics (age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, employment, marital status, payor source) and injury characteristics (etiology, Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS], command following, post-traumatic amnesia [PTA], Functional Independence Measure [FIM], acute and rehabilitation length of stay [LOS]). Mean age at injury increased from 34.6 years in 1988-1994 to 48.4 in 2020-2024, accompanied by a rise in fall-related injuries, a decline in violence-related injuries, and a shift in vehicular injuries from earlier increases to more recent declines. The proportion of participants who were retired increased substantially, while the proportion who were unemployed declined. Racial/ethnic minority representation declined from 1988-1994 to 2000-2004 and then increased through 2020-2024, particularly among younger individuals. Medicare coverage increased while Medicaid coverage declined. The proportion of participants with complicated mild TBI increased while moderate and severe classifications declined, accompanied by shorter time to command following and PTA duration. Despite these indicators of decreasing injury severity, FIM motor scores at rehabilitation admission declined modestly. Acute LOS declined slightly while rehabilitation LOS declined substantially. Over the past 35 years, the TBIMS population has shifted toward an older cohort, accompanied by changes in demographic patterns associated with aging, mechanisms of injury, functional profiles, payor source, and lengths of stay. These changes should be considered when interpreting TBIMS longitudinal outcomes, evaluating representativeness, translating prior research findings to contemporary populations, and planning rehabilitation services for individuals with TBI.

titre: Medication Burden and Its Escalation Predict Incidence of Hospital-associated Disability in Older Inpatients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
titre_fr: Medication Burden and Its Escalation Predict Incidence of Hospital-associated Disability in Older Inpatients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
auteurs: Kose Eiji, Wakabayashi Hidetaka, Nishioka Shinta, Nagai Takako, Hashida Nao, Momosaki Ryo
resume: Whether medication burden contributes to hospital-associated disability (HAD) in older inpatients remains unclear. We investigated the relationship between medication count and HAD incidence to identify potential pharmacotherapy targets. This multicenter prospective cohort study used data from a HAD registry collected from 1 February 2023 to 31 March 2025. Eligible patients were aged 70 years or older, admitted to medical wards, received rehabilitation, had hospital stays of 48 h or longer, and were independent in activities of daily living at admission (Katz Index of 6). HAD was defined as a Katz Index less than 6 at discharge. The primary outcome was medication count at admission; the secondary outcome was change in medication count during hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression models with varying covariate adjustment assessed whether admission medication count and in-hospital change were independently associated with HAD. Among the 206 patients (mean age 80.3 years; 60.7% men), 60 (29.1%) developed HAD. Across the models, the medication counts on admission independently increased the HAD risk [odds ratio (OR), 1.14; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.28]. Increased medication count during hospitalization was also associated with HAD development (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.01-1.45), reaching significance in most models. Subgroup analyses showed that a medication count on admission of at least five or at least six increased the HAD risk (OR, 1.89 and 1.93, respectively). Both admission medication count and increase in the in-hospital medication count were associated with HAD development. To prevent HAD development, medication regimens should be optimized, including efforts to reduce unnecessary polypharmacy.

titre: Immediate Weight-Bearing and Early Ambulation Rehabilitation After Femoral Neck System Fixation for Undisplaced Femoral Neck Fractures: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Immediate Weight-Bearing and Early Ambulation Rehabilitation After Femoral Neck System Fixation for Undisplaced Femoral Neck Fractures: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Li Chuanping, Yan Shanzhong, Yu Fan, Pan Huajie, Yin Gang, Yu Bo
resume: Internal fixation is the usual treatment for undisplaced intracapsular hip fractures (Garden I and II). This study aimed to determine the optimal rehabilitation protocol for patients undergoing femoral neck system (FNS) fixation. A prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted involving 58 patients who underwent FNS fixation for femoral neck fractures (FNFs) during a 10-month period from September 2023 to June 2024. They were randomly assigned to two groups: an immediate weight-bearing and early ambulation (IWBEA) group (within 48 h) and a delayed weight-bearing and ambulation (DWBA) group (after 6 weeks). Outcomes included time of hospitalization, fracture healing time, in-hospital complications, functional performance, pain severity, and activities of daily living. The IWBEA group showed a shorter time of hospitalization [median 6.0 (IQR 5.0-7.0) days vs. 7.0 (IQR 6.5-13.5) days, P = 0.002], a lesser fracture healing time [median 11.0 (IQR 10.0-12.5) weeks vs. 12.0 (IQR 11.0-13.0) weeks, P = 0.040], and a lower rate of in-hospital complications (6.9% vs. 27.6%, P = 0.037). At 12-month follow-up, activities of daily living [median 100.0 (IQR 95.0-100.0), P = 0.350], functional performance [median 12.0 (IQR 11.0-12.0), P = 0.289], pain severity [median 1.0 (IQR 0.0-2.0), P = 0.765], and Avascular Necrosis (AVN) incidence (χ 2 = 1.673, P = 0.196) were comparable between groups. The IWBEA rehabilitation protocol can reduce time of hospitalization, fracture healing time, and incidence of in-hospital complications. In undisplaced intracapsular hip fractures treated with FNS, an IWBEA should be preferred. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500099199).

titre: Methodological quality and clinical applicability of long COVID guidelines and scientific statements: a systematic review using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
titre_fr: Methodological quality and clinical applicability of long COVID guidelines and scientific statements: a systematic review using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
auteurs: Montoya Monsalve Ricardo, Campuzano Cortina Sofía, Jiménez Cárdenas Manuela
resume: Long COVID is projected to affect 0.6 to 1.0% of the population between 2025 and 2030. This study reviewed the methodological quality, clinical applicability and content of the care recommendations issued for adults ≥18 years with long COVID in clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) and scientific statements (SSs). Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261324906). PubMed, Scopus, trip, five guideline repositories and national health portals were searched between February and April 2026, and PubMed and Scopus were updated on 2 September 2026. Eligible documents were CPGs and SSs on adults with suspected or confirmed long COVID, published in English or Spanish. Screening and full-text review were duplicated independently; data were extracted by one reviewer and verified by a second. Methodological quality was appraised with AGREE II, reporting the six standardised domain scores separately, each rescaled within its domain and never summed into an overall score; applicability was appraised with AGREE-REX. A narrative synthesis covered five predefined care domains. Twenty documents were appraised, 19 from the initial search and one from the update. From the 19 initial documents, 510 recommendations were extracted across five NICE-derived domains, mostly clinical management (63.3%) and care planning (29.6%). Quality was uneven (rigor of development 16.7-97.9%; applicability 0.0-95.8%; editorial Independence median 100%), and only one document reported a GRADE-compatible evidence-to-decision framework. Four documents were prioritised and contributed 99 recommendations; they scored higher than the remaining corpus in all six domains, yet applicability remained their weakest (68%). AGREE-REX showed recommendations directed far more clearly at clinicians than at patients or decision-makers. Content converged on shared decision-making, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, patient-centered care and return-to-work support. Guidance on long COVID is abundant but methodologically uneven, and the unevenness is concentrated in how evidence is linked to recommendations and in applicability. The corpus offers well-formulated clinical content whose evidence-to-decision reasoning and implementation requirements are seldom reported, and it therefore requires formal contextual adaptation, for example through GRADE-ADOLOPMENT, before use. Key limitations are the scarcity of guidance from low- and middle-income countries and the diversity of development methods. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261324906, Identifier CRD420261324906.
resume_fr: Long COVID is projected to affect 0.6 to 1.0% of the population between 2025 and 2030. titre: Network analysis of kinesiophobia and fear of progression and their association with cardiac rehabilitation adherence in post-CABG patients.
titre_fr: Network analysis of kinesiophobia and fear of progression and their association with cardiac rehabilitation adherence in post-CABG patients.
auteurs: Luo Zhengwei, Chen Fenghui, Li Huihui, Wang Weilong, Chen Duohuan, Zhu Wen, Xing Juan, Liang Fang, Tao Jianshuang
resume: Coronary heart disease is the major disease burden of cardiovascular diseases in China, and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is the preferred surgical procedure for complex coronary artery lesions. Postoperative cardiac rehabilitation can improve patient outcomes; however, kinesiophobia and fear of progression are associated with lower adherence to rehabilitation. This study aimed to identify core symptoms within the fear network, explore hypothesized directional relationships among symptoms, and analyze the associations between the two types of fear symptoms and adherence to cardiac rehabilitation. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 294 patients who underwent their first CABG at three tertiary hospitals in Urumqi, Xinjiang, between October 2025 and February 2026. Participants were assessed using the scale of adherence to cardiac rehabilitation, the scale to measure fear of activity in patients with coronary artery disease, and the fear of progression questionnaire-short form. R software was employed to construct the symptom network. Bayesian network analysis was used to construct a directed acyclic graph, and flow network analysis was applied to examine the associations between symptoms and cardiac rehabilitation adherence. In the symptom network, "My body does not allow me to do certain activities even though I would like to," "Being afraid of no longer being able to pursue hobbies," and "Being afraid of relying on strangers for activities of daily living" were identified as central symptoms, while "Being afraid of pain" and "Having physical symptoms, e.g., rapid heartbeat, stomachache, nervousness" served as bridge symptoms. In the Bayesian network, "Being afraid of no longer being able to pursue hobbies" was located at the apex of the network. In the flow network, a total of 19 symptoms showed negative associations with cardiac rehabilitation adherence, among which "Being afraid of pain," "I am afraid of any physical activity since I learned my heart problem," and "My body does not allow me to do certain activities even though I would like to" exhibited strong negative correlations. The network comparison test revealed no statistically significant differences in global strength or network structure between the middle-aged and elderly groups. Network analysis successfully identified the central and bridge symptoms in the kinesiophobia and fear of progression network among post-CABG patients, revealed the hypothesized directional relationships among symptoms, and identified the symptoms closely associated with cardiac rehabilitation adherence. These findings provide reference clues for postoperative symptom assessment and the subsequent development of personalized interventions.

titre: Phenotypic diversity and morphometric differentiation of indigenous chickens in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
titre_fr: Phenotypic diversity and morphometric differentiation of indigenous chickens in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
auteurs: Vilakazi Bongiwe Nontobeko, Ncobela Cyprial Ndumiso, Kunene Nokuthula Winfred
resume: Morphological variation among indigenous chickens reflects both adaptive divergence and underlying genetic structure; however, such information remains limited for KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. This study evaluated phenotypic differentiation among indigenous chicken populations sampled from seven communal areas: Cedara, Jozini, Ladysmith, Empangeni, Newcastle, Pietermaritzburg, and Port Shepstone. A total of 350 adult birds were characterised using six qualitative traits and eight quantitative morphometric measurements. Canonical discriminant analysis was employed to assess population differentiation. Substantial variation was observed in plumage, skin, shank, and comb characteristics, with golden-laced plumage and yellow skin predominating across most locations. Quantitative traits differed significantly among populations (p < 0.001), with body weight (Wilks' Λ = 0.813; F = 13.082) contributing most strongly to population discrimination. Mahalanobis distance analysis revealed pronounced separation between Jozini and Empangeni populations (D² = 53.23; p < 0.001), while Newcastle and Port Shepstone exhibited minimal divergence (D² = 3.58; p < 0.001). Hierarchical cluster analysis identified two primary population groupings, with Jozini forming a distinct outlier. The apparent classification accuracy based on the original grouped cases was 51.1%, suggesting considerable overlap in morphometric characteristics among populations. These findings demonstrate appreciable phenotypic diversity among indigenous chickens in KwaZulu-Natal, likely shaped by environmental adaptation and management practices. The observed variation represents a valuable genetic resource for community-based breeding and conservation programmes aimed at improving productivity while maintaining adaptive resilience.

titre: Proteomic adaptation of the hypervirulent pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus ST36 lineage to salinity and temperature stress.
titre_fr: Proteomic adaptation of the hypervirulent pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus ST36 lineage to salinity and temperature stress.
auteurs: González-Vidal Eloisa, Eslava-Alcón Sara, Jurado-Tarifa Estefanía, Guerrero-Lozano Inmaculada, Durán-Ruiz MaCarmen, Rodriguez-Iglesias Manuel A
resume: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a halophilic Gram-negative bacterium widely distributed in marine and estuarine ecosystems, and a leading cause of seafood-borne gastroenteritis worldwide. Among its genetic lineages, sequence type 36 (ST36) has emerged as a pandemic clone with remarkable environmental persistence and global dissemination. Its pathogenicity is closely associated with environmental conditions, particularly salinity and temperature, which modulate the expression of virulence factors, stress-response proteins, and metabolic pathways. In this study, we investigated the differential protein expression profiles of Vibrio parahaemolyticus under controlled salinity (1 and 3%) and temperature (20 °C, 31 °C, and 37 °C) using a label free-quantitative (LFQ) proteomic approach. Our results demonstrate that the Vibrio parahaemolyticus proteome is dynamically and non-linearly modulated by specific combinations of salt and heat rather than a simple additive effect of these factors. Temperature-salinity interactions drove most expression changes (2,144 proteins), with temperature acting as the primary driver (1,302 proteins). Proteome changes peaked mostly at 31 °C for salinity variations and at 3% salinity for temperature shifts, each affecting ~80% of proteins, though specific responses ultimately depended on the nature of individual proteins. Functionally, protein changes were representative of a shift from relatively balanced cellular metabolism at mild stress conditions toward respiratory remodeling, central-carbon reorganization, ATP production, and redox defense under elevated salinity and temperature. Additionally, virulence-, toxin-, motility-, chemotaxis-, and defense-associated proteins were distributed across several trend clusters. Overall, the proteomic patterns detected in Vibrio parahaemolyticus in response to temperature and salinity fluctuations reveal a coordinated regulation of virulence, stress-response, and metabolic proteins that underpins its ecological fitness. Beyond these biological insights, the proteomic workflow employed provides a robust methodological framework for studying bacterial stress adaptation. Ultimately, these findings deepen our understanding of the pathogen dynamics under climate change and for improving seafood safety and risk management. Future research is warranted to experimentally validate the molecular pathways identified and confirm their functional roles in adaptation.

titre: Plant compartment and understory habitat jointly shape endophytic bacterial communities in Monochasma savatieri.
titre_fr: Plant compartment and understory habitat jointly shape endophytic bacterial communities in Monochasma savatieri.
auteurs: Zou Yuling, Li Fengqing, Liu Suzhen, Lan Wendi, Zeng Mansheng, Luo Guisheng, Huang Wei, Shen Lili, Zhang Baolian, Sang Shutong
resume: Monochasma savatieri is a rare medicinal plant endemic to China that currently faces extinction, with wild-simulated understory cultivation representing a key conservation strategy. Endophytic bacteria play important roles in nutrient acquisition and environmental adaptation of hemiparasitic plants; however, how the understory environments influence above- and belowground endophytic bacterial communities remains poorly understood. We collected soil and plant tissue samples from four contrasting understory habitats (Pinus massoniana, Camellia oleifera, Phyllostachys edulis, and Gardenia jasminoides). The endophytic bacterial communities were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The soil physicochemical properties were measured to identify environmental drivers. Multivariate statistics, including permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA), redundancy analysis (RDA), and Mantel tests, were applied to link the community variation with environmental factors. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed that the type of plant tissue, habitat, and their interaction (all p < 0.001) significantly shaped the endophytic community structure. Belowground tissues generally harbored higher diversity than aboveground tissues, although this pattern was habitat-dependent. Each habitat enriched distinct bacterial genera. Functional predictions showed a complementary pattern: aboveground communities were enriched in sensing-related pathways, whereas belowground communities showed higher abundances of degradation-associated pathways. RDA identified the soil total and available potassium as strong environmental correlates of community differentiation. The findings of this study demonstrate that plant compartment and understory habitat jointly shape endophytic bacterial communities in M. savatieri, with potassium availability as a key correlate. However, because each habitat was represented by a single geographic site, the vegetation type is confounded with the location, climate, and soil properties; therefore, our inferences are correlative rather than causal. Within these constraints, the findings help identify candidate taxa and environmental associations that provide testable hypotheses for future cultivation and microecological research on this rare medicinal plant.

titre: Environmental adaptation in wheat landraces: integrating physiological, molecular, and ecological mechanisms for climate-resilient agriculture.
titre_fr: Environmental adaptation in wheat landraces: integrating physiological, molecular, and ecological mechanisms for climate-resilient agriculture.
auteurs: Francis Dali Vilma, Kishorkumar Malu, Abdulla Tarfa, Jaleel Abdul, Alsafar Habiba, Al Dhaheri Ayesha, Kurup Shyam S
resume: Climate change poses an increasing threat to wheat production, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions where rising temperatures, water scarcity, soil degradation, and salinity interact to reduce crop productivity and stability. Wheat landraces constitute an invaluable reservoir of adaptive genetic diversity that has evolved through centuries of natural and farmer-mediated selection under resource-limited environments. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the mechanisms underlying environmental resilience in wheat landraces, integrating evidence across physiological, biochemical, hormonal, molecular, ecological, and agronomic scales within a single framework. It examines how coordinated adaptive strategies-including stress escape, avoidance, tolerance, and recovery-interact with root system architecture, rhizosphere processes, plant-microbe associations, and resource-use efficiency to enhance resilience under multiple abiotic stresses. Recent advances in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, pangenomics, and multi-omics integration have substantially improved our understanding of the genetic and molecular basis of environmental adaptation, creating new opportunities for the identification and deployment of resilience-associated traits. The review further discusses how these discoveries are being translated into climate-smart wheat improvement through genome-wide association studies, marker-assisted and genomic selection, speed breeding, gene editing, and artificial intelligence-assisted phenotyping. In addition, sustainable agronomic management, conservation strategies, farmer participation, and policy frameworks are considered as complementary components supporting the effective utilization of wheat landraces. By integrating adaptive biology, modern breeding technologies, sustainable agronomy, and socio-economic perspectives, this review presents a comprehensive framework for conserving and utilizing wheat landrace diversity to accelerate the development of climate-resilient wheat cultivars and strengthen global food and nutritional security under increasingly unpredictable climatic conditions.

titre: Epidemiology of visual impairment and rehabilitation measures in adults-Data from the Swedish Quality Registry for Rehabilitation in Visual Impairment.
titre_fr: Epidemiology of visual impairment and rehabilitation measures in adults-Data from the Swedish Quality Registry for Rehabilitation in Visual Impairment.
auteurs: Kjellström Ulrika, Tornqvist Kristina, Baudin Katarina, Regardt Malin, Schroeder Marion
resume: To describe the Swedish Quality Registry for Rehabilitation in Visual Impairment (SKRS) and present rehabilitation measures and underlying diagnoses of visual impairment and blindness in adults in Sweden. The study includes data from the SKRS collected between January 2016 and December 2025 for patients aged ≥20 years who received rehabilitation services from low vision centres in Sweden. The degree and underlying causes of visual impairment, as well as rehabilitation interventions, were analysed. In 2025, SKRS recorded 12 622 registrations for 11 810 unique patients, with women accounting for 62%. The median waiting time from referral to first visit was 37 days. Most patients had a moderate visual impairment. In 2025, age-related macular degeneration (AMD) represented the most common diagnosis (50.2%), followed by glaucoma (18.3%), blindness of unspecified cause/visual impairment (5.9%), retinal diseases (5%), diabetic retinopathy (2.8%) and optic nerve diseases (2.2%). The most frequently registered procedure codes were in the group of assistive technology with 30.3%, followed by investigative procedures with 26.1% and follow-up with 19.9%. The proportion of International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health based instruments had increased significantly; from 0.04% in 2016 to 72.5% in 2025. The proportion of individual rehabilitation plans had risen by 18.6% since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic-from 53.2% in 2020 to 71.8% in 2025. SKRS provides representative data on rehabilitation measures and associated diagnoses among adults with visual impairments in Sweden. The data confirm that AMD and glaucoma are the most common causes and highlight inequalities in access to visual rehabilitation.

titre: Tracing the Evolutionary Origins of Jasmonate Signaling: Co-Evolution of Oxylipin Metabolism and Hormone Perception in the Green Lineage.
titre_fr: Tracing the Evolutionary Origins of Jasmonate Signaling: Co-Evolution of Oxylipin Metabolism and Hormone Perception in the Green Lineage.
auteurs: Chini Andrea, Jimenez-Aleman Guillermo H, Solano Roberto
resume: Jasmonates constitute a central class of lipid-derived signaling molecules that regulate plant defense, development, and environmental adaptation. Although jasmonic acid (JA) and its bioactive conjugate jasmonoyl-L-isoleucine (JA-Ile) are well characterized in angiosperms, recent evolutionary, biochemical, and structural studies have revealed that jasmonate signaling predates the origin of land plants. Jasmonates occur in streptophyte algae but are absent from chlorophytes, indicating that jasmonate biosynthesis evolved in the last common ancestor of streptophytes. However, the molecular nature, perception mechanisms, and biological functions of jasmonates have undergone profound changes during plant evolution. During terrestrialization, the recruitment of a pre-existing transcriptional regulatory network by a newly evolved COI1 receptor module established the canonical COI1/JAZ signaling system. Early diverging land plants employed dn-OPDA, a JA precursor, as the ancestral ligand, which was progressively replaced by JA amino acid conjugates such as JA-Ile in vascular plants. Here, we synthesize current evidence supporting a stepwise evolutionary model progressively shaping the COI1/JAZ-dependent hormone pathway. We discuss how (bio)chemical diversification of oxylipins, co-evolution of receptors and ligands, and the emergence of JA-Ile in vascular plants enabled the expansion, specificity, and systemic integration of jasmonate signaling as a requirement for plant terrestrialization.

titre: Design and assessment of the feasibility of a diagnostic and rehabilitation device for gait re-education.
titre_fr: Design and assessment of the feasibility of a diagnostic and rehabilitation device for gait re-education.
auteurs: Drużbicki Mariusz, Kordos Adrian, Kordos Damian, Guzik Agnieszka
resume: Gait after a stroke is characterized by a number of abnormalities, such as reduced walking speed, impaired stability, as well as asymmetry. This study presents a novel assistive device designed to aid gait training in stroke survivors by providing integrated visual, auditory, and tactile stimuli informing about lower limb weight-bearing and step length symmetry. Nine patients with hemiparesis at an early stage post-stroke were included in the study. A markerless 3D system was applied to assess gait. Participants walked at self-selected pace and were wearing their own orthotic devices. Gait speed, step length, gait phase duration, and cadence were measured. A symmetry index was calculated for step length and lower limb weight-bearing. The program consisted of ten gait training sessions with the assistive device, each session taking 30 min. Improved gait parameters were observed when acoustic and visual prompting was applied alone or in combination with tactile prompting. At the end of the program, decrease in step length asymmetry was observed and there was no statistically significant difference in the mean step length between the paretic and non-paretic lower limb (p = 0.002). An improvement was shown in the distribution of lower limb weight-bearing in a standing position, and the mean value of limb weight-bearing symmetry index was significantly lower compared to the baseline (p = 0.0001). Integrated tactile, auditory, and visual prompting may beneficially affect post-stroke gait rehabilitation, by inducing improvements in gait pattern, symmetry, body balance, and walking speed.

Participants walked at self-selected pace and were wearing their own orthotic devices. Gait speed, step length, gait phase duration, and cadence were measured. A symmetry index was calculated for step length and lower limb weight-bearing. The program consisted of ten gait training sessions with the assistive device, each session taking 30 min. Improved gait parameters were observed when acoustic and visual prompting was applied alone or in combination with tactile prompting. At the end of the program, decrease in step length asymmetry was observed and there was no statistically significant difference in the mean step length between the paretic and non-paretic lower limb (p = 0.002). An improvement was shown in the distribution of lower limb weight-bearing in a standing position, and the mean value of limb weight-bearing symmetry index was significantly lower compared to the baseline (p = 0.0001). Integrated tactile, auditory, and visual prompting may beneficially affect post-stroke gait rehabilitation, by inducing improvements in gait pattern, symmetry, body balance, and walking speed.

titre: An accessible pregnancy test for blind and low-vision users.
titre_fr: An accessible pregnancy test for blind and low-vision users.
auteurs: Huang Zeqi, Li Dan, Yin Haowen, Garaj Vanja
resume: Conventional pregnancy self-tests rely on the visual interpretation of test results, creating barriers to the independent use, privacy and confidence for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. This study reports the concept development and preliminary acceptability evaluation of an accessible pregnancy-test, through a five-phase user-centred design process. Phase 1 applied semi-structured interviews with ten BLV participants to identify the use barriers, needs and feedback preferences. Phase 2 translated these findings into a Product Design Specification. Phase 3 developed a concept combining tactile result feedback, a structured interaction flow and a sliding mechanism separating the sample-application area from the result-reading area. Phase 4 produced a 3D-printed prototype with manually operable mechanical features for tactile exploration, but without electronic sensing and diagnostic functionality. Phase 5 used the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)-informed semi-structured interviews to examine the perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and behavioural intention to use. The participants prioritised clear results, simple operation and privacy and generally preferred Braille and raised tactile markers over vibration and voice. The preliminary evaluation indicated positive perceptions of usefulness, ease of use and willingness to use the concept. The findings suggest that accessible pregnancy testing must prioritise not only non-visual result reading but also privacy, dignity, reproductive autonomy and independent health management. These results represent the preliminary evidence of acceptability rather than a conclusive test of device effectiveness and further functional, technical and clinical validation in the real-world conditions is required to fully understand the benefits of the new concept.

titre: Mito-Nuclear Interactions in Livestock: Implications for Adaptation, Productivity, and Precision Breeding.
titre_fr: Mito-Nuclear Interactions in Livestock: Implications for Adaptation, Productivity, and Precision Breeding.
auteurs: Panigrahi Manjit, Rajawat Divya, Upadhyay Amritanshu, Devadharshini K, Ranjith G, Rath Pratik Kumar, Verma Surya Kant, Nayak Sonali Sonejita
resume: Mitochondria are central regulators of cellular energy metabolism, stress responses, and physiological adaptation, with their functions depending on the coordinated interaction between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and nuclear DNA (nDNA). These mito-nuclear interactions are essential for maintaining oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), cellular homeostasis, and overall organismal fitness. Increasing evidence suggests that mito-nuclear compatibility influences a wide range of economically important traits in livestock, including growth, milk production, reproduction, feed efficiency, disease resistance, and environmental adaptation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of mitochondrial and nuclear genome organization, mechanisms of mito-nuclear communication, and their biological significance in livestock species. Key mechanisms discussed include mito-nuclear co-evolution, anterograde and retrograde signaling, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated signaling, epigenetic regulation, mitophagy, mitochondrial biogenesis, and mito-nuclear incompatibility. The review further highlights the role of mito-nuclear interactions in adaptation to heat stress, high-altitude environments, metabolic challenges, and disease resistance, as well as their influence on productivity traits such as milk yield, growth performance, fertility, reproductive efficiency, and longevity. Advances in genomic and multi-omics technologies, including genome-wide association studies (GWAS), mitogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, network biology, and systems genomics, have greatly enhanced our understanding of mitochondrial function and its contribution to complex traits. Furthermore, integrating mitochondrial information into genomic selection, marker-assisted breeding, climate-smart livestock improvement, and precision livestock farming (PLF) offers new opportunities to enhance productivity, resilience, and sustainability. Understanding the genetic and functional basis of mito-nuclear interactions will facilitate the development of next-generation precision breeding strategies aimed at improving livestock performance under changing environmental conditions.

titre: ATPPred: Prediction of Plant ATP-Binding Proteins Using ESM2 and 1D Convolution.
titre_fr: ATPPred: Prediction of Plant ATP-Binding Proteins Using ESM2 and 1D Convolution.
auteurs: Zhang Hong-Qi, Zhang Zi-Xuan, Qi Yi-Xuan, Chen Cheng, Huang Jian, Lin Hao, Deng Ke-Jun, Feng Juan
resume: Plant ATP-binding proteins play a central role in various physiological processes in plants, including growth and development, energy metabolism, signal transduction, and environmental adaptation. Accurately identifying ATP-binding proteins from plant protein sequences is crucial for a deeper understanding of plant physiology and their applications in agricultural biotechnology. In this study, we propose ATPPred, a tool based on the protein large language model Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2 (ESM2) and a 1-dimensional convolutional neural network for the high-precision prediction of plant ATP-binding proteins. The tool extracts global features of plant ATP-binding proteins using ESM2 and then further extracts feature information with the 1-dimensional convolutional neural network. Comprehensive performance metrics demonstrate ATPPred's competitive prediction capability. A systematic evaluation of the impact of protein sequence similarity thresholds on ATPPred yielded an average AUC ranging from 0.9191 ± 0.0161 to 0.9669 ± 0.0030 across thresholds from 0.4 to 0.9, highlighting its robustness. Cross-dataset benchmarking of ATPPred further validated the effectiveness of our framework, showcasing superior performance compared to existing methods. In summary, ATPPred provides a feasible computational approach for sequence-based prediction of plant ATP-binding proteins and may serve as a useful auxiliary tool for the preliminary screening and prioritization of candidate ATP-binding proteins.

titre: Bioinformatic Analysis and Tissue-Specific Expression of Clock Genes and Opn5 in the Chinese Giant Salamander (Andrias davidianus) Under Different Light Conditions.
titre_fr: Bioinformatic Analysis and Tissue-Specific Expression of Clock Genes and Opn5 in the Chinese Giant Salamander (Andrias davidianus) Under Different Light Conditions.
auteurs: Chen Biao, Zhou Qin, Jing Zhizhi, Yao Dong, Chen Jing, Zhou Xianwen, Wang Pei
revue: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
resume: Circadian rhythms are essential for physiological regulation and environmental adaptation of animals. Light, as a primary exogenous synchronizing signal, significantly influences the maintenance and remodeling of the circadian system. In vertebrates, circadian rhythms depend on the synergistic action of central and peripheral clocks; however, systematic studies on the molecular responses to light across different tissues in amphibians are still lacking. In this study, 64 juvenile Chinese giant salamanders (Andrias davidianus) were randomly assigned to four groups: a control group (approximately 12L:12D, 5-12 lx, C), a continuous intermediate-light group (24L:0D, 80 ± 5 lx, I), a continuous high-light group (24L:0D, 220 ± 10 lx, H), and a continuous dark group (0L:24D, 0 lx, B). The experiment spanned 13 days. We first identified candidate Clock and Opn5 homologues from transcriptome-derived sequences using homology searches, phylogenetic analysis and conserved-domain analysis. We then used RT-qPCR to measure expression changes across sampling days of Clock, Bmal1, Per2, Cry1 and Opn5 in the brain, eye and skin. The results indicated that under control and continuous intermediate-light conditions, the expression changes in core clock genes in brain and eye tissues were generally consistent, while the skin exhibited a relatively independent response pattern. Under continuous high-light conditions, the brain and eye exhibited distinct temporal expression patterns, whereas constant darkness was associated with a later-stage transcriptional response in the skin. In summary, prolonged exposure to bright light and continuous darkness were associated with distinct tissue-specific and time-dependent transcriptional responses of Opn5 and core clock genes in the brain, eye, and skin of juvenile Chinese giant salamanders. This study provides foundational data on the molecular responses of the clock genes and non-visual opsin in amphibians to abnormal lighting conditions.

titre: Nonuse and Nonpurchase of Assistive Devices After Stroke: An Exploratory Interview Study of Retrospective Device Histories Among Community-Dwelling Adults.
titre_fr: Nonuse and Nonpurchase of Assistive Devices After Stroke: An Exploratory Interview Study of Retrospective Device Histories Among Community-Dwelling Adults.
auteurs: Ro EunRae, An Kwang-Ok, Lee Sung-Yong, Kim Dong-A, Eun Seon-Deok
resume: Because function typically improves after stroke, the devices people need, and for how long, may change along the recovery trajectory. This exploratory study examined retrospective accounts of assistive device use, discontinuation, replacement, and nonpurchase across two post-onset stages, hospitalization and home and community reintegration. Ten community-dwelling adults with chronic stroke (mean disability duration 13.9 years) were interviewed twice at home, with caregivers contributing where present, and reconstructed their device histories from recall; the resulting accounts are treated as joint participant-caregiver reports. Instruments followed the Human-Activity-Assistive Technology (HAAT) model; field notes and completed device checklists were analyzed by inductive qualitative content analysis, and facilitators and barriers were classified with the World Health Organization people-centered assistive technology (5P) framework. Aggregate figures for the stroke subsample of the 2020 National Survey on Persons with Disabilities (n = 662) are reported as national context rather than as independent confirmation. Participants reported having used a mean of 11.2 device types, yet named only 1.3 devices that were needed but not purchased. Discontinuation was concentrated among devices used during inpatient rehabilitation: standing frames (9/9), walkers (5/5), and manual wheelchairs (8/10) had been set aside. Functional improvement was the only reason recorded for walkers, but for standing frames and manual wheelchairs it was recorded alongside cost, bulk, replacement, and, in one case, continuing unmet need, so its independent contribution could not be established. A second cluster reflected the poor fit of body-worn devices to a changing hemiplegic limb (ankle-foot orthoses, 4/6). The nonpurchase barrier reported most often was inability to find a suitable product on the market. These retrospective accounts from ten participants cannot support policy conclusions. They generate hypotheses, requiring prospective testing, about whether ownership-based funding with fixed durability periods fits stage-limited need and whether rental provision, prescription-based provision for orthoses, and targeted product development would fit it better.

titre: Investigation of the Relationship Between Health Literacy and Fall-Prevention Behaviours in Older Adults.
titre_fr: Investigation of the Relationship Between Health Literacy and Fall-Prevention Behaviours in Older Adults.
auteurs: Girgin Nuray, Göktaş Ayşe, Özgün Mete
resume: Background/Objectives: Falls are a leading cause of morbidity and loss of independence in later life, and more than half are preventable. Health literacy has been proposed as a modifiable determinant of preventive behaviour, but the evidence rests largely on unadjusted associations and on outcomes such as fear of falling rather than on behaviour itself. This study examined how health literacy relates to fall-prevention behaviour in community-dwelling older adults, and whether that relationship holds once sociodemographic and health-related characteristics are considered. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 253 adults aged 65 years and over completed a structured questionnaire comprising the Turkey Health Literacy Scale-32 (THLS-32) and the Falls Behavioural Scale for Older People (FaBS) between December 2023 and March 2024. The primary multivariable analysis used hierarchical multiple linear regression, with covariates selected on theoretical and clinical grounds and no automated variable selection. Results: Health literacy was inadequate or problematic-limited in 73.5% of participants. Health literacy and fall-prevention behaviour were negatively correlated (r = -0.304, p < 0.001). Exploratory subscale analyses showed the strongest inverse estimates for protective mobility (r = -0.388), practical strategies (r = -0.342) and avoidance (r = -0.331), whereas awareness-related subscales were not associated with health literacy. The sociodemographic and health-related covariate block explained 28.1% of the variance; in the final model, male sex, higher educational attainment, and assistive-device use were associated with FaBS scores. THLS-32 did not significantly improve the model (ΔR2 = 0.006, p = 0.151). Conclusions: Fall-prevention behaviour was more strongly associated with measured sociodemographic and health-related characteristics than with health literacy. Higher FaBS scores may partly reflect activity restriction as well as protective behaviour. These findings do not support the assumption that higher general health literacy alone is associated with greater use of the behaviours captured by the FaBS.

titre: Showering Barriers and Interaction Preferences of Older Adults with Mobility Disabilities for a Robotic Showerhead.
titre_fr: Showering Barriers and Interaction Preferences of Older Adults with Mobility Disabilities for a Robotic Showerhead.
auteurs: Bhowmick Pallabi, Shahid Kainat, Ren Zhiyu, Krishnan Girish, Rogers Wendy A, Rice Ian M
resume: Bathing and showering are among the most challenging daily activities for individuals with long-term mobility impairments, requiring substantial physical effort, coordination, and environmental support. Background/Objectives: This study aimed to understand showering challenges faced by older adults with long-term mobility disabilities who used wheeled mobility devices. We evaluated user and caregiver perspectives on three Soft Robotic Showerhead (SoRoSh) concepts: Elongation, Swing, and Two Showerhead designs. We explored preferred interaction modes (user-guided, voice-controlled, gesture-controlled), desired features, and perceptions of how such technologies could improve independence, safety, and usability. Methods: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 12 participants: 6 older adults aged 63-77 (M = 72.83; SD = 5.03) with at least 10 years of lower-body mobility disabilities, and 6 subject matter experts aged 30-78 (M = 60.83; SD = 16.82), including professional caregivers and family care partners. Participants discussed current routines, unmet needs, and provided feedback on the concepts and interaction modes. Data were thematically analyzed. Results: Participants reported challenges such as difficulty lifting arms, reaching body areas, handling showerheads, maintaining balance, and using unstable shower chairs. Voice control was strongly preferred due to low physical effort, whereas gesture control was viewed as impractical. Manual control was valued for familiarity, with many favoring hybrid approaches. Desired features included integrated controls, joystick input, adjustable spray modes, wake-word activation, and streamlined design. Participants believed these technologies could enhance independence, safety, and emotional well-being. Conclusions: Adaptive showering technologies should prioritize accessibility, intuitive multimodal control, customization, safety, and privacy to support independence and quality of life.

titre: Transposable elements: Drivers of regulatory innovation and adaptation in plants.
titre_fr: Transposable elements: Drivers of regulatory innovation and adaptation in plants.
auteurs: Sasaki Taku, Saze Hidetoshi
resume: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute a major fraction of eukaryotic genomes and represent one of the most abundant classes of repetitive sequences in plants. Recent advances in sequencing technologies, together with the increasing availability of telomere-to-telomere and pan-genome assemblies, have enabled comprehensive characterization of TE sequences, revealing their complex architectures, structural variation, and evolutionary dynamics across diverse plant species. Because TE mobilization can compromise gene function and genome integrity, plants have evolved sophisticated epigenetic mechanisms to restrict TE activity. In turn, TEs have co-evolved diverse strategies to evade host silencing, reflecting a continuous evolutionary arms race between host genomes and their mobile elements. Beyond their traditional view as genomic parasites, accumulating evidence now demonstrates that TEs are major drivers of genome innovation by providing novel protein-coding modules, cis-regulatory elements, and structural variation that reshape chromatin organization and gene regulatory networks. In this review, we highlight recent advances in our understanding of how TEs promote regulatory innovation, environmental adaptation, and genome evolution in plants.

titre: Deciphering genomic adaptations and climate resilience in the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica.
titre_fr: Deciphering genomic adaptations and climate resilience in the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica.
auteurs: Wang Hongzhen, Li Xinqi, Yang Jinghua, Zang Yu, Xin Jiayi, Wei Ziqing, Liang Shuo, Xue Song, Chen Wenqin, Zhang Qifan, Meng Xiying, Tang Xuexi, Chen Jun
resume: Seagrasses are coastal foundation species that support ecosystem stability but face increasing global change. Here, we assemble a chromosome-level reference genome for the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica to investigate adaptive evolution and climate resilience. Comparative genomic analyses reveal features underlying intertidal adaptation, including ion transport, circadian regulation, and stress responses. We identify positively selected genes associated with the transition to marine environments. Population genomic analyses identify strong divergence between northern and southern populations, reflecting deep historical separation, largely independent evolutionary trajectories, and local adaptation. Selection signals are enriched in stress response and ion transport genes, among which TIP3-1 confers tolerance to both salinity and heat. Genomic offset projections indicate greater climate vulnerability in northern populations, whereas southern populations show higher adaptive potential and may serve as genetic sources for assisted gene flow. Together, our study provides a genomic framework for understanding adaptation and guiding conservation under climate change.

titre: Genome-wide identification of UDP-glycosyltransferase gene family in Dendrobium huoshanense and functional characterization of DhUGT44 mediating flavonoid 7-O-glycosylation and cold tolerance.
titre_fr: Genome-wide identification of UDP-glycosyltransferase gene family in Dendrobium huoshanense and functional characterization of DhUGT44 mediating flavonoid 7-O-glycosylation and cold tolerance.
auteurs: Liu Siyuan, Ren Jiali, Liu Mengru, Yin Yongfei, Xu Tao, Lai Enhui, Guo Lanping, Han Bangxing, Yi Shanyong
resume: UDP-glycosyltransferases (UGTs) play essential roles in glycosylating plant specialized metabolites, thereby modulating their stability, solubility, and bioactivity to regulate growth, development, and environmental adaptation. Dendrobium huoshanense, a rare and endangered medicinal orchid endemic to China, is renowned for its rich bioactive glycosides, including polysaccharides, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which underpin its high medicinal value. However, systematic genome-wide identification and evolutionary analysis of the UGT gene family in Dendrobium remain limited, hindering their application in stress tolerance and quality improvement. In this study, we performed the first comprehensive genome-wide identification and functional characterization of the UGT family in D. huoshanense by integrating bioinformatics analyses with molecular experiments. A total of 71 DhUGT genes were identified and phylogenetically classified into 12 subfamilies. Cis-regulatory element analysis showed that most DhUGT promoters are enriched with phytohormone- and abiotic stress-responsive motifs. By integrating multi-omics transcriptomic data, we identified DhUGT44 (subfamily L) as a high priority candidate, exhibiting consistently high expression across tissues, cultivation conditions, and growth stages. Its promoter contains cold-responsive elements, and RT-qPCR confirmed significant induction under low temperature stress in leaves. Subcellular localization assays demonstrated dual localization of DhUGT44 to the plasma membrane and chloroplasts. In vitro enzymatic assays and transient expression in Nicotiana benthamiana revealed that DhUGT44 specifically catalyzes 7-O-glycosylation of flavonoid substrates. Furthermore, heterologous overexpression of DhUGT44 in Arabidopsis thaliana significantly enhanced primary root growth under cold stress compared to wild-type plants, indicating its positive role in cold tolerance. This study provides the first systematic insight into the evolutionary dynamics and transcriptional regulation of the UGT family in D. huoshanense, while elucidating the flavonoid glycosylation function and cold tolerance regulatory role of DhUGT44. These findings offer valuable genetic resources and a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and metabolic engineering of stress tolerance and bioactive compounds in Dendrobium.

titre: Technological interventions in dyslexia: a neurobiological perspective of language learning.
titre_fr: Technological interventions in dyslexia: a neurobiological perspective of language learning.
auteurs: R V Monicka Sre, Ponniah R Joseph
resume: Developmental dyslexia is a neurodevelopmental language learning disorder characterised by persistent difficulty in phonological processing and fluent word recognition. To address these challenges, a range of interventions has been developed to support reading acquisition and fluency. These interventions include a promising field of technological aids that cater to a broader audience. However, the limited understanding of the neurobiological effects of technological interventions restricts significant evaluation of their effectiveness. The paper examines the influence of technological interventions on the neural mechanisms that support reading in individuals with developmental dyslexia. This narrative review maintains methodological precision by focusing exclusively on literature that bridges the gap between instructional technology and its neurobiological outcomes, offering an integrated analysis of behavioural and neurobiological shifts in literacy development. The findings suggest that the technological interventions enhance phonological processing efficiency by strengthening neurocognitive networks and promoting compensatory activation patterns. However, these results cannot be widely generalised due to the inconsistencies in intervention design and methodological rigour. Thus, to take a closer look at the efficacy of technological interventions, this paper aims to offer a comprehensive neurobiological review of the effects of interventions and assistive technologies, highlighting the neural and behavioural outcomes while pointing to unresolved questions for future investigation.

titre: Integrated assays with in silico analyses indicated the biocontrol potential of Bacillus velezensis BJ1 against fungal phytopathogens.
titre_fr: Integrated assays with in silico analyses indicated the biocontrol potential of Bacillus velezensis BJ1 against fungal phytopathogens.
auteurs: Li Yonghua, Madushani Manawaduge Ayesha, Liu Mei, Wang Chenfang, Wang Hui, Li Xinghong, Hyde Kevin David, Zhang Wei, Yan Jiye
resume: Fungal diseases continue to devastate global fruit and vegetable production, emphasizing the urgent need for sustainable disease management approaches such as microbial biocontrol. In this study, a locally isolated bacterial strain was identified as Bacillus velezensis BJ1 based on phylogenomic analysis, and its biocontrol potential was evaluated using in vitro, in vivo, and in planta assays combined with in silico analysis. In vitro dual culture assay demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonistic activity of the BJ1 strain against 59 isolates of common fungal phytopathogens affecting fruit trees and vegetables, with inhibition rates ranging from 53.76% to 98.45%. The strongest suppression was observed against Diaporthe sojae OSS① (98.45%), followed by D. sojae B2 JZB320190 (89.15%), Cladosporium cladosporioides TZZG-11-A-S1 (85.37%), C. cladosporioides TZZG-6-A-S1 (85.22%), D. sojae JZB320189 (80.62%), and D. eres TZZG36-S1 (80.62%). Detached tomato leaf assays against the gray mold pathogen Botrytis cinerea demonstrated that BJ1 achieved high control efficiencies of 87.87% and 68.95% for therapeutic and preventive treatments, respectively, at a concentration of 1 × 10⁷ CFU/mL. Furthermore, a BJ1-based water-dispersible granule formulation applied at 2 × 108 CFU/mL achieved an 80.48% disease inhibition rate under greenhouse conditions. Genome mining identified 13 biosynthetic gene clusters encoding antimicrobial compounds, suggesting a genetic basis for BJ1's biocontrol activity. Overall, B. velezensis BJ1 demonstrates strong potential for development as an effective biocontrol product, offering both genomic insights and practical application in sustainable disease management. Biological control is a sustainable strategy for managing plant pathogens while reducing the environmental and health risks associated with chemical pesticides. However, their practical application is often limited by poor environmental adaptation, limited broad-spectrum activity, and inconsistent efficacy. Bacillus velezensis BJ1, a locally isolated strain, exhibited broad antagonistic activity against 59 isolates of common phytopathogens across eight host plants. Further, it exhibited consistent in vivo and in planta efficacy against the highly virulent pathogen Botrytis cinerea under both protective and therapeutic treatments, highlighting its potential for both disease prevention and post-infection suppression. Whole-genome phylogenomic analysis confirmed its precise taxonomic identity, and genome mining suggested multiple biosynthetic gene clusters potentially associated with antifungal activity and plant protection. This study highlights BJ1 as a robust and eco-friendly candidate for sustainable disease management.

titre: Effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative interventions for post-COVID-19 condition: a systematic review.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative interventions for post-COVID-19 condition: a systematic review.
auteurs: Negm Akram, Stolz Maike, Krauth Christian
resume: To evaluate supervised physical, psycho-logical, and alternative non-pharmacological interventions for improving patient-reported and objective functional outcomes in adults with post-COVID-19 condition. Systematic review of randomized controlled trials. PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycInfo, and Scopus were searched from 1 January 2020 to 29 January 2026. Eligible studies were supervised, face-to-face trials evaluating physical, psychological, or alternative non-pharmacological interventions against usual care, placebo/sham, or active comparators in adults with World Health Organization defined post-COVID-19 condition. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2. Due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed. 27 trials (1,998 participants) were included and evaluated physical, psychological, and alternative therapies. Supervised cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and multimodal exercise consistently improved cardiorespiratory fitness and walking capacity. Cognitive-behavioural therapy and lifestyle adjustments significantly reduced fatigue and subjective concentration complaints. Findings for neuromodulation, complementary, and oxygen therapies were heterogeneous, often showing no benefit over placebo. Only 18.5% of trials had low risk of bias, limited by small samples, unblinding, and short follow-ups. Supervised physical rehabilitation and CBT show promising evidence for improving functional capacity and symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm effectiveness and inform clinical guidelines.

titre: Clinical and functional outcomes of aquatic plyometrics in adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome: a dual-arm randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Clinical and functional outcomes of aquatic plyometrics in adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome: a dual-arm randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Alotaibi Mazyad A, Elnaggar Ragab K, Alhowimel Ahmed S, Alrawaili Saud M, Elnegamy Tamer E, Alfeheid Hesham A, Basha Maged A, Kamel FatmaAlzahraa H, Aloraini Saleh M, Alsultan Feras, Alharbi Amal, Elfakharany Mahmoud S
resume: Optimal management of adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome requires evidence-based interventions that maximize physical recovery without overloading the patellofemoral joint. This study investigated the efficacy of aquatic plyometric (Aquatic-Plyo) exercises on pain, muscle strength, and functional disability and health-related quality of life in this demographic. A dual-arm randomized controlled trial. 56 adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome (age: 10-18 years). Adolescents were allocated to an experimental Aquatic-Plyo group or a control group performing conventional exercises. Both arms completed 45-min sessions twice weekly for 12 weeks. Pre- and post-treatment assessments included pain intensity, isokinetic knee (quadriceps and hamstrings) torque at 120°/s and 180°/s, functional disability, and health-related quality of life. Mixed-model ANOVA confirmed the therapeutic dominance of the Aquatic-Plyo protocol. It yielded superior pain relief (p = 0.004, η2p = 0.14) and larger increases in quadriceps [120°/s (p = 0.006, η2p = 0.13); 180°/s (p = 0.008, η2p = 0.12)] and hamstring [120°/s (p = 0.007, η2p = 0.13); 180°/s (p = 0.023, η2p = 0.09)] peak torque. Moreover, the Aquatic-Plyo intervention drove greater reduction in functional disability (p = 0.03, η2p = 0.08) and notable enhancement in perceived health-related quality of life (p = 0.023, η2p = 0.09). Aquatic-Plyo exercises effectively reduces pain and disability while improving muscle strength and health-related quality of life in adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome, making it a valuable addition to conservative rehabilitation strategies.

titre: Severe Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy and Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Following Accidental Butane Exposure: A Case Report.
titre_fr: Severe Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy and Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Following Accidental Butane Exposure: A Case Report.
auteurs: Tiburzi Simona Paola, Nistico' Rosetta, Stivala Vincenzo, De Luca Archina, Justiz-Pérez Isora, Putignano Antonella, Vescio Virginia
resume: Butane is a highly lipophilic aliphatic hydrocarbon widely used as a domestic fuel and aerosol propellant. Acute exposure in enclosed environments may cause severe neurological and cardiovascular toxicity through oxygen displacement, respiratory depression, myocardial sensitisation to catecholamines, and potentially direct toxic effects. A 45-year-old woman was found unconscious in a small, closed studio apartment, while her husband was found deceased in the same environment. Subsequent inspection by the judicial authorities identified deterioration of the gas tubing associated with a gas leak. The patient presented in deep coma (Glasgow Coma Scale score 5) and required tracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial carboxyhaemoglobin was 16.9% and progressively normalised during oxygen therapy. Brain imaging demonstrated extensive cortical, deep grey matter, brainstem, cerebellar, and white-matter abnormalities consistent with severe hypoxic-ischaemic injury. Cardiac evaluation showed mild ST-segment elevation, increased cardiac biomarkers, and severe transient Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction (LVEF 25%) with a pattern highly suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy; LVEF subsequently improved to 44%. Severe neurological impairment persisted, and the patient was transferred to neurological rehabilitation. She died approximately six months after the index event; reliable documentation of the precise cause of death was unavailable. This case illustrates the severe neurological and cardiovascular consequences that may follow accidental butane exposure in an enclosed environment. The coexistence of extensive hypoxic- ischaemic brain injury and transient stress-related ventricular dysfunction highlights the importance of integrated neurological, cardiological, and toxicological assessment.

titre: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
titre_fr: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
auteurs: Baudry Guillaume, Joyce Emer, Adamo Marianna, Batista Dos Santos Pedrosa Rafaela, Ben Gal Tuvia, Bonios Michael, Crespo-Leiro Maria Generosa, Hoejskov Ida E, Iacovoni Attilio, Kapelios Chris, Lim Hoong Sern, Metra Marco, Schoenrath Felix, Skouri Hadi, Van Laake Linda W, Damman Kevin
resume: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.
