titre: Conservative and Nonsurgical Management of Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
titre_fr: Conservative and Nonsurgical Management of Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
auteurs: Hong Christopher X, LaCross Jennifer
resume: Pelvic organ prolapse is a common condition for which treatment should be guided by symptom burden, functional impairment, and patient goals. Conservative management represents first-line therapy and includes expectant management, lifestyle and behavioral modification, pelvic floor physiotherapy, and vaginal pessary treatment. This review summarizes contemporary evidence supporting these approaches, including pelvic floor muscle training, constipation and activity management, and pessary fitting, maintenance, and outcomes. We additionally highlight recent advances in pelvic floor rehabilitation, pessary biomechanics, patient self-management, and patient-specific pessary technologies that may further individualize prolapse care.

titre: Walking and strength outcomes of targeted hip resistance training may be predicted by both MRI and clinical measures in multiple sclerosis.
titre_fr: Walking and strength outcomes of targeted hip resistance training may be predicted by both MRI and clinical measures in multiple sclerosis.
auteurs: Fritz Nora E, Eloyan Ani, Keller Jennifer, Zackowski Kathleen M
resume: Compromised neural function contributes sensation, strength, and walking deficits in persons with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). Progressive resistance training (PRT) promotes neural adaptations, leading to favorable functional outcomes, while advances in MRI enable the evaluation of white matter tract pathology in vivo. The purpose of this work was to examine the utility of MRI with clinical measures to predict exercise responsiveness to PRT. Twenty-eight PwMS (mean age: 49.3 and EDSS: 3.8) and 26 controls (mean age: 50) participated in 12-weeks of PRT. Primary outcomes were change in walk velocity and hip strength. Model predictors included baseline demographics, falls, walk velocity, strength, cognitive performance, quality of life, vibration sensation and 3T MRI measures of spinal cord area (SCA) and corticospinal tract (CST) fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD) and magnetization transfer ratio (MTR). A random forest procedure was used as an exploratory analysis for prediction of exercise responsiveness. The predictive accuracy was measured using the normalized mean squared error (MSE) within a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure, but was not externally validated. Strength change predictors included baseline strength, diagnosis, age, disease severity, falls, cognitive performance, quality of life, vibration, and CST (FA, MD, and MTR) (normalized MSE: 0.1792). Walk velocity change predictors included baseline walk velocity, age, disease severity, sex, cognitive performance, vibration, and CST (FA, MD, and MTR) (normalized MSE: 0.2147). A combination of motor, cognitive, and MRI measures may predict responsiveness to a PRT program in PwMS. These data confirm that optimizing function relies on knowledge of pathology, disability level and intervention selection in pwMS, and that using imaging information in combination with functional performance may offer advantages to optimizing functional recovery for pwMS.

titre: Economic evaluation of the Akwenda Intervention Program for children and young people with cerebral palsy in rural Uganda: A trial-based analysis of costs and outcomes.
titre_fr: Economic evaluation of the Akwenda Intervention Program for children and young people with cerebral palsy in rural Uganda: A trial-based analysis of costs and outcomes.
auteurs: Asige Elizabeth, Kintu Eric, Saloojee Gillian, Wanjala Godfrey, Andrews Carin, Namaganda Lukia H, Kakooza-Mwesige Angelina, Damiano Diane L, Forssberg Hans
resume: To relate the trial-based costs of the Akwenda Intervention Program, a multi-component, community-based intervention for children and young people with cerebral palsy (CP) in rural Uganda, to multiple prespecified child and caregiver outcomes. An economic evaluation was conducted within a cluster-randomized, assessor-blinded trial of 94 participants with CP (aged 2-23 years; 42 females) and their caregivers, allocated to intervention or usual care. Programme delivery costs were assessed from a restricted health care or provider perspective; selected out-of-pocket costs incurred by participating families were reported separately over 12 months. Outcome-specific incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were estimated for child outcomes (66-item Gross Motor Function Measure, Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory [Ugandan version], and Picture My Participation) and caregiver outcomes (Zimbabwe Caregiver Challenges Scale and Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory Family Impact Module). Uncertainty was assessed using bootstrapping, cost-effectiveness planes, and exploratory acceptability curves. Costs were also determined per minimal clinically important difference (MCID) gained. The mean incremental cost per child was US$1069 to US$1075. Outcome-specific ICERs ranged from US$26 to US$352 per unit of improvement for 10 of 11 outcomes; the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory (Ugandan version) mobility had a higher and highly uncertain ICER. Costs per MCID gained ranged from US$230 to US$600. Acceptability analyses were presented as exploratory uncertainty analyses because no established Uganda-specific willingness-to-pay thresholds exist for these outcome measures. The Akwenda Intervention Program improved child functioning, participation, and caregiver well-being at additional but predictable costs. This trial-based economic evaluation quantifies the costs associated with improvement across multiple prespecified outcomes and provides economic information relevant to the implementation of community-based rehabilitation in low-resource settings.
resume_fr: To relate the trial-based costs of the Akwenda Intervention Program, a multi-component, community-based intervention for children and young people with cerebral palsy (CP) in rural Uganda, to multiple prespecified child and caregiver outcomes. titre: When Deviation Is Necessary: Balancing Intervention Fidelity and Contextual Adaptation in Haemodialysis Physiotherapy.
titre_fr: When Deviation Is Necessary: Balancing Intervention Fidelity and Contextual Adaptation in Haemodialysis Physiotherapy.
auteurs: Dobhal Santosh P, Shukla Manish Prannath, Mishra Abhishek, Indurkar Ira
revue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
resume: Exercise-based physiotherapy is recommended as a core component of haemodialysis care; however, its implementation in routine clinical practice remains inconsistent. While intervention fidelity is considered essential for ensuring evidence-based practice, little is known about how physiotherapists adapt rehabilitation protocols in response to the complexities of real-world clinical environments. To explore how physiotherapists balance intervention fidelity with contextual adaptation during haemodialysis rehabilitation and to examine the cognitive, social, and contextual factors influencing clinical decision-making. A qualitative interpretive study was conducted across four haemodialysis centres using semi-structured interviews with 16 physiotherapists. Participants were recruited through purposive maximum-variation sampling to capture diverse clinical experiences and practice settings. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, with findings subsequently interpreted through the Mindlines model. Four interrelated themes were identified: Safety Overrides Protocol, Experience as the Primary Guide, Context Shapes Practice, and Guidelines as Flexible References, which collectively informed the overarching theme of Adaptation as Skilled Practice. Physiotherapists consistently prioritised patient safety by modifying interventions according to physiological status and individual patient needs. Clinical decisions were informed by experiential knowledge, interprofessional interactions, and organisational constraints, with guidelines serving as flexible reference points rather than prescriptive rules. The findings demonstrate that context-sensitive adaptation represents deliberate clinical reasoning rather than simple protocol non-adherence. Intervention fidelity in haemodialysis physiotherapy should be understood as a dynamic process that accommodates appropriate contextual adaptation while preserving the core intent of rehabilitation. Recognizing adaptive clinical expertise may strengthen the implementation of evidence-based physiotherapy in complex healthcare settings.

titre: Deep palmar thermal burns in children: predictive factors of post‑burn contracture and timing of secondary surgery - a cohort study of 273 palms.
titre_fr: Deep palmar thermal burns in children: predictive factors of post‑burn contracture and timing of secondary surgery - a cohort study of 273 palms.
auteurs: Lancien Ugo, Thuau François, Creusat Mathilde, Elie Estelle, Perrot Pierre
resume: Deep palmar burns in young children frequently cause disabling contractures. We aimed to identify the incidence, risk factors, and optimal timing of secondary surgery for surgically significant palmar contracture after split-thickness skin grafting in children under five years. We conducted a retrospective study of all children <5 years with deep palmar thermal contact burns requiring skin grafting at a single pediatric burn center (2006-2021, minimum 5-year follow-up). All palms were uniformly resurfaced with thin, non-glabrous split-thickness skin grafts harvested from the scalp under a single institutional protocol.Exclusions included non-contact or dorsal injuries, incomplete data, and loss to follow-up. The primary outcome was scar contracture with functional impairment requiring corrective surgery; time to intervention was secondary. Multivariable Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis identified risk factors. Across 273 burned palms in 229 children (mean age at burn 16.5 months, 55.7% male), 125 hands (45.8%) developed a palmar contracture requiring secondary surgery. After adjustment, first web space involvement (HRa 4.45) and third-degree depth (HRa 1.93) were independent predictors, and metacarpal head involvement was protective (HRa 0.32). Referral to a specialized rehabilitation center was also associated with contracture (HRa 1.95) but is best interpreted as a marker of initial burn severity rather than an independent predictor. Mean time to surgery among affected cases was 3.2 years, earliest for hypothenar and first web space involvement. Surgical contracture is common after deep palmar burns in young children, especially with first web space involvement and severe burns. Early risk stratification enables targeted surveillance and intervention, and may help improve patient outcomes. These findings apply to palms resurfaced with thin split-thickness skin grafts; the uniform protocol did not allow comparison with full-thickness or glabrous grafts, which remain alternative options.

titre: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial.
titre_fr: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial.
auteurs: Boldó Alcaine Maria, Durà Mata Maria José, Sandoval Ruíz Gabriel-Fernando, Llaberia Marcual Maria, Carceller de la Torre Marta, Domingo Teixidor Mar, Santiago Vacas Evelyn, Bayés Genís Antoni
resume: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but access remains suboptimal. Telerehabilitation may overcome barriers, yet evidence from real-world, public health systems is limited. This randomized controlled trial study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured telerehabilitation programme compared with standard centre-based CR in patients after ACS, focussing on cardiovascular risk factor control and lifestyle adherence. TELECOR is a pragmatic, open-label, randomized trial conducted at a tertiary public hospital. Adults with recent ACS were randomized 1:1 to an 8 week structured telerehabilitation or a centre-based CR programme. The primary outcome was achievement of a composite target (≥4 of 7 predefined cardiovascular and lifestyle goals) at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in functional capacity, medication adherence, quality of life, psychological status, satisfaction, and cardiovascular events at 6 months. A total of 129 patients were randomized (65 telerehabilitation, 64 centre-based). At 8 weeks, 86% of telerehabilitation vs. 79.7% of centre-based participants met the composite target (P = 0.37). At 6 months, this was 87% vs. 80.4% (P = 0.34). Both groups showed similar improvements in functional capacity (≈+1 metabolic equivalent of tasks), adherence (>84%), and satisfaction (>91/100). No between-group differences were observed in clinical events or psychological outcomes. In a real-world public hospital setting, telerehabilitation was non-inferior to conventional CR in achieving cardiovascular risk factor control and improving functional capacity. These results support the broader integration of digital CR models into routine secondary prevention care.

titre: Voice Rehabilitation After Early Laryngeal Cancer: A Narrative Review.
titre_fr: Voice Rehabilitation After Early Laryngeal Cancer: A Narrative Review.
auteurs: Nosratian Yasaman Ekram, Dabirmoghaddam Payman, Khatoonabadi Ahmadreza, Aghadoost Samira
revue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
resume: Early-stage laryngeal cancer, particularly glottic carcinoma, is commonly treated with radiotherapy or transoral CO₂ laser microsurgery. Although these treatments offer favorable oncologic control, voice impairment often persists as a long-term functional concern, affecting quality of life and communication. Voice therapy has been proposed as a rehabilitative intervention to address these voice limitations; however, no standardized protocol currently exists. This narrative review aims to synthesize and critically evaluate the available evidence on voice therapy techniques employed for voice rehabilitation in patients treated for early laryngeal cancer. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar through May 2026. The search strategy combined terms related to laryngeal cancer and voice therapy using Boolean operators. Studies published in English that investigated voice therapy techniques, protocols, or outcomes following conservative treatment (radiotherapy or transoral laser microsurgery) for early-stage laryngeal cancer were included. Reviews, non-English publications, case reports unrelated to therapy, and papers without an accessible full text were excluded. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies employed structured rehabilitation protocols combining breathing, relaxation, posture, and phonation exercises, typically delivered over 8-10 sessions. Findings consistently indicated that voice therapy provides clinically meaningful improvements in voice-related quality of life, perceptual voice outcomes, and patient-reported voice outcomes, particularly over short- to intermediate-term follow-up periods. Improvements were sustained but partially attenuated over longer follow-up durations. Acoustic outcomes remained variable despite perceptual and functional gains. Voice therapy appears to be an effective rehabilitative intervention for improving voice outcomes following conservative treatment for early laryngeal cancer. Structured physiologic voice therapy seems more effective than indirect approaches alone. However, substantial heterogeneity in intervention protocols, outcome measures, and follow-up durations limits direct comparison across studies. Future research should prioritize large-scale controlled trials with standardized multidimensional outcome measures and long-term follow-up to better delineate treatment efficacy and durability.

titre: Modified Suzuki Frame Fixation for the Treatment of Dorsal Proximal Interphalangeal Joint Fracture-Dislocation.
titre_fr: Modified Suzuki Frame Fixation for the Treatment of Dorsal Proximal Interphalangeal Joint Fracture-Dislocation.
auteurs: Jerome J Terrence Jose, Malshikare Vijay
resume: The proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint is critical for hand function, contributing substantially to grasping and overall dexterity<sup>1-3</sup>. Injuries to this joint, often caused by axial loading, can lead to various fracture patterns and dislocations, resulting in long-term complications such as pain, stiffness, reduced range of motion, arthritis, and instability<sup>1,2</sup>. Traditional surgical approaches for unstable dorsal PIP joint fracture-dislocation include dorsal block pinning, open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF), hemi-hamate or hemi-capitate arthroplasty, and external fixation<sup>1-3</sup>. Although these methods can be effective, they may have limitations in certain situations. The Suzuki frame, a pins-and-rubber-band traction system, offers a dynamic external fixation option that allows for early controlled motion while maintaining fracture reduction. This technique has several advantages, including ligamentotaxis (the traction force helps to reduce fracture fragments and restore joint alignment), early mobilization (the dynamic nature of the frame allows for early active motion, minimizing joint stiffness), and simplicity (the technique is relatively straightforward and can be performed with readily available materials). The modified Suzuki frame procedure for dorsal PIP joint fracture-dislocation involves administering local anesthesia and establishing a sterile field. Under fluoroscopic guidance, three 1.0-mm Kirschner wires are inserted: 1 through the center of rotation of the proximal phalangeal head, 1 through the center of rotation of the middle phalangeal head, and 1 (the "translation pin") in the middle phalanx distal to the fracture. The wires are then bent to create a frame with hooks, and the translation pin is secured to the proximal wire. Rubber bands are applied between the hooks to provide traction and maintain reduction. PIP joint congruency is confirmed through a full range of motion under fluoroscopy. Dressings and a splint are applied, allowing for limited immediate postoperative motion. Formal hand therapy begins 1 week postoperatively. Although nonsurgical treatment may be considered for stable, minimally displaced dorsal PIP joint fracture-dislocations, unstable injuries often necessitate operative intervention to restore joint congruity and stability. Several surgical techniques are available to treat these injuries, each with its own advantages and limitations. These techniques include dorsal block pinning, ORIF, hemi-hamate or hemi-capitate arthroplasty, and the use of modified external fixators with various external fixation constructs and pins to provide stability and allow for early controlled motion. The modified Suzuki frame is a dynamic external fixator that addresses the limitations of other treatment options for dorsal PIP joint fracture-dislocation. The modified Suzuki frame provides distraction, ligamentotaxis, and a volar-directed force while allowing early range of motion, preventing stiffness, and promoting cartilage healing<sup>1,2</sup>. This technique dynamically adjusts traction, unlike the use of static fixation, and is less invasive than ORIF, preserving joint anatomy that is crucial for younger patients. Use of the modified Suzuki frame is also simpler than that of traditional external fixators, making it ideal for complex fractures, soft-tissue injuries, and early mobilization<sup>1-3</sup>. The modified Suzuki frame is designed to stabilize finger fractures while permitting early mobilization during the healing process. This approach helps reduce stiffness and increases the likelihood of regaining full finger function. Dynamic external fixation of this type has been shown to be highly effective for complex PIP joint injuries. Suzuki et al. reported that patients achieved an average range of motion of 80° at the PIP joint<sup>1</sup>. Ellis et al. demonstrated comparable outcomes, with patients achieving an average range of motion from 1° to 89°<sup>2</sup>. With appropriate care and diligent rehabilitation, patients can generally expect to regain satisfactory motion and function of the injured finger. Continuous monitoring and structured exercise programs are recommended to support optimal recovery outcomes. Emphasize proper pin care to patients.Kirschner wire migration or breakage can occur. Monitor pin sites regularly and address any issues promptly.Excessive traction can lead to distraction of the fracture or joint. Adjust the rubber bands as needed to maintain appropriate tension.Achieving and maintaining adequate reduction in complex fracture patterns can be challenging.Balancing stability and motion requires careful adjustment of the frame and rubber band tension.Patient compliance with pin care and rehabilitation protocols is essential for optimal outcomes. titre: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
titre_fr: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
auteurs: P G Rini, Doreswamy Yoganarasimha, T R Laxmi
resume: Preclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet. The present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity. Cerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. VPA (300 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily) was administered within 3 h after reperfusion and continued for 7 days, followed by constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for another week (6 h/day). The ischaemic stroke phenotype was assessed based on neurological deficits, gait, forelimb use, rotarod stay time, reach success and infarct volume. Functional recovery, with associated changes in neural activities, was carried out by analysing the local field potential signals from the first reach success during the reach-to-grasp task on day 8 and day 15 post-stroke. Cortical oscillations were analysed at delta (0-4 Hz), theta (4-8 and 8-12 Hz) and beta (12-20 Hz) during the first reach success. Combination therapy after ischaemic stroke significantly improved motor and neurological functions compared to monotherapy and vehicle controls. The neural oscillations revealed a significant increase in theta power in the injured motor cortex after combination therapy when compared to that with monotherapy and control groups. The significant increase in the cross-correlation between hemispheres in the combination therapy group over monotherapy indicating an increased synchronised functional connectivity between the injured (left) and uninjured motor (right) cortices. Interestingly, VPA as monotherapy did not significantly reduce infarct volume compared to the vehicle controls. Furthermore, the therapeutic efficacy of monotherapies with VPA and early-onset CIMT (initiated immediately post-stroke) showed limited efficacy in promoting motor and neurological recovery. In conclusion, the study demonstrates that VPA combined with physical rehabilitative training (CIMT) enhances functional recovery by enhancing inter-hemispheric functional connectivity and represents a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate persistent post-stroke motor deficits.

titre: The Most Recent European and American Guidelines on Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Lack of Focus on Diaphragm Training.
titre_fr: The Most Recent European and American Guidelines on Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Lack of Focus on Diaphragm Training.
auteurs: Bordoni Bruno, Morabito Bruno, Escher Allan R
resume: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death and morbidity worldwide. Patients with vascular and cardiac conditions undergo cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a process that may begin before surgery (less frequently), after invasive procedures, or as part of chronic disease management, with durations varying by healthcare facilities or national policies. CR is a valuable non-pharmacological intervention that supports patient health and the resumption of daily activities. These rehabilitation programmes are strongly recommended for cardiac patients and are structured according to guidelines from organisations such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the American Heart Association/American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation (AHA/AACPR). This editorial reviews the latest ESC and AHA/AACPR guidelines, emphasising physical activities such as endurance and resistance training, while highlighting the lack of detail on inspiratory muscle training (IMT). The editorial reiterates the Italian Association of Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC) proposals regarding IMT and calls for further clinical trials.
resume_fr: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death and morbidity worldwide. Patients with vascular and cardiac conditions undergo cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a process that may begin before surgery (less frequently), after invasive procedures, or as part of chronic disease management, with durations varying by healthcare facilities or national policies. CR is a valuable non-pharmacological intervention that supports patient health and the resumption of daily activities. These rehabilitation programmes are strongly recommended for cardiac patients and are structured according to guidelines from organisations such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the American Heart Association/American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation (AHA/AACPR). This editorial reviews the latest ESC and AHA/AACPR guidelines, emphasising physical activities such as endurance and resistance training, while highlighting the lack of detail on inspiratory muscle training (IMT). The editorial reiterates the Italian Association of Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC) proposals regarding IMT and calls for further clinical trials.

titre: Postoperative functional rehabilitation for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: An integrative review guided by Orem's self-care deficit theory.
titre_fr: Postoperative functional rehabilitation for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: An integrative review guided by Orem's self-care deficit theory.
auteurs: Wang Xiaoping, Zhang Xuerong, Zhao Qing, Liu Can, He Yanling, Li Meifang
revue: International journal of nursing studies advances
resume: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy is the predominant cause of spinal cord dysfunction in adults, for which surgical decompression remains the mainstay of treatment. Surgical success alone does not guarantee functional restoration, and postoperative rehabilitation is a critical determinant of long-term outcome. A comprehensive, theory-grounded nursing framework to guide rehabilitation practice for this population has not been available. To synthesise the current evidence on postoperative rehabilitation nursing for patients with cervical spondylotic myelopathy, to develop a theory-informed nursing framework anchored in Orem's Self-Care Deficit Nursing Theory, and to identify research gaps and priorities. Integrative review following the methodology of Whittemore and Knafl, with reporting guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement where applicable. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Complete, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase and OpenAlex, together with reference-list screening, searched for reports published between January 2014 and January 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and appraised methodological quality using instruments appropriate to each study design. A theory-driven narrative synthesis with thematic analysis was performed, and the findings were mapped onto the constructs of Orem's theory. Fifty-one studies met the inclusion criteria. Four synthesis domains were identified: risk stratification and acute-phase management; phased functional exercise rehabilitation; pain management and psychobehavioural support; and long-term follow-up and telerehabilitation. Psychological barriers were prominent; a single-centre study reported a kinesiophobia prevalence of 75.4% after surgery, although this estimate derives from limited evidence and requires confirmation in larger, multi-centre cohorts. A Rehabilitation Nursing System Selection Framework was developed to operationalise the constructs of Orem's theory as a conceptual basis for individualising postoperative nursing care. Effective postoperative rehabilitation after surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy requires concurrent attention to physical and psychological dimensions. The kinesiophobia prevalence reported in individual studies suggests that screening for psychological barriers may help identify patients who could benefit from additional psychological or behavioural support alongside physical rehabilitation. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing standardised nursing protocols and for advancing intervention research in this field. Registered retrospectively with the Open Science Framework Registries (https://osf.io/4jh7q) on 12 December 2025.

titre: Effects of Single-Session High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (HD-tACS) Combined with Robot-Assisted Hand Exercises on Corticospinal Excitability in Chronic Stroke.
titre_fr: Effects of Single-Session High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (HD-tACS) Combined with Robot-Assisted Hand Exercises on Corticospinal Excitability in Chronic Stroke.
auteurs: Meng Hao, Houston Michael, Rao Ahmad Z, Rho Jinsook, Francisco Gerard E, Li Sheng
revue: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
resume: This preliminary study investigated whether a single session of high-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) could improve corticospinal tract (CST) excitability compared with sham stimulation in healthy individuals and individuals with chronic stroke. Twelve healthy adults and 7 individuals with chronic stroke received active and sham HD-tACS over the primary motor cortex (M1) flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) hotspot, ipsilesional in stroke subjects, for 30 minutes at 2mA and 21 Hz in a randomized crossover design. All subjects performed robot-assisted grasp-and-open hand exercises during active and sham stimulation. HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in the healthy group (15.3%). In the stroke group, FDS MEP amplitudes were increased by ∼22.3% after HD-tACS, but this change was not statistically significant. When MEP amplitudes were normalized as percentage change, HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in both groups compared with the sham condition. No significant extensor digitorum communis (EDC) modulation was observed in either group. HD-tACS combined with robot-assisted hand exercises may enhance CST excitability compared with robot-assisted hand exercises alone after a single session in both healthy and stroke subjects. However, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

titre: Osteopathic manual therapy in fibromyalgia: a pilot study.
titre_fr: Osteopathic manual therapy in fibromyalgia: a pilot study.
auteurs: Dengiz Aziz, Kabul Elif Gur, Tikac Gulsum, Calik Bilge Basakci, Karasu Uğur
resume: The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and feasibility of integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques combined with Clinical Pilates on pain, symptom severity, and sleep quality in patients with fibromyalgia. Twenty women with fibromyalgia were randomized into Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates (n=11) and Clinical Pilates (n=9) groups. The protocol lasted 6 weeks (3 sessions/week). Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques included rib raising, suboccipital myofascial release, Sternocleidomastoid (SCM) mobilization, diaphragm/mediastinum techniques, and visceral mobilizations. Primary outcomes were the Widespread Pain Index, Symptom Severity Scale, and Pressure Pain Threshold. Sleep was assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Both groups showed significant intra-group improvements (p<0.05). Within-group analyses revealed that the Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates group achieved significant improvements in Widespread Pain Index (p=0.003), Symptom Severity Scale (p=0.005), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (p=0.007). However, in the between-group analysis of change scores, the Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates group demonstrated significantly superior improvements exclusively in sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, p=0.034) and maximal Pressure Pain Threshold at the trapezius (p=0.035) compared to the Clinical Pilates-only group, while between-group differences for Widespread Pain Index and Symptom Severity Scale did not reach statistical significance (p>0.05). Integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques into exercise-based rehabilitation presents promising preliminary evidence for enhancing central sensitization symptoms and sleep quality in fibromyalgia patients, though larger trials are needed.

titre: Effect of Hand Grip Exercise on Rotator Cuff Strength and Shoulder Function Recovery after Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
titre_fr: Effect of Hand Grip Exercise on Rotator Cuff Strength and Shoulder Function Recovery after Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
auteurs: Park Byeong Sun, Cho Seung Ik, Jeong Da Hui, Nam Hailey, Yoo Ji Seung, Lee Dong Hwan, Chung Seok Won
resume: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of hand grip exercise on rotator cuff strength and shoulder function after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Ninety patients who underwent arthroscopic rotator cuff repair were randomly allocated into the grip exercise group (n = 45) and control group (n = 45). The hand grip strengthening exercise (3 sets of 15 repetitions, twice daily) was applied only to the grip exercise group immediately after surgery up to 3 months. From 3 months postoperatively, the same rotator cuff and periscapular muscle strengthening exercises were applied to both groups. The isometric strength of the shoulder joint (abductor, external rotator, and internal rotator) and periscapular muscles, tone and stiffness of the upper trapezius muscle, range of motion (ROM), pain visual analog scale (VAS) score, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Constant score, and University of California, Los Angeles score were measured preoperatively and at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Changes in the supraspinatus muscle atrophy and repair integrity were assessed via magnetic resonance imaging at 6 months postoperatively. At 3 months, abductor, external rotator, and internal rotator muscle strengths were not significantly different between groups, but at 6 months, the grip exercise group showed significantly higher external rotator and internal rotator strengths (all p < 0.05). Similarly, the periscapular muscle strengths were not different at 3 months, but the serratus anterior muscle strength was higher in the grip exercise group at 6 months (p = 0.034). At 12 months postoperatively, the differences in the external rotator and internal rotator muscle strengths, and serratus anterior muscle strength disappeared. There were no significant differences in the tone and stiffness of the upper trapezius muscle, ROM, pain VAS, and functional scores. In addition, changes in the supraspinatus muscle atrophy and the repair integrity were not different between groups. Hand grip exercise affected the rotator cuff and periscapular muscle strengths at 6 months after rotator cuff repair. The grip exercises can effectively and safely promote a faster recovery of shoulder muscle strength and function, without compromising rotator cuff healing.

titre: Exploring adapted water polo: a feasibility study on improving psychosocial recovery in women post-breast cancer treatment.
titre_fr: Exploring adapted water polo: a feasibility study on improving psychosocial recovery in women post-breast cancer treatment.
auteurs: Cuvelier S, Goetgheluck-Villaron C, Zemmour C, Bernasconi S, Tallet A, Arthur A, Dantin P, Viens P, Cohen M, Calvin S
revue: Frontiers in sports and active living
resume: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an adapted water polo programme (Aqua polo) for women following breast cancer treatment. Exploratory secondary objectives were to examine changes in cancer-related fatigue (CRF), quality of life, post-traumatic growth, physical function and participants' psychosocial experiences. The intervention was conducted in a municipal swimming pool within a renowned local club, as part of a community-based research collaboration between a cancer center and a sport psychology laboratory. A 16-week intervention was implemented, with participants engaging in structured weekly sessions to evaluate both physical and psychosocial outcomes. Fifteen participants took part in weekly 2-hour Aqua polo sessions, supervised by a multidisciplinary team. A mixed-methods approach was used to assess feasibility (session adherence), physical improvements (aerobic capacity, muscle mass), and psychosocial dimensions, including CRF (R-PFS), quality of life (QLQ BR23), post-traumatic growth (PTG-I), and relational dynamics within the sporting environment (through semi-structured interviews). Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and mixed linear models; qualitative interviews were coded inductively using grounded theory principles and NVivo software. The programme achieved a high adherence rate, with 87% of participants attending at least 60% of the sessions. Exploratory analyses showed increases in aerobic capacity (p = 0.009), muscle mass (p = 0.01) and quality of life (p = 0.04), whereas no significant changes were observed in cancer-related fatigue. Participants described positive psychosocial experiences, including greater self-confidence, renewed competence and improved body image. Qualitative findings highlighted the importance of social interactions, team cohesion and the coach-athlete relationship in fostering engagement and perceived psychosocial recovery. This feasibility study demonstrates that an adapted water polo programme is feasible and well accepted by women following breast cancer treatment. Exploratory findings suggest potential benefits for physical function and psychosocial well-being, while supporting the development of future adequately powered controlled studies evaluating team-based aquatic interventions in cancer rehabilitation. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04235946, identifier: NCT04235946. French national registry identifier: ID-RCB 2019-A03003-54.

titre: Factors associated with 1-year health-related quality of life after neck-specific exercise in chronic whiplash-associated disorders: an exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
titre_fr: Factors associated with 1-year health-related quality of life after neck-specific exercise in chronic whiplash-associated disorders: an exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
auteurs: Peolsson Anneli, Ljunggren Stefan, Peterson Gunnel
resume: Factors associated with changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes in neck disorders have not been investigated after internet-based support for exercise. The purpose of the study was to investigate baseline and short-term outcome factors associated with changes in HRQoL (EQ-5D-3L and EQ-VAS) at 3 and 15 months, respectively, after a neck-specific exercise programme (NSE) for individuals with chronic whiplash-associated disorders grades 2 and 3. This was a secondary analysis of a prospective randomized controlled multi-centre trial with concealed allocation. Participants (n = 140) were randomized to NSE at a physiotherapy clinic or internet-based NSE with four physiotherapy visits (NSEIT). Assessor-blinded investigators obtained measurements at baseline and at 3- and 15-month follow-up. Orthogonal partial least square (OPLS) and OPLS discriminant statistical analyses (OPLS-DA) were used. There were no significant differences between the exercise programmes. Improvement in psychosocial measures, pain, disability and several objective measures were associated with improvements in HRQoL in OPLS models (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.20 to 0.27, Q2 = 0.06 to 0.12, p < 0.05 to < 0.001). Higher baseline score on adverse psychosocial measures and disability, together with lower dizziness, self-efficacy, and neck-muscle endurance in extension, were associated with clinically relevant improvement in EQ-5D-3L at 15-month follow-up (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.26, Q<sup>2</sup> = 0.13, p < 0.01). The other models were non-significant. Several factors, including adverse psychosocial measures, may be clinically relevant for HRQoL after neck-specific exercise interventions. Given the models' weak predictive ability, the findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The study was registered before data collection started, ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol ID: NCT03022812, initial release 12/20/2016. The study was approved by the regional ethical review board in Linköping, Sweden (Dnr 2016/135-31; 2016/526-32; 2017/45-32).

titre: Effects of single-modality sensory stimulation on brain function in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness: a near-infrared spectroscopy-based study.
titre_fr: Effects of single-modality sensory stimulation on brain function in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness: a near-infrared spectroscopy-based study.
auteurs: Zhang Juan, Zhou Bin, Tian Huifang, Ma Tianyi, Cai Siyan, Ren Xuyan, Fan Yingjie, Zhang Guodong, Su Min
resume: To explore the effects of four single-modality sensory stimulations on the brain functional networks in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (pDOC), and to clarify the correlation between different sensory stimulations and the improvement of patients' consciousness level, so as to provide references for clinical treatment and rehabilitation of pDOC patients. A prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial design was adopted. A total of 57 patients with pDOC were enrolled and divided into visual stimulation group, auditory stimulation group, olfactory-gustatory stimulation group, somatosensory-nocieptive stimulation group, and control group. The intervention duration of each group was 15 min. Behavioral assessments were performed using the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS). Combined with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), hemodynamic parameters and brain functional connectivity were detected. Changes in brain function and consciousness level before and after different sensory stimulation interventions were evaluated. Visual, auditory and olfactory-gustatory stimulations induced significant and robust alterations in cerebral activity across most detected channels (p < 0.001), while the cerebral response to somatosensory-nocieptive stimulation was relatively limited (p < 0.05). At the channel activation level, viewing family photographs in visual stimulation, light music, personalized music and family voice calling in auditory stimulation, and acetic acid stimulation in olfactory-gustatory stimulation significantly activated the corresponding brain regions (p < 0.05). At the brain functional connectivity level, viewing family photographs markedly enhanced functional connectivity within visual-related brain regions (p < 0.05); ethanol stimulation improved functional connectivity of olfactory-gustatory brain regions (p < 0.05). Single-modality sensory stimulation elicits acute cerebral activation in pDOC patients, which is superior to conventional rehabilitation alone. Visual and auditory stimulations exert significantly better intervention effects than olfactory-gustatory and somatosensory-nocieptive stimulations. Among olfactory-gustatory interventions, acetic acid stimulation produces prominent brain region activation, and ethanol enhances functional connectivity of related brain regions. Both can serve as an effective supplementary intervention for pDOC patients with visual and auditory dysfunction, and possess important value for further research and clinical application in the management of pDOC.

titre: Application effect and sleep quality impact of multimodal analgesia (MMA) combined with Mindfulness-Based stress reduction (MBSR) therapy in Post-Spinal fusion surgery patients.
titre_fr: Application effect and sleep quality impact of multimodal analgesia (MMA) combined with Mindfulness-Based stress reduction (MBSR) therapy in Post-Spinal fusion surgery patients.
auteurs: Wu Qianqian, Sun Zhaochu
revue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
resume: We aim to investigate the clinical application effect of multimodal analgesia (MMA) combined with mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) therapy in patients following spinal fusion surgery, analyze its impacts on post spinal-fusion surgery pain control, rehabilitation progress, and sleep quality, thereby providing evidence to inform comprehensive postoperative care protocols. In this single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 124 patients were allocated 1:1 to an intervention group (MMA plus MBSR, n = 62) or a control group (conventional analgesia, n = 62) with concealed allocation and blinded outcome assessment. The results were compared between the two groups, including: pain intensity measured by the visual analogue scale (VAS) at 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h postoperatively; analgesic drug utilization (rate of use, number of rescue doses, duration of use); rehabilitation indicators (time to first ambulation, length of hospital stay, spinal function recovery score); sleep quality by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI); and psychological status evaluated by the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) and Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS). Cumulative opioid consumption expressed as oral morphine equivalents, adverse events, and treatment adherence were also recorded, and repeatedly measured outcomes were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models. Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at all measured time points (6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h and 72 h) compared to the control group (all P < 0.001), with a significant group-by-time interaction (P < 0.001). The intervention group also demonstrated a lower rate of analgesic drug use, fewer rescue doses, and a shorter duration of analgesic use, together with lower cumulative oral morphine equivalents. Rehabilitation outcomes were superior in the intervention group, as evidenced by a shorter time to first ambulation, reduced hospital stay, and a higher spinal function recovery score. At one and two weeks postoperatively, PSQI scores were significantly lower in the intervention group. Furthermore, SAS and SDS scores at two weeks were lower in the intervention group compared to the control group. Adverse events were less frequent in the intervention group. In this single-center trial with short follow-up, the combination of MMA and MBSR therapy effectively alleviates postoperative pain, reduces analgesic use, enhances early rehabilitation and functional recovery, and improves sleep quality while mitigating anxiety and depression. However, because the design was not intended to separate the independent effects of MMA and MBSR, these findings require confirmation in multicenter trials.
resume_fr: We aim to investigate the clinical application effect of multimodal analgesia (MMA) combined with mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) therapy in patients following spinal fusion surgery, analyze its impacts on post spinal-fusion surgery pain control, rehabilitation progress, and sleep quality, thereby providing evidence to inform comprehensive postoperative care protocols. In this single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 124 patients were allocated 1:1 to an intervention group (MMA plus MBSR, n = 62) or a control group (conventional analgesia, n = 62) with concealed allocation and blinded outcome assessment. Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at all measured time points (6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h and 72 h) compared to the control group (all P < 0.001), with a significant group-by-time interaction (P < 0.001). Furthermore, SAS and SDS scores at two weeks were lower in the intervention group compared to the control group. Adverse events were less frequent in the intervention group. In this single-center trial with short follow-up, the combination of MMA and MBSR therapy effectively alleviates postoperative pain, reduces analgesic use, enhances early rehabilitation and functional recovery, and improves sleep quality while mitigating anxiety and depression. However, because the design was not intended to separate the independent effects of MMA and MBSR, these findings require confirmation in multicenter trials.

titre: Bibliometric analysis of VR interventions in cancer research based on multiple databases: mapping research hotspots and developmental trends.
titre_fr: Bibliometric analysis of VR interventions in cancer research based on multiple databases: mapping research hotspots and developmental trends.
auteurs: Wang Ruihan, Zhang Yujie, Fang Lidong, Li Shuoqi
resume: Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. This study looks at how VR interventions in cancer research have evolved over the past two decades, identifies research hotspots, and explores future directions. We collected publications related to VR in cancer research from the Web of Science Core Collection and Pubmed, covering the period from 2005 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace software, we performed bibliometric and visual analyses. These included examining publication trends, contributions by countries and institutions, author collaboration networks, journal impact, keyword co-occurrence, and citation bursts. A total of 1,259 publications from 110 countries were included. The number of publications fluctuated over time but generally increased, reaching its highest point in 2024 with 184 articles. The United States and China were the most active countries. Jordan had the highest average number of citations per paper. Among institutions, McGill University published the most papers, followed by the University of Toronto. The most productive journal was Surgical Endoscopy and Other Interventional Techniques, whilst Cancers and Supportive Care in Cancer showed the fastest growth. Main research themes included pain management, anxiety reduction, breast cancer, and surgical training. Emerging trends involve the combination of augmented reality (AR), digital health, and artificial intelligence (AI) with VR. This study shows that VR research in cancer care is expanding worldwide, with most contributions coming from North America and Europe. Pain management remains the most common application. New technologies such as AR, AI, and telemedicine are becoming more integrated into VR interventions.

titre: Effects of blood flow restriction training in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A systematic review.
titre_fr: Effects of blood flow restriction training in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A systematic review.
auteurs: Khan Lama Saif, Alqawlaq Abdulelah K, Almech Majd Hussain, Alaryani Abdulaziz Khalid, Alhusaini Yousef I, Sultan Adnan Alaa, Alnajjar Fouad Turki, Falqi Abdullah Mohammed, Alshaibani Wahib Shehab, Hassan Mohamed Ibrahim, Samargandi Ramy, Jamjoom Maan
resume: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) has been proposed as a low-load rehabilitation strategy for symptomatic and postoperative upper-limb musculoskeletal conditions. This review evaluated the clinical effects, tolerability, and prescription characteristics of BFRT in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation. This systematic review was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261299726) and reported with reference to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. CENTRAL/Cochrane Library, Embase via Ovid, MEDLINE/PubMed, Science Citation Index/Web of Science, and Scopus were searched without a start-date restriction before February 18, 2026; backward reference-list/citation checking was also used. Randomized trials, case series, and case reports were eligible. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity, and studies were appraised using risk of bias 2 or design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Twenty reports were included: 9 parallel-group randomized trials, 1 randomized crossover trial, 2 case series, and 8 case-report publications. Across the reports, 340 participants were enrolled or randomized and 326 contributed to the analyzed/treated clinical samples; 158 were men (48.5%) and 168 were women (51.5%). In a sham-controlled lateral elbow tendinopathy trial, BFRT resulted in a significantly greater reduction in 12-week pain (between-group difference -1.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.89 to -0.18; P = .026) and patient-rated tennis elbow evaluation (PRTEE) (-15.23, 95% CI -23.57 to -6.90; P < .001). In patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis, PRTEE reduction (-24.20 ± 4.02 vs -15.60 ± 3.71; P = .001) and quick disabilities of the arm, shoulder and hand reduction (-12.83 ± 4.97 vs -7.51 ± 4.72; P = .025) were significantly greater with BFRT plus conventional therapy, whereas between-group pain and strength changes were not significant. In nonoperative distal-radius-fracture rehabilitation, mean activity-pain reduction was 4.0 versus 2.3 points (P = .03). In rotator-cuff tendinopathy, BFRT resulted in significantly greater biceps thickness (P = .002) and internal-rotation strength (P = .040). Conversely, a pragmatic elbow trial found no significant between-group difference in 12-month PRTEE (adjusted contrast + 4.32, 95% CI -9.17 to 17.81; P = .53). BFRT may be considered a low-load adjunct in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation settings, but it is not consistently superior to active rehabilitation for pain, strength, or function. Confidence remains limited by small samples, heterogeneous prescriptions and co-interventions, uncontrolled designs, and incomplete adverse-event ascertainment.

titre: Comparative effectiveness of telerehabilitation vs. face-to-face rehabilitation in adults with chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
titre_fr: Comparative effectiveness of telerehabilitation vs. face-to-face rehabilitation in adults with chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
auteurs: Liu Shaowen, Yang Jiayin, Lei Beibei, Wang Yage, Zhuang Weisheng, Liu Hongjian
resume: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a major cause of disability worldwide and creates substantial rehabilitation demand. When core rehabilitation content is similar, the comparative effectiveness of telerehabilitation (TR) and face-to-face rehabilitation as delivery modes remains unclear. Methods: This meta-analysis used strict eligibility criteria to distinguish the two delivery pathways and better isolate delivery-mode effects. PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched for randomized controlled trials in adults with CLBP. Paper-based home exercise programs, continuous hybrid delivery, and remote-assessment-only designs were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses used standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RoB 2 and GRADE assessed risk of bias and evidence certainty. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted. Ten trials involving 562 participants were included. Content-matched primary analyses found no significant difference between TR and face-to-face rehabilitation in pain intensity (7 trials; SMD = -0.05, 95% CI - 0.34 to 0.24; very low certainty) or functional disability (8 trials; SMD = 0.22, 95% CI - 0.07 to 0.52; low certainty). In secondary analyses including two trials that provided manual therapy only to the face-to-face group, pain intensity did not differ significantly (9 trials; SMD = -0.01, 95% CI - 0.26 to 0.24), whereas functional disability favored face-to-face rehabilitation (10 trials; SMD = 0.26, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.52). Subgroup interaction tests were nonsignificant for intervention duration, weekly treatment frequency, and supervision status. When rehabilitation content was similar, TR and face-to-face rehabilitation showed no statistically significant differences in pain intensity or functional disability. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent effectiveness between TR and face-to-face rehabilitation, because the certainty of evidence was low for functional disability and very low for pain intensity, and the functional disability estimate was sensitive to the exclusion of one study. Future high-quality trials with comparable interventions and longer follow-up are needed, particularly direct comparisons of supervised and unsupervised TR. PROSPERO, CRD420261467122.

titre: Impact of early goal-directed mobilization on ICU-acquired weakness: a meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Impact of early goal-directed mobilization on ICU-acquired weakness: a meta-analysis.
auteurs: Zhou Jiayi, Dai Lifei, Liu Xiaoli, Xiang Junlian
resume: ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) significantly impairs muscle strength and physical function in critically ill patients. Early mobilization interventions have been increasingly adopted, yet the specific effects of a structured EGDM program on ICU-AW and functional outcomes have not been systematically quantified. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of EGDM on ICU-AW, muscle strength, and functional outcomes. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, and Viper Information Products (VIP) databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) up to November 30, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2.0. RevMan 5.4 was used for meta-analysis. Subgroup analysis was prespecified by allocation concealment. Nine RCTs (907 patients) were included. EGDM reduced ICU-AW [RR = 0.57, 95%CI (0.33 ~ 0.97), p = 0.04 for the overall effect; I2 = 77%, p = 0.002 for heterogeneity], but sensitivity analysis of high-quality trials showed no significant effect [RR = 0.84, 95%CI (0.48 ~ 1.46), p = 0.54 for the overall effect]. EGDM improved muscle strength [MD = 4.94, 95%CI (3.39 ~ 6.50), I2 = 59%, p = 0.02 for heterogeneity], shortened the duration of mechanical ventilation [MD = -81.95 h, 95%CI (-115.45 ~ -48.46), p < 0.00001 for the overall effect; I2 = 85%, p < 0.00001 for heterogeneity], and reduced ICU stay[MD = -4.55 days, 95%CI (-6.22 ~ -2.89), p < 0.00001 for the overall effect; I2 = 74%, p = 0.0004 for heterogeneity], both with substantial heterogeneity. Although the primary Barthel Index analysis was not statistically significant, sensitivity analysis suggested improvement in patients with moderate baseline function [MD = 8.27, 95%CI (5.66 ~ 10.87), p < 0.00001 for the overall effect]. EGDM may improve muscle strength and physical function in ICU patients. The available evidence does not confirm a reduction in ICU-AW. The effects on ventilation duration and ICU stay varied substantially across studies, likely influenced by sedation protocols, weaning practices, and other context-specific factors. Further rigorous trials with detailed reporting of interventions and contextual factors are needed to guide precise clinical implementation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261280603, CRD420261280603.

titre: The effects of olfactory stimulation on postural control in adults: A systematic review.
titre_fr: The effects of olfactory stimulation on postural control in adults: A systematic review.
auteurs: Sadir Yunus, Khosravi Mojtaba, Khazanin Hossein, Fakoor Rashid Hossein, Alavi Emad, Ceylan Tülay, Karakulak Izzet, Tan Suriye, Alimoradi Mohammad, Alghosi Mohammad
resume: Olfactory stimulation has emerged as a potential modulator of postural control, yet the evidence has not been systematically synthesized. This systematic review aimed to aggregate, critically appraise, and narratively synthesize the available literature on the effects of olfactory stimulation on postural control in adults. This systematic review was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guideline and the Cochrane Handbook. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261326528). A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus was performed from inception to December 1, 2025, supplemented by grey literature searches and reference list screening. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental designs, and clinical trials examining olfactory stimulation effects on any quantitative measure of postural control were eligible. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Downs and Black checklist. The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) framework. Due to substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was conducted following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines. Ten studies (six RCTs and four Non-RCTs) involving 365 participants (mean age 47.9 ± 19.8 years) were included. Olfactory stimulation with pleasant odors (e.g., lavender, black pepper) generally enhanced postural stability, particularly in older adults and under eyes-closed conditions, while unpleasant odors consistently increased postural sway. However, inhibitory effects were observed during high-precision athletic tasks. Odor-specific effects were identified, with appetitive cues producing unique facilitatory effects. According to GRADE, the certainty of evidence was moderate for dynamic balance and functional mobility, low for fear of falling, and very low for static balance. Olfactory stimulation can modulate postural control in adults, with effects dependent on odor valence, participant traits, and task demands. Pleasant odors generally enhance stability during sensory deprivation, while unpleasant odors increase sway; however, trigeminal stimulants like ammonia may impair high-precision tasks. Evidence certainty was low to moderate, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings lay the groundwork for future research on olfactory-motor integration and clinical applications in balance rehabilitation and fall prevention. Registration: The study was registered on the International Prospective Registry of Systematic Reviews database (CRD420261326528).

titre: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
auteurs: Hortobágyi Tibor, Granacher Urs, Brach Jennifer, Malatesta Davide, Csizmadia Beáta, Kovács Bálint, Ye Jingyi, Emam Mohamed Abdelaziz, Horváth András Attila, Vetrovsky Tomas
resume: The metabolic cost of walking (Cw) increases with heathy aging and in neurological conditions. No comprehensive assessment has been performed yet to determine whether chronic exercise training and rehabilitation could improve Cw. The purpose of this study was to determine whether the effects of chronic exercise interventions on Cw differ by type, dose, and intensity in healthy adults and individuals with neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, and stroke). Systematic review and robust variance estimation meta-analysis with meta-regression following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Systematic search of Medline, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases. A total of 27 studies with 36 intervention arms and 54 outcomes in 1177 participants, of those 703 healthy adults and 474 patients with multiple sclerosis (1 study), Parkinson's disease (1 study), and stroke (9 studies) were included. Across all types of training (aerobic, resistance, other), chronic physical exercise training improved Cw (g = 0.40, p = 0.001). Improvements were significant in healthy individuals (g = 0.49, p = 0.001) but not in patients with stroke (g = 0.24, p = 0.065). Meta-regression confirmed that population moderated the effects of training on Cw (p = 0.043) after adjusting for exercise training characteristics. In the adjusted meta-regression, higher study-level mean body mass index (BMI) was associated with smaller intervention effects on Cw (β = - 0.20, p = 0.040). Training type, duration, intensity, frequency, and session duration did not significantly moderate the training effects on Cw, although the meta-regression may have been underpowered to detect such associations. Heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup> < 62.5%) and risk of bias were moderate. This is the first meta-synthesis examining the effects of diverse forms of exercise training on Cw in different populations. Chronic physical exercise training improves Cw in healthy adults, with smaller effects observed in individuals with stroke. The findings support chronic physical exercise training as an effective strategy for improving walking economy.

titre: Comparative effectiveness of acupuncture combined with rehabilitation for post-stroke hemiplegia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
titre_fr: Comparative effectiveness of acupuncture combined with rehabilitation for post-stroke hemiplegia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
auteurs: Wang Hongliang, Tang Xiaoyan, Li Peizhe, Dong Zhihao, Shang Kun, Zhang Xin
resume: Hemiplegia, as a common sequela of stroke, can severely affect patients' quality of life. Although rehabilitation therapy can improve neurological function and motor abilities, a single therapy often has limited effectiveness in meeting the comprehensive rehabilitation needs. Clinical observations have demonstrated that the integration of acupuncture with rehabilitation therapy yields significant synergistic benefits. However, given the paucity of direct comparative studies between distinct combination therapies, the optimal treatment regimen remains to be definitively established. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of rehabilitation combined with different acupuncture techniques in treating patients with post-stroke hemiplegia using a network meta-analysis (NMA). We systematically searched eight databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) related to acupuncture combined with rehabilitation (ACU + RT) for post-stroke hemiplegia, with the searched period from database inception to March 5, 2026. The included literature was analyzed using Bayesian NMA with R software version 4.5.0. This study included 71 RCTs, involving 6,121 patients and nine interventions. The NMA results indicated that for Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) efficacy, the top three interventions were floating acupuncture combined with rehabilitation (FACU + RT), warm needle moxibustion combined with rehabilitation (WNM + RT), and moxibustion combined with rehabilitation (MOX + RT). However, as the number of studies reporting MAS data is relatively small (5 cases), the robustness of this result still needs to be further confirmed in future research. titre: Co-designing embodied extended reality telehealth for veteran mental health: from movement care to whole health.
titre_fr: Co-designing embodied extended reality telehealth for veteran mental health: from movement care to whole health.
auteurs: Elor Aviv, Kuznetsov Maxim, Kusumoto Laura, Duval Jared, Burnett Kedron, Skelton Felicia, Touchett Hilary
resume: Veterans in rural and underserved communities face persistent care barriers from provider shortages, travel burdens, and the digital divide. Within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the Clinical Resource Hub (CRH) National Telehealth Program delivers primary, mental health, specialty, surgical, and rehabilitative care into veterans' homes and rural clinics, while VA Immersive scales extended reality (XR) across the system. Embodied XR telehealth, where provider and patient meet as full-body avatars in a shared immersive environment, intersects these programs and introduces new design requirements. This study extends our embodied XR codesign series from physical rehabilitation to mental health and whole health. Stakeholders from VA, academia, and industry ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>30</mn></math> ), drawn from Boise and other participating CRHs, joined a 3-day codesign at the Boise VA Medical Center in June 2026, including shadowing telehealth workflows, a full-day workshop with five teams, and a half-day debrief with program leads. Seven usability task ratings, 164 four-axis ideas (Raise, Reduce, Eliminate, Create), 95 debrief proposals, 188 prioritization votes, and 19 discussion transcripts were analyzed through descriptive statistics and reflexive thematic analysis. Perceived task ease was high among a cohort with mixed VR experience across seven tasks (tutorial, joining a telehealth room, exercise completion, movement recording, environment and interactable customization, and spatial drawing), each above 4.1 of 5 on the Single Ease Question, led by customizing virtual environments ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>4.84</mn> <mo>±</mo> <mn>0.37</mn></math> ). Stakeholders most endorsed minimalist defaults, onboarding resources, and out-of-the-box readiness, followed by embodiment with personalized environments, disability representation, and veteran identity markers. The debrief prioritized breathing and grounding, graded exposure, psychoeducation, and whole-health movement, delivered through headsets paired to an in-clinic tablet or monitored home deployment. Infrastructure compatibility, workforce fit, and governance emerged as pervasive constraints. Workshop satisfaction was high ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>4.82</mn> <mo>±</mo> <mn>0.53</mn></math> of 5) with 88% requesting follow-up; platform-specific ratings were favorable but lower and more variable (e.g., user-friendliness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>3.76</mn> <mo>±</mo> <mn>0.97</mn></math> of 5). We propose candidate design principles for extending an embodied XR telehealth platform, built for physical rehabilitation, to mental health and whole health care for veterans, and discuss implications for platform design, piloting, and deployment.

titre: Mental health status and associated factors among Chinese postoperative breast cancer survivors of working age: a cross-sectional study.
titre_fr: Mental health status and associated factors among Chinese postoperative breast cancer survivors of working age: a cross-sectional study.
auteurs: Su Zhongge, Wang Yongshi, Yan Yan, Naito Toshio, He Yi, Yokokawa Hirohide, Tang Lili
revue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
resume: Mental health is a critical component of overall wellness among breast cancer survivors of working age; however, research in this area remains limited in China. This study aims to evaluate the mental health status and identify associated factors among this particular population. A cross-sectional study was conducted from July 5 to November 5, 2023, at a cancer hospital in Beijing, with patients from across China. A total of 443 postoperative breast cancer survivors of working age were recruited. Data on socio-demographics including occupation before diagnosis and current work status, diagnosis and treatments were self-reported by participants. Mental health status was assessed using GAD-7, PHQ-9, and FCRI-SF for anxiety, depression and fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) symptoms, respectively. Descriptive and logistic regression analyses were used to explore associations between socio-demographic, clinical factors and mental health outcomes. Among 443 participants (mean age: 49.4 years; age 18-60; all women), 27.1%, 29.3% and 31.8% were assessed to have anxiety, depression and fear of cancer recurrence symptoms, respectively. Residents of Beijing (44.0%) were significantly less likely to report FCR symptoms than non-residents (adjusted OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.37-0.90, p = 0.02). Those with non-professional occupations before cancer diagnosis (47.6%) showed a trend toward a lower likelihood of depression (adjusted OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.34-0.99, p = 0.05). Residence and occupational disparities were associated with FCR and depressive symptoms. Digital health interventions may help address unmet psychological supportive care needs in non-central cities, while vocational rehabilitation support may benefit individuals with professional backgrounds.

titre: Caregiver Outcomes from the BRITE Study: Secondary Outcomes of a Multisite Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Post-Rehabilitation Discharge Transitional Support after Traumatic Brain Injury.
titre_fr: Caregiver Outcomes from the BRITE Study: Secondary Outcomes of a Multisite Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Post-Rehabilitation Discharge Transitional Support after Traumatic Brain Injury.
auteurs: Whyte John, Jou Stacey, Hart Tessa, Ciol Marcia A, Fann Jesse R, Hammond Flora, Moore Megan, Hoffman Jeanne M
resume: Caregivers of individuals admitted to inpatient rehabilitation following traumatic brain injury (TBI) often experience high burden and unmet needs after hospital discharge. Transitional periods are challenging, and standard discharge planning with referrals to outpatient care is typically not enough support for this critical phase. We sought to evaluate the impact of a post-inpatient rehabilitation patient/caregiver intervention (rehabilitation transition planning; RTP) on caregiver burden and quality of life, compared to standard rehabilitation discharge planning (RDP). Of 925 randomized patient participants at six inpatient rehabilitation centers, 591 had caregivers who enrolled in the study. Patients and caregivers in the RTP group (N = 295) received up to 12 remote follow-up support contacts for 6 months post-discharge. The RDP control group (n = 296) received standard discharge planning. Caregiver outcomes (Bakas, Zarit, PROMIS, SF-12 Physical/Mental) were assessed at 6 and 12 months. Data analysis used intention-to-treat principles. No significant differences were observed in any caregiver outcome measures at 6 or 12 months between RTP and RDP groups. In exploratory analyses, greater functional impairment, need for assistance, and a history of prior mental health problems on the part of the patient were associated with greater burden and reduced quality of life for caregivers irrespective of treatment assignment. Female caregivers, White caregivers, and those with greater education tended to show greater burden on some measures. No patient or caregiver attributes were consistently associated with a differential response to the intervention. Future research should explore alternative or more targeted interventions for this vulnerable population using both intervention-sensitive and global measures of outcome.

titre: Reconstructing Hope Through Horticultural Therapy: A Phenomenological Study of Individuals with Post-Stroke Depression.
titre_fr: Reconstructing Hope Through Horticultural Therapy: A Phenomenological Study of Individuals with Post-Stroke Depression.
auteurs: Gong Yuehua, Shen Haijian, Ren Lingli, Zhu Xiaoping
resume: Background: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a common psychological complication that negatively affects rehabilitation and quality of life. This study explored the lived experiences of patients with PSD participating in horticultural therapy (HT). Methods: A descriptive phenomenological study was conducted among 15 individuals with mild-to-moderate PSD who completed a six-month HT program in Shanghai, China. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Results: Five themes emerged: rebuilding self-efficacy, reconstructing hope, enhancing social connectedness and sense of value, facilitating physical and psychological rehabilitation, and challenges during horticultural activities. Participants described HT as a meaningful experience that fostered confidence, hope, social participation, and motivation for recovery. Plant growth was often interpreted by participants as a symbol of personal resilience and hope, while horticultural activities were described as meaningful experiences that fostered social interaction and a sense of purpose. Nevertheless, plant loss and physical limitations sometimes generated frustration and helplessness. Conclusions: Participants described HT as a meaningful experience associated with self-efficacy, hope, social connectedness, and engagement in rehabilitation. The findings highlight the potential value of individualized horticultural activities as a supportive component of care for individuals with PSD and may inform the development of person-centered rehabilitation programs.
