titre: Multimodal rehabilitation for hard flaccid syndrome in a retrospective case series.
titre_fr: Multimodal rehabilitation for hard flaccid syndrome in a retrospective case series.
auteurs: Mendias Christopher L, Awan Tariq M
resume: Hard flaccid syndrome (HFS) is an emerging condition of male sexual dysfunction characterized by a persistent semi-rigid penis in the flaccid state, altered penile sensation, erectile dysfunction, and pelvic or perineal pain. Single-modality treatments have shown limited success, and multimodal protocols have been reported only in single-patient case studies. To describe clinical outcomes associated with completion of an integrative multimodal rehabilitation protocol in a retrospective case series of men with HFS. Thirty-two men with HFS completed a comprehensive protocol combining class IV laser therapy, dry needling, radial pressure wave shockwave therapy, therapeutic ultrasound, biofeedback training, manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, behavioral coaching, and daily oral tadalafil. Patient-reported outcomes were collected at treatment initiation and completion. Erection Hardness Scale (EHS), penile function satisfaction, PROMIS Interest in Sexual Activity, and PROMIS Global Health Physical and Mental Component scores. Median EHS increased from 2 to 4 and median penile satisfaction increased from 2 to 5 (both P < 0.01). All 32 patients achieved EHS ≥3 by treatment end, compared to 8 of 32 (25%) at baseline. PROMIS Interest in Sexual Activity, Global Physical Health, and Global Mental Health scores all improved significantly (P < 0.01). Common comorbid features included low back pain (53%), hip or groin pain (38%), pelvic floor pain (31%), and urinary symptoms (28%). In this retrospective case series, completion of a multimodal rehabilitation program was associated with improvements in erection hardness, penile satisfaction, sexual interest, and global health in men with HFS. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective controlled studies evaluating efficacy, durability, and component-specific effects.

titre: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human-Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication.
titre_fr: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human-Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication.
auteurs: Huo Ziwei, Xu Nuo, Fu Yixuan, Gu Rui, Liu Chao, Wang Zhong Lin, Sun Qijun
resume: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time-frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human-machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled "Feeding Frenzy" interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

titre: Adjunctive Immersive Virtual Reality for Urinary Incontinence-Related Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women with Urinary Incontinence: A Non-Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
titre_fr: Adjunctive Immersive Virtual Reality for Urinary Incontinence-Related Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women with Urinary Incontinence: A Non-Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.
auteurs: Kołodyńska Gabriela, Cieślik Błażej, Piątek Aleksandra, Zalewski Maciej, Szczepańska-Gieracha Joanna, Andrzejewski Waldemar
resume: Background/Objectives: This study examined whether adding relaxation-oriented immersive virtual reality (VR) to pelvic floor muscle electrostimulation with electromyographic (EMG) biofeedback was associated with additional improvement in incontinence-related quality of life among postmenopausal women. Methods: In this exploratory non-randomized controlled pilot trial, 40 postmenopausal women received electrostimulation with EMG biofeedback alone (ES; n = 20) or the same intervention preceded by VR (VR + ES; n = 20). Participants completed eight sessions over 2 weeks and were assessed at baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and 2-week follow-up (T2); T1 was the prespecified primary assessment. The primary outcome was the Incontinence Quality of Life Questionnaire (I-QOL) total score. Secondary outcomes included pelvic floor EMG, bladder-diary variables, other quality-of-life measures, perceived stress, and self-esteem. Baseline-adjusted linear mixed models were used. The registry record was submitted before enrollment (NCT07070063). Results: Thirty-six participants contributed to the primary analysis. The adjusted between-group difference in I-QOL was -1.65 points at T1 (95% CI, -10.03 to 6.74; p = 0.70) and -4.00 points at T2 (95% CI, -12.38 to 4.39; p = 0.35). Adjusted contrasts were non-significant for the remaining questionnaire and EMG outcomes. Selected bladder-diary outcomes differed between groups, but these analyses were exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and did not directly quantify urinary leakage. Conclusions: The study did not detect a statistically significant additional improvement in incontinence-related quality of life with adjunctive VR. Confidence intervals remained compatible with potentially meaningful effects in either direction. Given the small sample and non-randomized design, the findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

titre_fr: Rehabilitation in Pediatric Patients with Acute and Subacute Acquired Brain Injury: A Scoping Review on Non-Pharmacological Interventions.
auteurs: Cardile Davide, Marafioti Giulia, Tanner Giuliana, Cappadona Irene, Pagano Maria, Corallo Francesco, Rifici Carmela, Quartarone Angelo, Calabrò Rocco Salvatore
resume: Background: Acquired brain injury in children and adolescents may lead to long-term neurological, cognitive, motor, and behavioral impairments. However, pediatric-specific evidence on rehabilitation strategies remains limited. Objective: This review aimed to summarize current evidence on non-pharmacological neurorehabilitation interventions for children and adolescents with acute/subacute acquired or traumatic brain injury, including a subset of patients with disorders of consciousness. Methods: A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus. Eligible studies investigated non-pharmacological rehabilitation approaches in pediatric or adolescent patients with severe acquired brain injury, traumatic brain injury, stroke, or disorders of consciousness. Data on interventions, outcomes, and main findings were extracted. Results: The reviewed studies included heterogeneous interventions, such as multidisciplinary rehabilitation, constraint-induced movement therapy, virtual-reality-based training, speech therapy, parent-child interaction therapy, sensory stimulation, autonomic monitoring, and neuromodulation. Overall, these approaches were feasible and generally well tolerated, with reported improvements in motor, functional, behavioral, autonomic, and consciousness-related outcomes. Conclusions: Non-pharmacological rehabilitation may support recovery in children and adolescents with severe brain injury, although current evidence remains preliminary and heterogeneous. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols and outcome measures are needed to guide pediatric-specific rehabilitation practice.

titre: Short-term vestibulo-ocular and postural effects of virtual reality in healthy young adults.
titre_fr: Short-term vestibulo-ocular and postural effects of virtual reality in healthy young adults.
auteurs: Turkoglu Enes, Altin Busra, Aksoy Songul
revue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
resume: BackgroundVirtual reality can simulate the testing of cognitive, sensory, and motor skills using simulated environments. Eye stabilization is necessary to maintain visual acuity during rapid head movements; this is achieved through mechanisms such as the vestibulo-ocular reflex.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the short-term effect of a passive, non-interactive virtual reality stimulus on dynamic visual acuity and postural sway in healthy young adults.Methods24 healthy young adults (9 males, 15 females) aged 20-39, with an average age of 26.08 ± 4.14 were included in the study. All participants underwent the Sensory Organization Test (SOT), Static Visual Acuity Test (SVAT), Perception Time Test (PTT), Dynamic Visual Acuity Test (DVAT), Gaze Stabilization Test (GST), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) to assess symptoms that may arise from virtual reality. These tests were repeated for all participants after the virtual reality experience, and completed on the same day.ResultsStatistically significant differences were obtained in the balance score of the SOT (COMP, mean decrease 2.29 points, 95% CI 0.49-4.10, p = 0.015, Cohen's d = 0.54) and the left-side GST (mean increase 24.7 ms, 95% CI -45.82 to -3.64, p = 0.024, Cohen's d = -0.52) in the pre/post virtual reality experience comparison. Virtual reality had no statistically significant effect on SOT conditions 1-6 individually (all p > 0.05), although CON6 and PTT were borderline (CON6: p = 0.095, r = 0.34; PTT: p = 0.053, r = 0.40). No statistically significant differences were found between pre- and post-treatment in PTT and DVAT (both p > 0.05).ConclusionIt has been demonstrated that a passive, non-interactive virtual reality stimulus may affect balance and gaze stabilization by increasing postural sway over a short, same-day time frame. Clinicians and researchers should be aware of these possible short-term effects when using similar VR-based paradigms for vestibular assessment and rehabilitation.

titre: The value of promoting "Internet Plus" home-based pulmonary rehabilitation for university staff with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
titre_fr: The value of promoting "Internet Plus" home-based pulmonary rehabilitation for university staff with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
auteurs: Wei Jia, Zhang Haijun, Wang Yiwei, Su Qiaoli
resume: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a non-pharmacological intervention for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). "Internet-Plus" technologies create opportunities for home-delivered PR to overcome barriers of center-based rehabilitation, yet real-world implementation evidence among university staff with COPD remains scarce. This mini review synthesizes six major "Internet-Plus" home-based PR modalities: short message service (SMS)/telephone follow-up, social media platforms, video conferencing telerehabilitation, wearable devices and Internet of things (IoT) systems, smartphone applications and virtual-reality-integrated rehabilitation. Available evidence indicates that telehealth PR yields comparable clinical outcomes to center PR in many studies, though considerable heterogeneity across trials leads to inconsistent conclusions regarding exercise capacity, quality of life and hospitalization endpoints. Notably, no interventional studies have delivered telehealth PR specifically for university staff with COPD. We conceptually propose that university staff with high digital literacy and structured occupational settings, constitute a promising target population for translational research in this domain. The review concludes with a conceptual framework for designing precise, intelligent home PR management within university communities.

titre: Implementing Somalia's National Transformation Plan 2025-2029 for health-system reform: a policy and practice review of governance, financing, and institutional readiness.
titre_fr: Implementing Somalia's National Transformation Plan 2025-2029 for health-system reform: a policy and practice review of governance, financing, and institutional readiness.
auteurs: Osman Nor Haji, Mohamed Dahir Osman, Osman Hamdi Mohamud, Rage Abdifatah Nour, Abdi Abdiweli Mohamed, Iman Mohamed Ismael, Moallim Aweis Ahmed, Jimale Abdirahman Mohamed, Ali Mohamed Ahmed, Dahir Ahmed Ismail, Adam Abdikarim Abdi, Mohamud Abdirahman Ahmed, Dhakane Siham Mohamed, Mohamud Osman Mohamed
resume: Somalia's National Transformation Plan (NTP) 2025-2029 presents an ambitious health-reform agenda centred on maternal and child health, workforce development, health-system strengthening, regulation, financing, digitalisation, and emergency preparedness. The policy challenge is whether the institutional conditions required for implementation can be assembled in a fragile, federal, highly aid-dependent and predominantly mixed-provider health system. This Policy and Practice Review critically examines the implementation readiness of the NTP health chapter and proposes a sequenced framework for converting national commitments into measurable results. A structured narrative review was undertaken from June to July 2026 using peer-reviewed literature, national policy documents, and reports from governmental and international institutions. Evidence was interpreted through the health-policy triangle, the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), applied prospectively to anticipated determinants, and a health-system resilience lens. The synthesis generated six interdependent proposed readiness foundations: a negotiated federal-state governance compact; a technically validated, costed and sequenced operational plan; sustainable financing and strategic purchasing; workforce and regulatory capacity; integrated information, monitoring and public accountability systems; and shock-responsive adaptive management. Important policy strengths include explicit targets for service coverage, workforce expansion, hospital rehabilitation, regulation and digital health. Key risks include inconsistent or under-specified targets and baselines, uncertain fiscal pathways, weak federal-state role specification, and dependence on external resources and non-state providers. Comparative evidence suggests that contracting and pooled financing can expand services when stewardship, fiduciary safeguards, workforce integration, community accountability and learning systems develop concurrently. We propose a phased 2026-2029 pathway prioritising technical validation, essential-service continuity, subnational compacts, workforce payroll transition, interoperable data systems and annual public performance reviews. The proposed framework is prospective and has not yet been empirically validated; consultation with federal and subnational authorities, providers, partners, civil society and communities is required before formal adoption.

titre: Effectiveness of Gamified Rehabilitation Interventions in Patients with Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Meta-Analysis.
titre_fr: Effectiveness of Gamified Rehabilitation Interventions in Patients with Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Meta-Analysis.
auteurs: Cao Yongxin, Liu Xiaohan, Zhao Jing, Zhao Jie, Chang Hong
resume: To evaluate the effects of gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation on functional oral intake and bedside swallowing function in patients with post-stroke dysphagia, and to explore feedback modality, post-stroke duration, and the robustness of the main findings. This meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Data, and SinoMed were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials published through December 22, 2025. The Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) was designated as the primary outcome and the Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) as the secondary outcome. All pooled analyses used random-effects models, with exploratory subgroup analyses and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Seven RCTs involving 340 participants were included. Gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation was associated with higher FOIS scores (MD=1.53, 95% CI: 0.58-2.49, P=0.002), with very high between-study heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup>=96%). Pooled results from four RCTs showed lower SSA scores after gamified swallowing rehabilitation (MD=- 2.44, 95% CI: - 3.84 to - 1.04, P<0.001; I<sup>2</sup>=54%). The between-subgroup difference for FOIS according to sEMG use was not statistically significant (P=0.39), whereas the SSA subgroup difference was statistically significant (P=0.01). After excluding Hou et al. (2024) in the sensitivity analysis, the direction of the FOIS effect remained unchanged (MD=1.04, 95% CI: 0.46-1.61, P=0.0004; I<sup>2</sup>=85%). Current evidence suggests that gamified swallowing rehabilitation may improve FOIS and SSA outcomes in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. However, the number of included studies and participants was limited, heterogeneity for FOIS was very high, several studies had a high risk of bias, and multiple co-intervention components made the independent effect of gamification difficult to isolate. Findings from the sEMG and post-stroke-duration subgroups should therefore be considered exploratory. Further high-quality studies are needed to optimize intervention strategies and reduce heterogeneity.

titre: Brain-computer interfaces in pediatric populations: research advances, application challenges, and future directions.
titre_fr: Brain-computer interfaces in pediatric populations: research advances, application challenges, and future directions.
auteurs: Wang Shan, Wu Qian, Lei Qiaorong, Li Chunyang, Lei Fenfang
resume: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) establish direct communication pathways between the brain and external devices. Leveraging the unique neuroplasticity of the developing brain, BCIs have emerged as a novel rehabilitative technology for children with neurodevelopmental disorders, including cerebral palsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and perinatal brain injury. This review comprehensively examines five major BCI paradigms-P300, motor imagery (MI), steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and multimodal hybrid systems-with respect to their pediatric adaptability, technical limitations, and optimization strategies. We summarize the existing evidence across four key clinical applications: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), motor function rehabilitation, ADHD attention training, and ASD social-emotional intervention. Key intrinsic (cognitive and physiological) and extrinsic (device and environmental) variables affecting BCI performance in children are analyzed, along with general optimization approaches including personalized parameter tuning, pre-training neurofeedback, and lightweight hardware modifications. Furthermore, we examine multilayer barriers to pediatric BCI adoption, including user experience, clinical workforce readiness, translational pathways, and child-specific ethical considerations. Preliminary evidence suggests that non-invasive BCIs can be feasibly used in children above 5 years of age, although this finding is based on short-term studies with small sample sizes and requires further validation through larger longitudinal trials. However, the immature pediatric brain, short attention spans, and low device tolerance preclude direct translation of adult BCI systems. While evidence is more established for AAC and motor rehabilitation in cerebral palsy, large-scale long-term data are still lacking for ADHD and ASD interventions. Future efforts should prioritize child-specific lightweight wearable devices, multicenter longitudinal trials, immersive integration with virtual reality (VR) and social robots, standardized clinical service frameworks, and ethical guidelines for invasive pediatric BCIs, thereby facilitating the transition of BCI technology from laboratory to clinical and home settings and maximizing its value in promoting neurodevelopmental plasticity in children with special needs.

titre: Campagne de vaccination contre la grippe 2026 : le meilleur moyen de se protéger des formes graves
resume: La campagne de vaccination contre la grippe démarre aujourd’hui. Cette année encore, les personnes les plus à risque ont reçu l’invitation de l’Assurance Maladie pour se faire vacciner contre la grippe, avec la recommandation de se faire vacciner également contre le Covid-19. En Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur, 1,5 million de personnes sont considérées comme à risque et sont invitées à se faire vacciner. Pourtant, lors de la précédente campagne, seules 46 % de ces personnes à risque s’étaient fait vacciner dans la région. Une couverture encore insuffisante, alors que l’Organisation mondiale de la santé recommande un objectif de 75 % chez les personnes à risque.

resume: Depuis plus de 30 ans, le Baromètre de Santé publique France est une enquête, unique en son genre, qui permet de mesurer et suivre les comportements, attitudes, opinions et connaissances en lien avec la santé des personnes vivant en France.

titre: Résultats de l’édition 2024 du Baromètre de Santé publique France : mieux connaître et comprendre les comportements, connaissances et opinions de la population en lien avec la santé
resume: Depuis plus de trente ans, le Baromètre de Santé publique France est une enquête, unique en son genre, qui permet de disposer d’informations impossibles à recueillir par ailleurs : comportements individuels, opinions, connaissances, ou encore événements de santé qui ne sont pas collectés par les systèmes de surveillance existants. Désormais actualisés tous les deux ans, les résultats produits éclairent les enjeux de santé publique, enrichissent les connaissances sur l’état de santé et fournissent des informations nécessaires pour guider les politiques de prévention et aider à réduire les inégalités sociales et territoriales de santé.

titre: PLFSS 2027 : le Conseil de la CNSA alerte sur un financement de l’autonomie en retard sur les besoins et un risque de fragilisation de la branche Autonomie
resume: Réuni le 15 octobre en présence de Camille Galliard-Minier, ministre déléguée chargée de l’Autonomie et des personnes handicapées, le Conseil de la CNSA, présidé par Paul Christophe, a appelé à un changement de cap. Son constat est sans appel : les moyens prévus ne sont pas à la hauteur des besoins des personnes âgées, des personnes en situation de handicap, de leurs proches et des professionnels qui les accompagnent. Le Conseil demande des ressources nouvelles pour la branche Autonomie, la mobilisation effective des crédits votés et la suppression du transfert de 300 millions d’euros de CSG aux départements prévu par l’article 13 du projet de loi de financement de la Sécurité sociale.
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)

titre: Résidences autonomie : 30 millions d’euros mobilisés en 2026 pour renforcer l’offre dans les territoires
resume: Face au vieillissement de la population et à l’évolution des aspirations des personnes âgées, les résidences autonomie apportent une réponse adaptée en proposant des logements individuels, sécurisés et ouverts sur leur environnement, qui contribuent à prévenir la perte d’autonomie et à lutter contre l’isolement. Pour soutenir la création de nouvelles places, la CNSA et l’Assurance retraite lancent une nouvelle édition de l’Initiative pour le développement des résidences autonomie (IDRA).
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)

titre: Intelligence artificielle dans la branche Autonomie : un an après son lancement, 80 % de la feuille de route déjà déployée
resume: Recensement de plus de 100 cas d’usage, expérimentations en MDPH, outillage des médecins évaluateurs en EHPAD, acculturation des équipes… Un an après le lancement de sa feuille de route IA 2025-2026, la CNSA dresse un premier bilan des actions engagées au sein de la branche Autonomie.
source: CNSA (Caisse Nationale de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie)
